fotw-es1701-e8.title: Historical Flags 1701-1785 (Spain)
fotw-es1701-e8.note: Burgundy cross dropped as ensign; red-gold-red ensign from 1785.

wp-first-mex-empire-e8.title: First Mexican Empire
wp-first-mex-empire-e8.note: Central American provinces annexed to the empire 1822-1823; map shows Nicaragua within it.

wp-voc-e8.title: Dutch East India Company
wp-voc-e8.note: Says the VOC monogram appeared on flags, cannons and coins.

wp-pt-ceylon-e8.title: Portuguese Ceylon
wp-pt-ceylon-e8.note: Infobox flag entry only; no flag text.

wp-flag-pt-e8.title: Flag of Portugal
wp-flag-pt-e8.note: Order of Christ cross over green and white as a naval pennon in the Discoveries.

wp-chola-flag-e8.title: Flag of Chola
wp-chola-flag-e8.note: Tiger flag of the Chola dynasty; tiger emblem on coins, seals and banners; Periya Puranam mention.

wp-tpr-e8.title: Tuvan People's Republic
wp-tpr-e8.note: Notes national symbols changed by 1941 and Cyrillic from September 1943; flag detail only in infobox.

wp-jerusalem-cross.title: Jerusalem cross
wp-jerusalem-cross.note: Says the cross became the arms of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem but was not used by its 12th-century rulers.

wp-ayyubid.title: Ayyubid dynasty
wp-ayyubid.note: No Ayyubid banner described; notes the Cairo Citadel eagle is commonly but unconfirmedly called Saladin's emblem.

wp-pan-arab-colors.title: Pan-Arab colors
wp-pan-arab-colors.note: White as the Umayyad dynastic colour and the Black Standard of the Rashidun and Abbasids; white banner also given for the Fatimids.

wp-jund-urdunn.title: Jund al-Urdunn
wp-jund-urdunn.note: Describes the district and its rule by Umayyad, Abbasid and Fatimid caliphates; mentions no banner.

wp-khvarenah.title: Khvarenah
wp-khvarenah.note: Iconography section: the Achaemenid winged emblem (Farr-e Kiyani/faravahar) from Darius I; identification disputed. The Faravahar URL now redirects to the Fravahr article.

wp-achaemenid.title: Achaemenid Empire
wp-achaemenid.note: Infobox: the Standard of Cyrus the Great, a golden eagle on a shaft, shown as a reconstruction; fall to Alexander in 330 BC.

wp-seleucid.title: Seleucid Empire
wp-seleucid.note: Note: horned horse, elephant, anchor, Nike and Tyche were common Seleucid symbols; empire dated 312-63 BC.

wp-seleucus-i.title: Seleucus I Nicator
wp-seleucus-i.note: Anchor legend: Seleucus said to have an anchor-shaped birthmark, from a ring with an anchor.

wp-parthian.title: Parthian Empire
wp-parthian.note: No Parthian standard described; coin of Mithridates II shows a seated archer with a bow.

wp-qadisiyyah.title: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
wp-qadisiyyah.note: Dated 16-19 November 636; the Sasanian Derafsh-e Kaveyan stood by Rustam and was taken as spoils.

wp-sasanian.title: Sasanian Empire
wp-sasanian.note: Infobox: 224-651, Derafsh Kaviani shown as the standard; fall to the Rashidun Caliphate 651.

wp-muisca-confederation.title: Muisca Confederation
wp-muisca-confederation.note: Long article on the Muisca (goldworking, El Dorado rite, 1537 conquest); describes no flag or banner.

devries-oman.title: Oman History and Heraldry
devries-oman.publisher: Hubert de Vries, National Arms and Emblems Past and Present
devries-oman.note: Early Omani heraldry: Diogo Homem 1555 map flag for Portuguese-held Oman; Ya'rubi flag from a mid-18th-century Dutch flag chart (13 stripes with green crescents); plain red flag of the Abu Sa'id dynasty from 1749.

wp-yarubid.title: Ya'rubid dynasty
wp-yarubid.note: Rulers of Oman 1624-1742; infobox shows an "Ensign of the Ya'rubids" citing de Vries (Oman History and Heraldry); the text describes no flag.

wp-portuguese-oman.title: Portuguese Oman
wp-portuguese-oman.note: Portuguese rule over the northern coastal cities 1507-1650/1656; no flag described.

wp-gna.title: Government of the Grand National Assembly
wp-gna.note: Ankara provisional government 1920-1923; the infobox flag file is the Ottoman flag, with no text describing it.

wp-mali-empire.title: Mali Empire
wp-mali-empire.note: Imperial regalia section: a red banner with a golden disc (Sun Banner of Sundiata, oral histories) and Mansa Musa's banner with yellow symbols on red (written sources); two possible reconstructions shown.

wp-songhai-empire.title: Songhai Empire
wp-songhai-empire.note: Long article on the empire; searched for flag, banner, standard, regalia, emblem: none described.

wp-viceroyalty-rdlp.title: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
wp-viceroyalty-rdlp.note: Infobox flag with a note calling it the first national flag, naval and fortress flag, the last to float in the continental Americas; Paraguay a province of the viceroyalty (Intendency of Paraguay).

wp-governorate-paraguay.title: Governorate of Paraguay
wp-governorate-paraguay.note: Governorate 1617-1782 within the Viceroyalty of Peru, then the Río de la Plata; no flag described in the text.

gov-si-zastava-f1.title: Dan slovenske zastave (7 April 2022)
gov-si-zastava-f1.publisher: GOV.SI (Ministrstvo za notranje zadeve, Government of Slovenia)
gov-si-zastava-f1.note: Slovenian government text: colours set from Carniola arms in 1848; Vienna Ministry of the Interior confirmed Carniolan provincial colours on 23 Sept 1848, set by Ferdinand in 1836; first raised in Ljubljana 7 April 1848.

muzej-nz-simboli-f1.title: Zepna zgodovina: Slovenski simboli (2026)
muzej-nz-simboli-f1.publisher: Muzej novejse zgodovine Slovenije (national museum of recent history)
muzej-nz-simboli-f1.note: Museum booklet repeating the 1848 account: Carniolan provincial colours confirmed by the Vienna Ministry of the Interior on 23 Sept 1848, set by Emperor Ferdinand in 1836.

fotw-yu-law1922-f1.title: Royal Yugoslavia (1918-1941): Law on the flags at sea, 1922 (full text)
fotw-yu-law1922-f1.publisher: Flags of the World (CRW Flags), transcribing Sluzbene novine #89/22
fotw-yu-law1922-f1.note: Transcribed text of the 1922 law: naval and merchant ensigns three equal horizontal fields blue-white-red (Articles 1 and 2).

fotw-yu-law1937-f1.title: Royal Yugoslavia (1918-1941): Law on the flags at sea, 1937 (full text)
fotw-yu-law1937-f1.publisher: Flags of the World (CRW Flags), transcribing the 1937 Zakon o zastavama jugoslavenskih brodova
fotw-yu-law1937-f1.note: Transcribed text of the 1937 law, which FOTW says left the blue-white-red ensign unchanged.

okupacijske-meje-f1.title: Make This Country German ... Italian ... Hungarian ... Croatian! (online exhibition, ch. 1)
okupacijske-meje-f1.note: Exhibition page on the 1941 occupation; one photo caption: Town Hall in Ptuj adorned with German flags. No flag designs described.

balkanflaghistory-si-f1.title: Flags of Slovenia under the Austrian Empire
balkanflaghistory-si-f1.note: Describes the Kingdom of Illyria flag as the Austrian arms over a white-red bicolour, 1816-1849, 2:3; its listed sources are Wikipedia articles and World Statesmen, so it is not independent.

ain-akbari-f1.title: A'in-i Akbari, Book 1, Ain 19: The Ensigns of Royalty (Blochmann translation)
ain-akbari-f1.publisher: Abu'l-Fazl Allami; transcription hosted by Frances Pritchett (Columbia University)
ain-akbari-f1.note: Primary text: the Alam or standard; when the king rides out not fewer than five are carried with the Qur, in scarlet cloth bags, unfurled on festivals and in battle. Describes no design.

terry-voyage-f1.title: A voyage to East-India (Edward Terry, 1655; 1777 edition), full text
terry-voyage-f1.note: Eyewitness chaplain at Jahangir court c.1617: the royal standard of the great Mogul is a couchant lion shadowing part of the body of the sun. No colour stated.

vam-mughal-standard-f1.title: Gouache: elephant with mahout and standard-bearer carrying a green standard with a gold sun (Delhi, c.1840)
vam-mughal-standard-f1.note: Museum record of a late Mughal court painting (c.1840): green standard with a gold sun.

fiav-chakrabarti-f1.title: A variant of a political party flag doubling as the national flag (S. Chakrabarti), ICV27 London 2017
fiav-chakrabarti-f1.note: Congress paper: Working Committee flag-committee resolution quoted; all-saffron proposal not accepted; Congress formally adopted the saffron-white-green flag with charkha on the white stripe at Bombay on 8 August 1931.

fiav-rao-f1.title: About the Genesis of the Indian National Flag (K. Sanjeeva Rao), ICV22 Berlin 2007
fiav-rao-f1.note: Congress address summary: a 1931 resolution adopted the saffron-white-green tricolour with a blue charkha on the white band; colour meanings given.

britannica-flag-in-f1.title: Flag of India
britannica-flag-in-f1.note: Britannica: the charkha flag was recognised as the Congress official flag at its meeting in August 1931, with saffron replacing red.

britannica-gupta-f1.title: Gupta dynasty
britannica-gupta-f1.note: Short page read; it does not mention a flag, banner or emblem.

pieris-ceylon-f1.title: Ceylon and the Portuguese, 1505-1658 (P. E. Pieris, 1920), full text
pieris-ceylon-f1.note: Historian text: Portuguese carried the Banner of Christ at Mulleriyawa (after 1559); the Royal Standard of Portugal was handed to Dom Antao at Malwana in 1597; designs not described.

britannica-flag-lk-f1.title: Flag of Sri Lanka
britannica-flag-lk-f1.note: Britannica: Kandy was forced to lower the Lion Flag on 2 March 1815; the Union Jack continued to fly until 29 October 1953.

bowdich-ashantee-f1.title: Mission from Cape Coast Castle to Ashantee (T. E. Bowdich, 1819), full text
bowdich-ashantee-f1.note: Eyewitness at Kumasi 1817: flags and banners waved in chiefs processions, the Kings banners, British, Dutch and Danish flags beside the state umbrella; no national design or colours described.

britannica-flag-gh-f1.title: Flag of Ghana
britannica-flag-gh-f1.note: Page read describes only the Convention Peoples Party flag of 1949; no colonial Gold Coast flag.

britannica-flag-my-f1.title: Flag of Malaysia
britannica-flag-my-f1.note: Britannica: Federated Malay States 1896 striped ensign with the Malay tiger on a white oval; Malayan Union 1 April 1946, Federation 1 February 1948; Federation flag first hoisted 26 May 1950. Nothing on Malacca.

britannica-flag-kn-f1.title: Flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis
britannica-flag-kn-f1.note: Britannica: united British colony 1882; associated state 27 February 1967 with a green-yellow-blue vertical flag and black palm of three fronds. No colonial flag described.

imamovic-lily-f1.title: The Bosnian Fleur-de-lis (Enver Imamovic), Spirit of Bosnia 1(2), 2006
imamovic-lily-f1.note: Advocacy essay by a Bosnian archaeologist: medieval Bosnia had a fleur-de-lis flag and arms, evidenced by King Tvrtko I seals, coins and mantle (14th century); no Banate-period flag described.

hrvatska-enc-kotromanici-f1.title: Kotromanici
hrvatska-enc-kotromanici-f1.note: Encyclopedia entry: dynasty c.1250-1463, Stjepan II ban 1322-53, Tvrtko I ban 1353-77 and king 1377-91; says nothing about a flag or arms.

britannica-flag-ba-f1.title: Flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina
britannica-flag-ba-f1.note: Britannica: the 1992 flag used the six-lily arms of King Stjepan Tomas (1443-61), attributed to Tvrtko I (1377-91).

cetin-ottoman-crescent-f1.title: Osmanli Bayraklarinda Ay ve Ay Yildiz (Elif Cetin), Turk Arkeoloji ve Etnografya Dergisi 83
cetin-ottoman-crescent-f1.publisher: Turk Arkeoloji ve Etnografya Dergisi (peer-reviewed journal, via DergiPark)
cetin-ottoman-crescent-f1.note: Article on Ottoman flags: sultan banners (saltanat sancaklari) existed in several colours; the Selim I banner (TSM 824) is described as indigo silk with three gold crescents; official crescent-and-star use is generally dated after Selim III. Nothing Egypt-specific.

hubert-herald-jerusalem-f1.title: Jerusalem Arms (Hubert de Vries)
hubert-herald-jerusalem-f1.note: Heraldry survey citing seals, coins, Matthew Paris, a York Minster window, Wijnbergen and Camden rolls: arms of the kings of Jerusalem only in the first half of the 13th century; no banner of the kingdom described.

henning-german-pacific-f1.title: German Colonial Policy in the Pacific Islands (R. M. Henning), MA thesis, University of Hawaii, 1982
henning-german-pacific-f1.note: Thesis: protectorate over the Marshall Islands claimed in 1885, administered first by the Jaluit Gesellschaft whose charter ended in 1906. No flag described.

paz-soldan-f1.title: Historia del Peru independiente, primer periodo 1819-1822 (M. F. Paz Soldan, 1868), full text
paz-soldan-f1.note: Nineteenth-century history citing the decrees: 21 Oct 1820 quartered flag; 15 Mar 1822 red-white-red with a sun on the white band; later made vertical; Congress approved Feb 1825.

britannica-flag-pe-f1.title: Flag of Peru
britannica-flag-pe-f1.note: Britannica: 1820 quartered flag; 15 March 1822 horizontal red-white-red; altered 31 May 1822 to vertical stripes with a sun; 25 February 1825 design with arms.

iranica-flags-f10.title: Flags i. Of Persia
iranica-flags-f10.note: Abbasid black banners and client rulers; Ghaznavid, Saljuq and Parthian-era banner notes.

iranica-deraf-f10.title: Derafš
iranica-deraf-f10.note: Banners of Achaemenid, Seleucid-era Persis, Parthian and Sasanian periods, with ancient authors cited.

iranica-army-f10.title: Army i. Pre-Islamic Iran
iranica-army-f10.note: Parthian army organisation; the drafsh as a unit of 1,000 and Parthian banners with dragons.

wp-khiva-f10.title: Khanate of Khiva
wp-khiva-f10.note: Footnote: pre-Soviet Khivan flag unknown (David Straub on FOTW); museum flag 1917-22.

commons-turk-flag-f10.title: File:Turkestan Autonomous SSR Flag.svg
commons-turk-flag-f10.note: File page names no source beyond 'Туркестан' / 'ЦИК ТССР'; uploaded 2022 as own work.

brit-flag-ru-f10.title: flag of Russia
brit-flag-ru-f10.note: Whitney Smith: white-blue-red merchant flag of 1699; the tsars' black-orange-white land flag failed.

he-ilirske-f10.title: Ilirske pokrajine
he-ilirske-f10.note: Illyrian Provinces under French administration 1809-13; no flag text.

brit-illyr-f10.title: Illyrian Provinces
brit-illyr-f10.note: Part of Napoleon's French Empire 1809-1814; no flag text.

ustav-fnrj-1946-f10.title: Ustav Federativne Narodne Republike Jugoslavije (1946), Article 4
ustav-fnrj-1946-f10.publisher: Wikisource (Serbian), text of the Constitution of 31 January 1946
ustav-fnrj-1946-f10.note: Article 4 states the state flag: blue, white, red with a red five-pointed star with golden-yellow edge.

fotw-yu-law1922-f10.title: Royal Yugoslavia (1918-1941): Law on the flags at sea, 1922
fotw-yu-law1922-f10.note: English translation (Z. Heimer) of the Law on Ensigns of War, Merchant and Private Vessels, Sluzbene novine 89/22, 28 Feb 1922.

zpe-godlo-f10.title: Znam swoje godlo, barwy, hymn narodowy (karta zadan)
zpe-godlo-f10.publisher: Zintegrowana Platforma Edukacyjna (Polish Ministry of Education)
zpe-godlo-f10.note: Says the eagle is on the coins, banners (chorągwie) and shields of the Piast state from the twelfth century.

rp-znamierowski-f10.title: Najpierw był karmazyn (interview with Alfred Znamierowski)
rp-znamierowski-f10.note: Heraldist: Polish banner for centuries was a red banner with a white eagle; eagle on seal of Przemysl II 1295; oldest colour depiction early 14th c.

pl-ustawa-1919-f10.title: Ustawa z dnia 1 sierpnia 1919 r. o godle i barwach Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
pl-ustawa-1919-f10.note: Art. 1 point 3: national colours white and red, the upper stripe white, the lower red.

pl-dekret-1955-f10.title: Dekret o godle i barwach Polskiej Rzeczypospolitej Ludowej oraz o pieczeciach panstwowych (Dz.U. 1955 nr 47 poz. 314)
pl-dekret-1955-f10.note: Colours white over red; last article repeals the regulations of 13 Dec 1927 on arms and colours.

commons-alam-f10.title: File:Alam (Banner) of Alauddin Hussain Shah.png
commons-alam-f10.note: Source: Bhattacharyya, Progressive Tripura (1930) p. 20, extracted from a photograph of a banner and gun of Hossein Shah captured by Dhanya Manikya, preserved at Agartala.

flaggenlexikon-se-f10.title: Schweden - Flagge in Lexikon und Shop
flaggenlexikon-se-f10.note: King John III's wish of 1569 that the cross be used on all banners and flags of the realm; timeline: conquest of Estonia 1561.

ozoutback-mw-f10.title: Flags from Malawi
ozoutback-mw-f10.note: Blue Ensign with emblem 1891; 1914 arms (leopard, rising sun) on a white disk; 1919, 1925 changes; 1953 Federation Blue Ensign.

ieu-regalia-f10.title: Regalia
ieu-regalia-f10.note: Cossack banners usually of carmine cloth with saints, crosses and coats of arms.

ieu-coa-f10.title: Coat of arms
ieu-coa-f10.note: Territorial arms (Lviv/Halych lion from the 14th c.; Zaporozhian Host's armed Cossack from the 16th c.).

unesco-abomey-f10.title: Royal Palaces of Abomey
unesco-abomey-f10.note: Twelve kings of Dahomey from 1625 to 1900; no flag text.

avalon-paris1763-f10.title: The Definitive Treaty of Peace 1763 (Treaty of Paris)
avalon-paris1763-f10.note: Article IX: Dominica, St Vincent and Tobago to remain in full right to Great Britain.

unesco-stlouis-f10.title: Island of Saint-Louis
unesco-stlouis-f10.note: First French chartered-company post on the Atlantic coast of Africa, 1659; capital of French West Africa to 1902; no flag text.

vexil-tuva-f10.title: Флаги Тувы (Flags of Tuva)
vexil-tuva-f10.note: Specialist page citing the Tuvan constitutions of 1926 and 1930, Tuvan historians and V. Sokolov in The Flag Bulletin XXII.

tdv-bayrak-f2.title: BAYRAK
tdv-bayrak-f2.note: Encyclopedia article on Islamic and Turkish flags, naming its sources (Yafii, Kalkashandi, Selaniki, Ibn Iyas, d'Ohsson): Ayyubid and Mamluk sultanic banners yellow, Baybars' lion/panther, Ottoman white and red sancaks, crescent-and-star from the late 18th century.

heraldica-jerusalem-f2.title: Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem (Heraldica)
heraldica-jerusalem-f2.note: Cites Pinoteau (Cahiers d'Heraldique) and Schlumberger: Jerusalem arms not known before the 1230s; seals of the kings bear no arms; little evidence on arms of the Crusader states; nothing for Oultrejordain.

heraldica-byzantine-f2.title: Byzantine Heraldry (Heraldica)
heraldica-byzantine-f2.note: Main source D. Cernovodeanu (Jahrbuch der Osterreichischen Byzantinistik 32, 1982): heraldry only after 1261; the tetragrammatic cross was the arms of the empire; Palaiologos arms a gold cross and four B's on red; eagle an imperial-family emblem, double-headed settled in the 15th century.

britannica-jo-flag-f2.title: Flag of Jordan
britannica-jo-flag-f2.note: Transjordan flag = Arab Revolt flag plus a white seven-pointed star; recognized under the Transjordan constitution of 16 April 1928; unchanged at independence on 22 March 1946.

ws-jo-f2.title: Jordan (flags and chronology)
ws-jo-f2.note: Flag strip with dates: Ottoman flag to 25 Sep 1918; British flag 25 Sep 1918-25 May 1923; Emirate of Transjordan flag 30 Mar 1921-16 Apr 1928; Hashemite Kingdom flag adopted 16 Apr 1928. Images only, no descriptions.

britannica-cd-flag-f2.title: Flag of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
britannica-cd-flag-f2.note: Free State flag blue with a gold star from 1877; six stars added along the hoist at independence in 1960; Kabila restored that flag from 17 May 1997; the red-diagonal flag returned with the Third Republic on 18 Feb 2006.

cd-constitution-f2.title: Constitution of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2005 (rev. 2011), Article 1
cd-constitution-f2.note: Article 1: the flag is sky-blue with a yellow star in the upper-left corner, crossed on the bias by a red band finely outlined in yellow.

ws-cd-f2.title: Congo (Kinshasa) (flags and chronology)
ws-cd-f2.note: Flag strip: Congo Free State and Belgian Congo flag 21 Jun 1877-30 Jun 1960; flag of 17 May 1997-18 Feb 2006; current flag adopted 18 Feb 2006. Images only.

baloji-villamedici-f2.title: Sammy Baloji, Congo's Fragments (exhibition book; introduction to the 1514 letter of Afonso I)
baloji-villamedici-f2.note: Introduction to the letter held at the Torre do Tombo: Manuel I proposed that Afonso put the memory of his 1506 victory in his coat of arms; the design was brought to Kongo in 1512 by Simao da Silva and Alvaro Lopes; Afonso adopted it.

wp-history-sm-f2.title: History of San Marino
wp-history-sm-f2.note: Foundation by tradition in 301; the Statutes of 1600 promulgated 1 September 1600; no flag is mentioned.

ws-sm-f2.title: San Marino (flags and chronology)
ws-sm-f2.note: Flag strip: old flag before 1465 to before 1797; later flag before 1797-2011 (state flag from 6 Apr 1862); Statutes dated 8 Oct 1600. Images only.

hardman-malta-f2.title: A History of Malta during the Period of the French and British Occupations, 1798-1815 (ed. W. Hardman)
hardman-malta-f2.publisher: Longmans, Green & Co., 1909 (full text on the Internet Archive)
hardman-malta-f2.note: Narrative built on contemporary dispatches: French tricolour cockade decree and tricolour at Valletta, white and red Maltese standard at Notabile (Sept 1798), Sicilian and British colours hoisted together, British colours only at Valletta in Sept 1800.

ws-mt-f2.title: Malta (flags and chronology)
ws-mt-f2.note: Flag strip: French flag 12 Jun 1798-8 Sep 1800; flag of the United Kingdom 8 Sep 1800-1875. Images only.

ws-lc-f2.title: Saint Lucia (flags and chronology)
ws-lc-f2.note: Flag strip: Union flag 1781-83, 1794-95, 1796-1802 and 1803-1875; colonial flag 1875-1939 and 1939-1967; Pitons flag 1967-79. Dated list of British and French periods.

britannica-br-flag-f2.title: Flag of Brazil
britannica-br-flag-f2.note: Independent Brazil's flag: green field, yellow diamond, imperial arms in the centre with a star for each state; colours from Braganza and Habsburg; arms replaced in 1889.

ws-br-f2.title: Brazil (flags and chronology)
ws-br-f2.note: Flag strip: first flag of the Empire 18 Sep-1 Dec 1822; second flag 1 Dec 1822-15 Nov 1889. Images only.

britannica-sv-flag-f2.title: Flag of El Salvador
britannica-sv-flag-f2.note: Central America's independence of 15 Sep 1821 reasserted in 1823 after two years of Mexican rule; Arce's blue-white-blue flag blessed in San Salvador on 20 Feb 1822; no mention of an imperial flag.

ws-sv-f2.title: El Salvador (flags and chronology)
ws-sv-f2.note: Province of San Salvador repudiated incorporation into Mexico on 11 Jan 1822; incorporation into Mexico dated 10 Feb 1823; Central America independent 1 Jul 1823; flag strip lists a provincial flag 1821-22 and a Salvador civil flag 1823, no Mexican flag.

ws-kz-f2.title: Kazakhstan (flags and chronology)
ws-kz-f2.note: Flag strip lists a Russian flag for 1824-Dec 1917 (no design given), nothing earlier.

lawphil-act1696-f2.title: Act No. 1696 (Flag Law), 23 August 1907
lawphil-act1696-f2.note: Philippine Commission act punishing display of flags used against the authority of the United States and of Katipunan flags.

lawphil-act2871-f2.title: Act No. 2871, 22 October 1919
lawphil-act2871-f2.note: Repeals Act 1696 and provides a holiday for the restoration of the use of the Filipino flag.

philippinediary-1898-f2.title: Saturday, August 13, 1898 (Philippine Diary Project)
philippinediary-1898-f2.note: Diary entry of the day Manila was surrendered: the Spanish flag was lowered and replaced by the American flag.

ws-ph-f2.title: The Philippines (flags and chronology)
ws-ph-f2.note: Flag strip: United States flag 14 Aug 1898-25 Mar 1936; Philippine flags listed separately (1898-1907, unofficial local flag from 1920). Images only.

britannica-sg-flag-f2.title: Flag of Singapore
britannica-sg-flag-f2.note: Singapore acquired its own flag on 3 Dec 1959; there was no change in its flag when it became a state of Malaysia in 1963, nor on separation on 9 Aug 1965.

ws-sg-f2.title: Singapore (flags and chronology)
ws-sg-f2.note: Flag strip: 1959 flag adopted 3 Dec 1959 and listed without interruption; no Malaysian-period flag listed.

britannica-to-flag-f2.title: Flag of Tonga
britannica-to-flag-f2.note: Flag first hoisted in 1866 and codified in the constitution of 4 November 1875; by law the national flag of Tonga may not be altered.

constitution-tonga-f2.title: Constitution of Tonga, 1875 (rev. 2013), section 47
constitution-tonga-f2.note: Section 47: the Flag of Tonga (the flag of King George) shall never be altered but shall always be the flag of the Kingdom. Text read is the 2013 revision.

ws-to-f2.title: Tonga (flags and chronology)
ws-to-f2.note: Flag strip: one national flag, adopted 1866 and confirmed 4 Nov 1875, listed to the present with no separate protected-state flag.

ws-bg-f2.title: Bulgaria (flags and chronology)
ws-bg-f2.note: Flag strip: Ottoman flag to 16 Apr 1879 (de jure to 5 Oct 1908); Bulgarian nationalist flag 'Freedom or Death' 1868-1877.

ws-gr-f2.title: Greece (flags and chronology)
ws-gr-f2.note: Flag strip: Ottoman flag to 24 Jan 1822, then provisional Greek flags.

ws-vn-f2.title: Vietnam (flags and chronology)
ws-vn-f2.note: Flag strip labels a Long Tinh emperor's flag 1802-1878/c.1885 (to 1863); image captions only, no description or basis (the FOTW chronology cites this site).

snl-pt-flag-f3.title: Portugals flagg og våpen
snl-pt-flag-f3.note: Encyclopedia article: republic flag adopted by parliament 19 June 1911; royal flag before 1910, blue-and-white from 1830.

pt-pres-simbolica-f3.title: Do azul-branco ao verde-rubro: a simbólica da bandeira nacional
pt-pres-simbolica-f3.publisher: Presidência da República Portuguesa (arquivo Jorge Sampaio)
pt-pres-simbolica-f3.note: Official essay: decree of 1911; says the same flag stood through the Military Dictatorship, the Estado Novo and 25 April; blue-and-white flag under the constitutional monarchy.

pt-pres-simbolos-f3.title: Símbolos Nacionais: Bandeira Nacional (decree of 19 June 1911)
pt-pres-simbolos-f3.note: Quotes the Constituent Assembly decree of 19 June 1911 (Diário do Governo no. 141) and cites the regulation of 30 June 1911 (no. 150).

bri-zambia-f3.title: flag of Zambia
bri-zambia-f3.note: Independence flag of 24 Oct 1964 based on the UNIP flag; Northern Rhodesia shield approved 1930 and used as a Blue Ensign badge, arms confirmed 16 Aug 1939.

fotw-rs-despo-f3.title: Despotovac (Municipality, Serbia)
fotw-rs-despo-f3.note: Describes Despot Stefan Lazarević's arms (double-headed eagle kept; a Hungarian-derived shield probably marking vassalage), citing Samardžić 1983 and Spasić et al. 1992.

wp-serbian-eagle-f3.title: Serbian eagle
wp-serbian-eagle-f3.note: Stefan Lazarević adopted the double-headed eagle as despot in 1402; Richental's Council of Constance chronicle (1420) shows his arms as a red shield with a gold double-headed eagle.

n1-srb-zastava-f3.title: Od Prvog srpskog ustanka do danas: kako se menjala srpska zastava
n1-srb-zastava-f3.note: Says no single flag in 1804 (voivodship banners, mostly with a cross); Miloš unfurled his old voivodship banner at Takovo in 1815 (no colours); gives the 1835 Sretenje flag and the December 1835 and January 1839 firmans.

nr-belgrade-heraldry-f3.title: Under the Eagle's Shield: a little heraldic history of Belgrade
nr-belgrade-heraldry-f3.note: States Belgrade had no coat of arms under Turkish rule; Serbia received arms and a flag with the 1835 Sretenje constitution.

hotw-ruanda-urundi-f3.title: Ruanda-Urundi
hotw-ruanda-urundi-f3.note: Unofficial colonial arms of Ruanda-Urundi (crane over lion's head) used until 1962; no flag described.

rmg-red-ensign-f3.title: Red Ensign (before 1864)
rmg-red-ensign-f3.note: Museum record: Red Ensign worn by British merchant vessels from the early 17th century; Union Flag in canton after 1707, St Patrick's saltire only from 1801.

fotw-lv-riga-f3.title: Riga - Historical Flags (Latvia)
fotw-lv-riga-f3.note: Riga merchant flag white with red arms after 1582; mid-17th-century Swedish merchant flag with arms on red; city flags only.

wp-flag-riga-f3.title: Flag of Riga
wp-flag-riga-f3.note: Riga white flag with red arms after 1582; blue flag with yellow cross granted by the Swedish king, used until 1860; blue-white city flag of 1673.

hubert-gq-f3.title: Guinea Ecuatorial
hubert-gq-f3.note: History note: Bioko and Annobón colonised by Portugal in 1474, ceded to Spain 1778; no flag mentioned.

kure-tr-f3.title: Turkish Flag
kure-tr-f3.note: Encyclopedia article: red crescent-and-star flag official under the late Ottoman state and inherited by the Republic; says nothing of 1919-23.

wp-brothers-sword-f3.title: Livonian Brothers of the Sword
wp-brothers-sword-f3.note: Read for a banner or flag of the Order of the Sword Brothers (1202-1236): none described.

wp-karyenda-f3.title: Karyenda
wp-karyenda-f3.note: Karyenda drum on the national flag and arms 1962-1966 (cites Smith/Talocci, Guide to the Flags of the World).

wp-german-occ-lv-f3.title: German occupation of Latvia during World War II
wp-german-occ-lv-f3.note: Read for flag provisions under the German occupation: none in the text.

wp-livonian-confed-f3.title: Livonian Confederation
wp-livonian-confed-f3.note: Read for a banner of the Livonian Order or Confederation: none described.

gw-presidency-f3.title: Sobre a Guiné-Bissau
gw-presidency-f3.note: Official page: the national flag was adopted in 1973 at the proclamation of independence; says nothing of the PAIGC flag in the war.

ws-mv-f4.title: Maldives
ws-mv-f4.note: Chronology: Portuguese occupation of Male 19 May 1558 - 1 Jul 1573; British protectorate from 16 Dec 1887; republic 1 Jan 1953; sultanate restored 7 Mar 1954. Flag images captioned 19.. - c.1933, c.1933 - 1953, 1953 - 26 Jul 1965 (captions only, no description).

mv-rf-f4.title: Maldive flags, Part 1 (Xavier Romero-Frias)
mv-rf-f4.note: Essay by the ethnographer Xavier Romero-Frias: royal flags plain red pennants; no real national flag before about 1903; striped dhandimathi added at an undated time (perhaps early nineteenth century); crescent and green rectangle only later.

mv-flag-f4.title: The Maldive Flag Mystery
mv-flag-f4.note: Opinion page: red flag until 1903, crescent inserted 1903 on a green field, crescent turned to face the fly by 1949, striped hoist removed 1965; dates differ from Wikipedia.

nij-hist-f4.title: Historical flags (Torteneti zaszlok)
nij-hist-f4.publisher: Hungarian National and Historical Symbols (NISZ, Hungarian government)
nij-hist-f4.note: Government gallery of reconstructed historical flags: red-and-silver striped family flag of the Arpad kings used by all mixed-house kings; Zrinyi 1566, Nyitra county 1660, Rakoczi flags described.

nij-home-f4.title: National flag history (home page)
nij-home-f4.publisher: Hungarian National and Historical Symbols (NISZ, Hungarian government)
nij-home-f4.note: Red-silver-green appears from the fifteenth century on seal cords and banner edges, described in this order only in 1806, first prescribed by Act XXI of 1848.

ws-hu-f4.title: Hungary
ws-hu-f4.note: Flag image sequence (captions only): Kingdom of Hungary 1382-1804; Austrian imperial flag 1804-1848 and 1849-1867; Hungarian land-colours flag 1848-1918; state flag 21 Dec 1867 - 1 Feb 1946 variants.

martykan-f4.title: A history of Ottoman military flags (J. Martykan)
martykan-f4.publisher: International Congress of Vexillology proceedings, XVII (FIAV)
martykan-f4.note: Paper by a vexillologist: sanjak beys and provincial governors (beylerbeys) had personal flags and tughs, coloured fields with a gold zulfikar, few with crescents; simpler red flags in the 17th-18th century land forces.

albert-turul-f4.title: A hungarista allam cimere (1944-1945) (Z. M. Albert), Turul 98(3)
albert-turul-f4.publisher: Turul, journal of the Hungarian Heraldic and Genealogical Society
albert-turul-f4.note: Scholarly article quoting decree 23/1945 M.E. (1 Jan 1945): the Szalasi government redefined the small state arms (laid on a green arrow cross) for the state seal; no state flag is mentioned.

sk-snem-t15-f4.title: Government bill on the state flag, state arms and seal (print 15), Slovak Diet 1939
sk-snem-t15-f4.publisher: Slovak Diet 1939 (Czech Chamber of Deputies digital library)
sk-snem-t15-f4.note: June 1939 bill: white-blue-red state flag; reasons say the colours are to remain white, blue and red (Slovak tricolour of the Stur and Hurban banners) and that laws 252/1920 and 269/1936 were the flag laws then in force.

sk-snem-t19-f4.title: Committee report and final text on the state flag, arms and seal (print 19), Slovak Diet 1939
sk-snem-t19-f4.publisher: Slovak Diet 1939 (Czech Chamber of Deputies digital library)
sk-snem-t19-f4.note: Constitutional-legal committee report of 23 June 1939 and text of the law: flag of white, blue (Paris blue) and red fields; repeals conflicting earlier provisions.

ws-sk-f4.title: Slovakia
ws-sk-f4.note: Flag image sequence (captions only): Slovak flag 1848 and 14 Mar 1939 - 3 Apr 1945; Czechoslovak flag 30 Mar 1920 - 14 Mar 1939.

ws-cv-f4.title: Cabo Verde (Cape Verde)
ws-cv-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): Portugal flag to 5 Jul 1975; 1967 colonial flag proposal; independence flags from 1975.

ws-gy-f4.title: Guyana
ws-gy-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): Netherlands 1616-1781, 1784-96, 1802-03; United Kingdom flag 1781-82, 1796-1802, 1803-1875; British Guiana flags 1875-1906, 1906-1954, 1954-1966.

ws-fm-f4.title: Micronesia
ws-fm-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): Spanish ensign 1886 - 12 Oct 1899; German Empire flag 12 Oct 1899 - 7 Oct 1914; Japan flag 7 Oct 1914 - 1944; US flag from 1944.

bundesarchiv-ponape-f4.title: Aufruhr auf Ponape (Bundesarchiv online gallery)
bundesarchiv-ponape-f4.note: Archive gallery: imperial decree of 18 July 1899 making the Carolines, Marianas and Palau protectorates; handover protocol at Ponape 12 Oct 1899; attached to German New Guinea. No flag described.

fotw-jp-spa-f4.title: South Pacific Agency (Japan)
fotw-jp-spa-f4.note: Contributor note: Japan administered the former German islands from Koror; no special regional flag was made apart from a 1930 fishery vessel service flag.

ws-af-f4.title: Afghanistan
ws-af-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only) begins 1881 - c.1901; nothing for 1747-1881.

britannica-af-f4.title: Flag of Afghanistan (Whitney Smith)
britannica-af-f4.note: Covers twentieth-century flags only; the old Afghan flag (white emblem on black) restored after 1929.

ws-ag-f4.title: Antigua and Barbuda
ws-ag-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): UK flag to 1874; Leeward Islands colony flag 1874-1956; Antigua flag 1956-58 and 1958-1967.

ws-bf-f4.title: Burkina Faso
ws-bf-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): France 20 Feb 1895 - 9 Dec 1959; Upper Volta flag 9 Dec 1959 - 4 Aug 1984.

britannica-et-f4.title: Flag of Ethiopia (Whitney Smith)
britannica-et-f4.note: In 1975 a revolutionary government established a new coat of arms with socialist symbols; 1987 flag of the People's Democratic Republic had a red star at the top.

ws-et-f4.title: Ethiopia
ws-et-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): imperial flag 5 May 1941 - 1 Jan 1975; state flag 1 Jan - 12 Sep 1975 and 12 Sep 1975 - 12 Sep 1987; 1987-91 state flag.

hubert-kw-f4.title: Kuwait (Hubert de Vries)
hubert-kw-f4.publisher: Hubert Herald (Hubert de Vries, heraldic studies)
hubert-kw-f4.note: Heraldry survey: Kuwait's flag at first that of an Ottoman military commander (green, white crescent and star); Ottoman national flag added 1871; red flags with white inscription from 1903/1906.

ws-kw-f4.title: Kuwait
ws-kw-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only): Ottoman flag to 3 Nov 1914; a flag of Kuwait before 1899; British-protectorate flags 1899-1961.

ws-mn-f4.title: Mongolia
ws-mn-f4.note: Flag sequence (captions only) begins 29 Dec 1911; nothing for the Qing period.

vm-mn-f4.title: Mongolia history (Vexilla Mundi)
vm-mn-f4.note: Image-based page: pre-1872 sulde banners (white-haired banner, Nine White Banners); Qing dynasty flags listed for Mongolia 1872-1890 and 1890-1911.

treccani-bandiera-f4.title: Bandiera (Enciclopedia Italiana, 1930), section Bandiera pontificia
treccani-bandiera-f4.note: White-and-yellow papal flag adopted some years after 1814 for troops and state; the popes of the nineteenth century used a white cloth with personal arms as royal flag; nothing stated on 1870-1929.

vx-az-hanstva-f5.title: Azerbaijani khanates (Vexillographia)
vx-az-hanstva-f5.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vx-az-hanstva-f5.note: Describes surviving Ganja, Nakhchivan, Sheki and Baku khanate banners in Russian and Azerbaijani museums, citing P. Gezalov's work, Dubrovin and a 1804 report by Tsitsianov; says information on khanate banners is scarce.

vx-az-inrussia-f5.title: Azerbaijani lands in the Russian Empire (Vexillographia)
vx-az-inrussia-f5.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vx-az-inrussia-f5.note: Says the 'reconstructed' flags of Azerbaijani counties and towns shown in the Baku flag museum are decorative and not based on real historical flags.

vx-az-soviet-f5.title: Soviet Azerbaijan (Vexillographia)
vx-az-soviet-f5.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vx-az-soviet-f5.note: Quotes the flag articles of the Azerbaijan SSR constitutions and the 1952, 1953 and 1956 decrees; the 1953 text gives the lower stripe as blue, one quarter of the width.

vx-az-modern-f5.title: Republic of Azerbaijan from 1990 (Vexillographia)
vx-az-modern-f5.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vx-az-modern-f5.note: Quotes the Nakhchivan resolution of 17 Nov 1990, the decree of 29 Nov 1990, the law of 5 Feb 1991 and Article 23 of the 1995 Constitution.

vx-turkestan-f5.title: Turkestan (Vexillographia)
vx-turkestan-f5.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vx-turkestan-f5.note: Describes the 1917 autonomous Turkestan flag and the 1921 Jami'at flag (after Trembicky) and says the Turkestan ASSR had no official flag or coat of arms.

worldstatesmen-az-f5.title: Azerbaijan (World Statesmen)
worldstatesmen-az-f5.note: Shows a Russian flag, unspecified, for Azerbaijan from 6 Oct 1806 to 22 Apr 1918.

egypt-museum-sneferu-f5.title: Statue of King Sneferu (Egypt Museum)
egypt-museum-sneferu-f5.note: Describes Cairo Museum JE 98943, a Fourth Dynasty limestone statue of Sneferu (c. 2600 BC) wearing the White Hedjet crown.

res-gestae-f5.title: Res Gestae Divi Augusti, Section V (chapter 27)
res-gestae-f5.publisher: LacusCurtius (Bill Thayer), after the Loeb Classical Library edition, 1924
res-gestae-f5.note: Chapter 27 of Augustus's own record states that he added Egypt to the empire of the Roman people (no date given in the chapter).

amica-nectanebo-f5.title: The God Horus Protecting King Nectanebo II (Metropolitan Museum 34.2.1, AMICA record)
amica-nectanebo-f5.publisher: AMICA Library, contributed by The Metropolitan Museum of Art
amica-nectanebo-f5.note: Museum record of a Dynasty 30 statue: Horus wears a double crown said to symbolise dominion over Upper and Lower Egypt; the small king wears a nemes headcloth and uraeus.

iranica-flags-f5.title: Flags i. Of Persia (Encyclopaedia Iranica)
iranica-flags-f5.note: Survey of Persian banners from the Umayyad and Abbasid period to the Qajars, citing Tabari, Chardin, Hanway, Herbert and other named sources.

lorimer-gazetteer-f5.title: Gazetteer of the Persian Gulf, Vol I Historical, Part IA, p. 672 (J. G. Lorimer, 1915)
lorimer-gazetteer-f5.publisher: British Library India Office Records, via Qatar Digital Library
lorimer-gazetteer-f5.note: Says Article 3 of the 1820 General Treaty prescribed the 'White-pierced-Red' flag, the red centre understood to perpetuate the blood-red flag of the Qawasim and the white border a symbol of peace (machine transcription, may contain errors).

qdl-ior-1694-f5.title: 'Flags Flown by the Sheikh of Qatar. (Bahrain and Trucial Coast)' IOR/R/15/2/1694, f. 32r
qdl-ior-1694-f5.publisher: British Library India Office Records, via Qatar Digital Library
qdl-ior-1694-f5.note: 1930s British official note: a flag used only by the sheikhs of Sharjah and Ras al-Khaimah (the Qawasim tribal flag); all other Trucial sheikhs fly an oblong flag about three times as long as wide, five-sixths red with the sixth nearest the mast white (machine transcription, garbled).

govis-flag-f5.title: A brief history of the Icelandic flag (B. Thorlacius)
govis-flag-f5.note: Official history quoting the royal decrees of 22 Nov 1913 and 19 June 1915 and the 1918 and 1944 flag legislation; says the 1913 decree does not restrict flying the Dannebrog 'as in the past'.

snl-island-f5.title: Islands flagg og våpen (L. Roede)
snl-island-f5.note: Says the flag was adopted for use on land on 19 June 1915, at sea in 1918, and as national flag on 17 June 1944; Iceland's stockfish arms were part of the Danish-Norwegian royal arms from 1592.

snl-finland-f5.title: Finlands flagg og våpen (L. Roede)
snl-finland-f5.note: Says Finland was part of Sweden from the Middle Ages and had no flag of its own; Russia's flag served until 1917.

snl-sverige-f5.title: Sveriges flagg og våpen (L. Roede)
snl-sverige-f5.note: Says the Swedish flag is first shown in Gustav Vasa's 1557 letter of arms to Duke John and was probably first used officially in connection with the 1562 mission to England.

he-crna-gora-f5.title: Crna Gora (Hrvatska enciklopedija)
he-crna-gora-f5.note: History section: Zetska banovina created by the law of 3 Oct 1929; Italian occupation in 1941; an 'independent Montenegro' proclaimed by the Montenegrin assembly on 12 July 1941 under Italian protectorate. No flag is described.

bernal-diaz-f5.title: Verdadera historia de los sucesos de la conquista de la Nueva-España (B. Diaz del Castillo)
bernal-diaz-f5.note: Eyewitness chronicle: in Cuba Cortes had standards and banners made, worked in gold, with the royal arms and a cross on each side and a Latin motto on following the sign of the Holy Cross.

britannica-flag-turkey-f5.title: Flag of Turkey (W. Smith)
britannica-flag-turkey-f5.note: Says there were several Ottoman flags in red or green with crescent and star, and that the present design was established for the navy in June 1793 (eight-pointed star), the star reduced to five points about 1844.

canada-ca-flag-history-f5.title: The history of the National Flag of Canada
canada-ca-flag-history-f5.publisher: Government of Canada, Canadian Heritage (Canadian Heraldic Authority images)
canada-ca-flag-history-f5.note: Says that from the first days of European presence the flags of homelands such as France were displayed, and describes the historic royal banner of France as a blue field with three golden fleurs-de-lis.

sudan-convention-f5.title: Sudan Convention (1899), Article II
sudan-convention-f5.publisher: Wikisource (text of the Anglo-Egyptian agreement of 19 January 1899)
sudan-convention-f5.note: Article II: the British and Egyptian flags shall be used together on land and water throughout the Sudan, except in Suakin, where the Egyptian flag alone shall be used.

britannica-ruanda-f5.title: Ruanda-Urundi
britannica-ruanda-f5.note: Says Belgium administered Ruanda-Urundi 1922-62 (League of Nations mandate from 1924, UN trust territory from 1946) as an integral part of the Belgian Congo with a separate budget; no flag mentioned.

marineinfo-parmentier-f6.title: Profit and neutrality: the case of Ostend, 1781-1783 (bibliographic record)
marineinfo-parmentier-f6.publisher: VLIZ / Flanders Marine Institute (MARBEF Marine Info)
marineinfo-parmentier-f6.note: Abstract of Parmentier (1997): the use of the neutral imperial flag in Ostend shipping, 1781-83; no design given.

lupant-fiav-f6.title: Flags and Coats of Arms of the Kingdom of Belgium (Lupant)
lupant-fiav-f6.publisher: FIAV, Proceedings of the 30th International Congress of Vexillology (Beijing 2024)
lupant-fiav-f6.note: Brabant colours 1787-90; 26 Aug 1830 flag on Brussels city hall; horizontal first flag; vertical flag adopted 23 Jan 1831; black at the hoist set Sept-Oct 1831.

gibson-journal-f6.title: A Journal from Our Legation in Belgium (Hugh Gibson)
gibson-journal-f6.publisher: Project Gutenberg (diary of a US legation secretary, 1914-15)
gibson-journal-f6.note: Diary entry of 18 Sept 1914 reproducing the military governor von Luettwitz's notice asking Brussels householders to take down Belgian flags; says nothing of a German flag.

eupen-lre-f6.title: Eupen Town Hall
eupen-lre-f6.note: Heimattreue Front took over Eupen town hall and hoisted a swastika flag on 10 May 1940 (area annexed by Germany).

flaginst-union-f6.title: History of the Union Flag
flaginst-union-f6.note: Quotes the 1606 and 1634 proclamations on the Union Flag and ships' flags; Treaty of Union 1707; Act of Union 1801 and the St Patrick's saltire.

nzhistory-flag-f6.title: The NZ flag (Flags of New Zealand, page 4)
nzhistory-flag-f6.publisher: NZ History, Ministry for Culture and Heritage
nzhistory-flag-f6.note: Colonial Naval Defence Act 1865: colonial-government ships to fly the Blue Ensign with the colony's badge; Union Jack remained the legal flag.

commonwealth-history-f6.title: Our history
commonwealth-history-f6.note: Modern Commonwealth dated to the London Declaration of 26 April 1949; no mention of a flag.

breschi-fiav-f6.title: Flags in Italy under Napoleon's rule (Breschi)
breschi-fiav-f6.publisher: FIAV, Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Vexillology (Stockholm 2003)
breschi-fiav-f6.note: Piedmont incorporated into France in 1801; in annexed Italian states the old flags were lowered and the French tricolour hoisted; Piedmontese Republic flag of 1796-1800.

normattiva-l2264-f6.title: Legge 24 dicembre 1925, n. 2264 (conversion of R.D.L. 24 September 1923, n. 2072, on the use of the national flag)
normattiva-l2264-f6.publisher: Presidenza del Consiglio dei Ministri, Normattiva
normattiva-l2264-f6.note: Title and Gazzetta Ufficiale details of the law (in force 29 Dec 1925, since repealed); the article text is not shown on the page.

difesa-tricolore-f6.title: Simboli del 2 giugno: il Tricolore
difesa-tricolore-f6.note: Only in 1925 were the national and State flag models fixed by law, the State flag adding the royal crown to the arms; a decree of 19 June 1946 set the new flag.

gu1944-313-f6.title: Gazzetta Ufficiale 21 Nov 1944, n. 84 (d.lgs.lgt. n. 313, removal of the fasces from the state arms)
gu1944-313-f6.note: Lieutenancy decree of October 1944 restoring the state arms to their form before the 1926-1929 decrees (fasces removed); concerns the arms and seals, not the flag.

snl-wales-f6.title: Wales’ flagg og våpen
snl-wales-f6.note: Gwynedd princes bore the four-lions arms; Glyndwr dragon banner from 1400; Henry Tudor 1485; Wales not represented in the Union Flag.

flaginst-wales-f6.title: Flag of Wales: a blood-red dragon on a field of green
flaginst-wales-f6.note: Dragon and Britons, Henry Tudor adding green and white after Bosworth, official flag in 1959; the 'since 830' claim is stated without a source.

adam-usk-f6.title: English Battles and Campaigns from The Chronicle of Adam of Usk
adam-usk-f6.publisher: De Re Militari (Society for Medieval Military History)
adam-usk-f6.note: Translated chronicle extract: Owain unfurled a golden dragon on a white field at Caernarfon on 2 November (1401).

nippon-hinomaru-f6.title: Origin of the Hinomaru (nippon.com)
nippon-hinomaru-f6.note: 701 sun flag at the New Year ceremony; a white flag with red disc said to appear in the Genpei War; government answer of 1999 that earlier use is recorded but origin unclear.

bunshun-hando-f6.title: Hando Kazutoshi on the Hinomaru (Bungeishunju Online)
bunshun-hando-f6.note: Popular essay: Hinomaru said to have become common in the Nanbokucho period (14th century), daimyo flags in the late 16th.

sla-holmes-203-f6.title: General William Holmes diary, 23 Aug 1914-22 Feb 1915, page 203
sla-holmes-203-f6.publisher: State Library of New South Wales
sla-holmes-203-f6.note: Holmes's telegram: troops took Nauru on 6 Nov 1914, "German Flag lowered, British Flag hoisted".

sla-holmes-192-f6.title: General William Holmes diary, 23 Aug 1914-22 Feb 1915, page 192
sla-holmes-192-f6.publisher: State Library of New South Wales
sla-holmes-192-f6.note: Gazette account in the diary: the British flag took the place of the German flag on the Government House flagstaff at Nauru; official hoisting that afternoon.

worldstatesmen-nauru-f6.title: Naoero (Nauru)
worldstatesmen-nauru-f6.note: Flag chronology: German Empire flag 1888-1914 (flag raising 2 Oct 1888), UK flag 1914-1920, Australian flag 1920-42 and 1945-68; no design details.

trove-register-1924-f6.title: The Empire Flags (The Register, Adelaide, 6 March 1924)
trove-register-1924-f6.note: Commonwealth circular on flag usage: Commonwealth Flag (Blue Ensign with stars) at Commonwealth buildings, State vessels fly the Blue Ensign with State badge; Nauru not mentioned.

trove-argus-1901-f6.title: The Australian Flag (The Argus, Melbourne, 4 September 1901)
trove-argus-1901-f6.note: Judges' letter on the federal flag competition refers to existing State flags with the Southern Cross (New Zealand, Victoria).

rmg-qing-ensign-f6.title: Imperial Chinese naval ensign (1866-1888)
rmg-qing-ensign-f6.note: Triangular yellow dragon flag announced 1866, adopted as state flag and naval ensign in 1872 (museum text).

devries-algeria-f6.title: Algeria Arms
devries-algeria-f6.publisher: Hubert de Vries, National Arms and Emblems Past and Present
devries-algeria-f6.note: Algerian flag chart c.1750: Ottoman merchant flag and a blue war ensign with an arm swinging a sword; all-red flag attributed to Tlemcen from 1488.

atenea-flag-f6.title: El triple camino de la bandera nacional (Atenea no. 10)
atenea-flag-f6.publisher: Atenea magazine (Antonio Manzano), hosted at aesvm.com
atenea-flag-f6.note: Red-yellow-red recruiting flags of Fernando VII volunteer battalions in the War of Independence; nothing on Joseph Bonaparte's flag.

ref-ge-dulcert-f7.title: Dulcerti Angelino
ref-ge-dulcert-f7.note: Describes red five-cross flags tied to the Georgian state on Dulcert's 1339 portolan chart.

ref-ge-heraldry-f7.title: The Story of Georgian Heraldry (T. Asatiani)
ref-ge-heraldry-f7.publisher: State Council of Heraldry at the Parliament of Georgia
ref-ge-heraldry-f7.note: 2023 official book: David IV coin with cross and four roundels resembling the five-cross flag; 17th-century arms of Kartli and Kakheti.

ws-ge-f7.title: Georgia (flags and chronology)
ws-ge-f7.note: Flag strip: black flag with white cross for 1762-1802; Russian white-blue-red flag listed for 1802-1918.

ws-kh-f7.title: Cambodia (flags and chronology)
ws-kh-f7.note: Flag strip with dates: Cambodian flag c.1863-1940, French flag 1887-1945/1948, Khmer Republic 1970-75, PRK 1979-89, State of Cambodia 1989-92.

ws-jm-f7.title: Jamaica (flags and chronology)
ws-jm-f7.note: Flag strip: British (Union) flag to 1875, then colonial Blue Ensigns 1875-1906, 1906-57, 1957-62.

ws-cg-f7.title: Congo (Brazzaville) (flags and chronology)
ws-cg-f7.note: Flag strip: French flag 1 Oct 1880 - 18 Aug 1959; People's Republic flag 31 Dec 1969 - 10 Jun 1991.

ws-lt-f7.title: Lithuania (flags and chronology)
ws-lt-f7.note: Flag strip: Russian flag 1795-1915; interwar Lithuanian flag listed 'semi-official' 18 Nov 1941 - 1 Aug 1944.

ws-np-f7.title: Nepal (flags and chronology)
ws-np-f7.note: Flag strip: separate Flag of the Kings and Rana prime ministers' flag, each a single pennant with a face, c.1847-1923.

ws-tt-f7.title: Trinidad and Tobago (flags and chronology)
ws-tt-f7.note: Flag strip: Union flag 18 Feb 1797 - 1 Jan 1889, then colonial flag 1889-1958.

ws-bs-f7.title: The Bahamas (flags and chronology)
ws-bs-f7.note: Flag strip: Union flag 1718-1869, pirate flag 1706-1718, badged colonial Blue Ensign from 1869.

ws-km-f7.title: Comoros (flags and chronology)
ws-km-f7.note: Flag strip: five Comorian flags 1963-2002 with dates (1975-78, 1978-92, 1992-96, 1996-2002).

ws-gt-f7.title: Guatemala (flags and chronology)
ws-gt-f7.note: Flag strip: Spanish war ensign of 1785 listed to 15 Sep 1821 for Guatemala.

ws-pw-f7.title: Palau (flags and chronology)
ws-pw-f7.note: Flag strip: German Empire flag 12 Oct 1899 - 8 Oct 1914.

ws-ws-f7.title: Samoa (flags and chronology)
ws-ws-f7.note: Flag strip: New Zealand flag 29 Aug 1914 - 25 Jan 1925, colonial ensign 1925-48, 1948 flag.

ws-sd-f7.title: Sudan (flags and chronology)
ws-sd-f7.note: Flag strip: Ottoman flag listed for 1820/22 - 26 Jan 1885.

ws-ad-f7.title: Andorra (flags and chronology)
ws-ad-f7.note: Flag strip: Catalan Quatre Barres to 1806, yellow-red 1806-1866, tricolour from 1866; no basis given.

ref-ad-langvalchs-f7.title: La bandera andorrana i l'escut d'armes (G. Lang-Valchs)
ref-ad-langvalchs-f7.publisher: Papers de recerca historica 8, Societat Andorrana de Ciencies (IEC repository)
ref-ad-langvalchs-f7.note: Scholarly article: no document mentions an Andorran flag before 1866; doubts a pre-1866 flag existed.

lrt-lt-f7.title: Valstybes veliava, herbas ir himnas: kaip jie tapo tokiais, kokie yra dabar
lrt-lt-f7.note: History of Lithuanian state symbols: Grand Duchy flags vanished after 1795; 19th-century rising flags and diaspora tricolours; no Russian-era flag named.

atlas-np-f7.title: Decoding the Unusual Shape of the Nepali Flag (D. Nosowitz)
atlas-np-f7.note: Says no historical reproductions of a recognisable double-pennant flag survive from the unification era; 1928 book shows faces and a green border.

ratopati-np-f7.title: How the national flag design came about (Ratopati, in Nepali)
ratopati-np-f7.note: Says Nepal had no standard flag before 1962: two triangles with moon and sun, some with faces, sun placed above or below.

wp-jm-list-f7.title: List of Jamaican flags
wp-jm-list-f7.note: Unsourced table: Castile arms 1510-16, Cross of Burgundy 1516-1655, flag of Great Britain 1655-1800, UK flag 1801-1875, badged Blue Ensign from 1875.

wp-occ-samoa-f7.title: Occupation of German Samoa
wp-occ-samoa-f7.note: Union Flag raised at the courthouse in Apia on 30 August 1914.

wp-occitan-f7.title: Occitan cross
wp-occitan-f7.note: Toulouse cross attested on 12th-13th-century seals and coins of the counts of Toulouse; Tripoli not mentioned.

wp-fr-congo-f7.title: French Congo
wp-fr-congo-f7.note: French Congo began as a protectorate at Brazzaville on 10 September 1880; infobox flag, no description.

libro-markham-f8.title: Book of knowledge of all the kingdoms, lands, and lordships that are in the world (Markham translation, 1912, of the Libro del conoscimiento)
libro-markham-f8.publisher: Hakluyt Society edition, via Internet Archive
libro-markham-f8.note: Full text of the 14th-century armorial travelogue in translation: gives the Emperor of Persia a yellow flag with a red square in the middle, the Emperor of Sara a white flag with a red sign, and Tunis a white flag with a black moon. The Wikipedia article on the work says the travelogue is largely imaginary.

wp-libro-f8.title: Book of Knowledge of All Kingdoms
wp-libro-f8.note: Describes the Libro as an anonymous 14th-century armorial manual in the form of an imaginary travelogue; used only for that caveat.

ws-libya-f8.title: Libya
ws-libya-f8.note: Dated flag sequences per region: Italy flag over Tripolitania 3 Oct 1911 - 23 Oct 1942, Cyrenaica 15 Oct 1912 - Feb 1941, Fezzan 15 Oct 1912 - 12 Jan 1943; United Kingdom flag over Tripolitania from 23 Oct 1942 and Cyrenaica Feb 1941 - 1947; French flag over Fezzan 12 Jan 1943 - 1951; Ottoman flag to 1911/12; a Karamanli local flag c.1727-1835.

awm-ensign-f8.title: Italian naval ensign taken from Tobruk: Corporal E S Grant, 2/4 Battalion, AIF
awm-ensign-f8.note: Museum record of an Italian naval ensign (green-white-red with the arms of Savoy in the white stripe) taken from the mast outside Navy House, Tobruk, on 22 January 1941.

dong-tang-f8.title: Study on the Military Flags of the Tang Dynasty (Dong Haipeng), Tang shi luncong 2023(2): 210-235 - abstract
dong-tang-f8.note: Abstract only: a study of Tang army flags from documents and murals finds six kinds of standard, gate flags, five-colour flags and others, mainly red and yellow with green, white, black and crimson; no state flag is discussed.

wubei-zhi-f8.title: Wubei zhi (Mao Yuanyi, 1621), vol. 32, page 8
wubei-zhi-f8.publisher: Source Library (Embassy of the Free Mind)
wubei-zhi-f8.note: Scan of a Ming military handbook page on the commander-in-chief signal flags of the five directions (machine translation, unreviewed); it concerns battlefield signalling, not a state flag.

aghn-sim-f8.title: Simbolos patrios de Nicaragua (from Briceño Tapia & Zúñiga Reyes, Antología escolar nicaragüense, 2019)
aghn-sim-f8.publisher: Academia de Geografía e Historia de Nicaragua
aghn-sim-f8.note: Chronology of Nicaraguan flags and arms: Mexican arms and flag ordered 1822-23; federal blue-and-white flag and arms from 1823; 1851 decree describing the arms (three volcanoes, rainbow, liberty cap); yellow-white-pearl flag of 21 April 1854; Walker flag 1856; blue-and-white and federal arms kept in 1858-1893; law of 4/5 September 1908.

ws-nic-f8.title: Nicaragua
ws-nic-f8.note: Flag sequence: Spanish ensign to 15 Sep 1821; Kingdom of Guatemala flag 15 Sep 1821 - 1 Feb 1822; federation flags 1823-1838; national flag 1838 - 21 Apr 1854; state flag 1854-1858; national flag 1858 - 1908. Notes the 1821 incorporation into Mexico as de jure ambiguous.

ws-pan-f8.title: Panama
ws-pan-f8.note: Lists the Spanish war ensign (1785-1931) for Panama up to 6 Oct 1821, then the Isthmus Province flag.

ws-lux-f8.title: Luxembourg
ws-lux-f8.note: Lists an Austrian flag for 8 May 1713 - 15 Dec 1792 and 28 Apr 1793 - 1 Oct 1795 (French flag between); no flag is listed for 1940-44; notes the 1940-44 area as attached/integrated but not formally annexed.

ws-les-f8.title: Lesotho
ws-les-f8.note: Lists the Flag of the United Kingdom for 12 Mar 1868 - 4 Oct 1966, a Resident Commissioner flag 1951-65 and an unofficial Basutoland flag 1951-66.

oz-les-f8.title: Flag history of Lesotho
oz-les-f8.note: Says the Basotho flew the Union Jack after the 1868 protectorate; describes the 1951 Resident Commissioner flag.

ws-sa-f8.title: Saudi Arabia
ws-sa-f8.note: Lists a "possible" Hejaz flag and a Nejd flag for 1926-1932 (images only) and the Saudi flag from 22 Sep 1932; does not describe the 1926-32 designs in text.

saudipedia-flag-f8.title: The Saudi National Flag
saudipedia-flag-f8.note: Saudi reference encyclopedia: after the annexation of the Hijaz (1926) the flag reverted to a rectangle with the Shahada in white in the middle, devoid of swords and other inscriptions; later it became the current form with a sword beneath.

majalla-flag-f8.title: Saudi Flag Day: A celebration of great significance
majalla-flag-f8.note: Magazine account of six flag stages: sword added 1921-26 (Kingdom of Najd); sword removed, green with white border and central Shahada, 1926-1932 (Najd and Hijaz); solid green with Shahada and white sword from 1932.

ws-arm-f8.title: Armenia
ws-arm-f8.note: Lists the Iravan khanate flag c.1827, then the Russian flag 22 Feb 1828 - 22 Apr 1918; no flag listed before c.1827.

ws-cyp-f8.title: Cyprus
ws-cyp-f8.note: Lists Kingdom of Cyprus flags to 1474/1489, then the Ottoman flag 1571 - 1914; no flag listed for 1489-1571.

oz-cyp-f8.title: Flags from Cyprus - a flag history
oz-cyp-f8.note: Popular flag history: says Venice formally annexed Cyprus in 1489 and shows the winged-lion flag of the Republic of Venice in the island sequence; says the Ottoman flag was initially green and became red in 1793.

ws-tun-f8.title: Tunisia
ws-tun-f8.note: Lists the Ottoman flag (de jure) to 12 May 1881 and a Tunisian flag c.1831 - 1 Jun 1959, then 1959-1999 and from 3 Jul 1999; nothing listed for 1574-1831.

const-tn-f8.title: Tunisia 2014 Constitution, Article 4 (National flag)
const-tn-f8.note: English text: "The flag of the Tunisian Republic is red and bears in its midst a white circle in which is inscribed a five-pointed star surrounded by a red crescent, as provided for by law."

arch-by-f8.title: Belarus - first country to use a national ornament in its flag (State Archives of Belarus news item)
arch-by-f8.note: Official archives page: in 1951 the BSSR Supreme Soviet commissioned a new flag; the Markevich "Rising Sun" towel pattern was found in pre-war archives; artist Mikhail Gusev prepared the design, approved in December 1951.

vex-bssr-f8.title: Flags of BSSR 1920-1990
vex-bssr-f8.publisher: Russian Centre of Vexillology and Heraldry (Vexillographia)
vex-bssr-f8.note: Gives BSSR flags of 1920, 1927 (constitution), 1937 and 25 Dec 1951 (green 1/3, red 2/3, ornament by Matrena Markevich, 1917; artist Mikhail Gusev); flag law of 27 March 1952; cites Basov and Kurkov.

ws-bel-f8.title: Belarus
ws-bel-f8.note: Lists BSSR flags only up to 1920-22 and then the USSR flag for 1922-1991; gives no separate BSSR flag for the later years.

milt-flags-f8.title: La evolución de las banderas (Antonio Manzano Lahoz), Militaria. Revista de Cultura Militar 9 (UCM, 1997)
milt-flags-f8.note: Scholarly survey of Spanish military flags: the red aspa (Burgundy saltire) carried on flags from the early 16th century; the red-yellow-red colours come from the 1785 warship flag, extended to coastal fortifications in 1793, and replaced the older army flags in 1843. Does not mention the colonies.

ws-cub-f8.title: Cuba
ws-cub-f8.note: Lists the Spanish war ensign (1785-1931) for Cuba up to 1 Jan 1899, the Cespedes rebellion flag from 1868.

oz-cub-f8.title: Flag history of Cuba
oz-cub-f8.note: Popular flag history: says the Cross of Burgundy was Spain's land battle flag to 1843 and flew in the colonisation of the Americas, and that the 1785 red-yellow-red war ensign also flew in Cuba until independence.

ws-sui-f8.title: Switzerland
ws-sui-f8.note: Lists a Confederation war flag c.1470 - 14 Apr 1798, the Helvetic Republic flag 1798 - 10 Mar 1803, then the Swiss flag from 1848; nothing listed for 1803-1848.

dhm-lux-f8.title: Besetzung von Luxemburg 1940 (LeMO Zeitstrahl)

ged-lux-f8.title: Luxemburg unter deutscher Besatzung 1940-45 (Paul Dostert), Gedenkstätten-Rundbrief 116
ged-lux-f8.note: Historian's article on the occupation: Germanisation, party bans, the 15 August 1940 red-lion badge protest; it does not mention the flag flown over the country.

awm-46th-f9.title: Regimental standard, 46th Turkish Infantry Regiment, captured near Damascus, 1918 (RELAWM04772)
awm-46th-f9.note: Museum record of an Ottoman regimental standard taken near Damascus on 2 Oct 1918: crimson silk with the toghra of Mehmed V in gold, Koran texts on the reverse, pole once topped by a crescent and star.

cetin-ottoman-f9.title: Osmanlı Bayraklarında Ay ve Ay Yıldız (Moon and Star in Ottoman Flags), E. Çetin
cetin-ottoman-f9.publisher: Türk Arkeoloji ve Etnografya Dergisi 83 (2021), via DergiPark
cetin-ottoman-f9.note: Peer-reviewed survey of 20 museum flags and 7 depictions, 16th-19th c.: many banners in use at once, Selânikî's list of sultanic banners under Süleyman, the Topkapı flag attributed to Selim I, crescent-and-star depictions before Selim III.

sfv-drapeaux160-f9.title: Syrie : un (ancien) drapeau panarabe chasse l'autre... (C. Capron), Drapeaux & Pavillons no. 160, 2024/2
sfv-drapeaux160-f9.note: French vexillological society journal: Gouraud's 1920 blue flag with white crescent and French canton, the 1922 federation flag green-white-green with French quarter, the 1930 constitution flag first hoisted at Aleppo 1 Jan 1932 and Damascus 11 June 1932, and the 1932 flag back in use after December 2024.

wp-eagle-saladin-f9.title: Eagle of Saladin
wp-eagle-saladin-f9.note: Says the eagle is commonly believed to be Saladin's emblem but that historical sources do not confirm it; cites Smith (1975) and Rabbat (1995).

pacheco-cr-f9.title: Costa Rica: sus Símbolos Nacionales (A. P. Pacheco Ureña, 2010)
pacheco-cr-f9.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura y Juventud, Centro de Investigación y Conservación del Patrimonio Cultural (Costa Rica)
pacheco-cr-f9.note: Official history of Costa Rica's flags: 1823 provincial flag (white, red six-pointed star), 1824 federal blue-white-blue with arms, Free State flag 1840-42, Morazán decree of 20 April 1842, decree of 29 Sept 1848; quotes decrees and Zelaya (1989).

ihcm-banderas-f9.title: Guía de la exposición "Banderas históricas de España" (IHCM)
ihcm-banderas-f9.publisher: Instituto de Historia y Cultura Militar, Ejército de Tierra (Spain)
ihcm-banderas-f9.note: Spanish Army chronology: Cross of Burgundy from 1506, first Spanish flag in America 1519, white flag with red Burgundy cross 1530, red-and-gold flag for the navy 1785, extended to coastal places 1793, cross dropped from regimental colours 1802, red-and-gold flag for the army 1843.

loc-dr-f9.title: Dominican Republic: country study (the first colony; Santana and Báez; annexation by Spain 1861-65)
loc-dr-f9.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division, via countrystudies.us
loc-dr-f9.note: Says France nominally held all Hispaniola after 1796-97 without an effective presence in the east, the French fled in July 1809 and Spanish rule was restored; no flags described.

aeiou-bindenschild-f9.title: Bindenschild (AEIOU Österreich-Lexikon)
aeiou-bindenschild-f9.note: Reference entry: the Bindenschild appears as the Austrian duke's arms first on Frederick II's seal of 30 Nov 1230 for Lilienfeld; striped shields in the Petrus de Ebulo chronicle of 1194/97; the red-white-red colours taken for the flag of the Republic in 1919.

xujing-gaoli-f9.title: Xuanhe fengshi Gaoli tujing, juan 14 "Qizhi" (flags), Xu Jing, 1123
xujing-gaoli-f9.publisher: Wikisource (text of the work by Xu Jing)
xujing-gaoli-f9.note: Song envoy's 1123 report on Goryeo: ceremonial flags in five colours; elephant (black), hawk (red), sea-horse (blue), phoenix (yellow) and Taibai (white) flags, plus plain five-direction flags.

tomalevski-krusevo-f9.title: 13-te dena na Krushevskata republika (G. Tomalevski), in Ilindensko-Preobrazhenskoto vastanie 1903-1968 (Sofia, 1968)
tomalevski-krusevo-f9.note: Participant-historian's narrative: Pitu Guli's unfurled flag with red folds, a crimson banner inscribed "Freedom or Death", "the flag of the republic" over the town; a Bulgarian-published text.

vexilolog-cz-f9.title: Česká a československá vlajka: Historické symboly Českých zemí
vexilolog-cz-f9.publisher: Vexilolog.net (Czech vexillology site), archived by the Internet Archive 2005
vexilolog-cz-f9.note: Silver double-tailed lion of the Czech kingdom appears at the latest early 13th c., probably from the mid-12th; oldest depiction an equestrian seal of 1213 (tails not visible); double tail reliably shown only on a seal of 1247.

iranica-abbasid-f9.title: ʿAbbasid caliphate (C. E. Bosworth), Encyclopaedia Iranica
iranica-abbasid-f9.note: Reference entry: Abu Moslem unfurled the ʿAbbasid black banners in Khorasan in 747; does not discuss the banner at Baghdad.

aramco-flags-f9.title: Flags of the Arab World, Aramco World, Feb 1978
aramco-flags-f9.note: Magazine overview: the Abbasids chose black because it was the colour of the Prophet's banner.

lyon-lionrampant-f9.title: The 'Lion Rampant' Flag (Court of the Lord Lyon), archived 2011
lyon-lionrampant-f9.publisher: Court of the Lord Lyon (Scotland), via the Internet Archive
lyon-lionrampant-f9.note: Official heraldic authority: gold with a red rampant lion and royal tressure is the Scottish royal banner, use restricted by the 1672 Act; no medieval history given.

eb1911-bh-f9.title: British Honduras, Encyclopaedia Britannica (11th ed., 1911)
eb1911-bh-f9.note: Says the settlement dates from 1638, the colonists elected their own magistrates until 1786, a superintendent served until 1862; no flag mentioned.

loc-mg-f9.title: Madagascar: country study (Colonial period)
loc-mg-f9.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division, via countrystudies.us
loc-mg-f9.note: Says that in 1896 France declared Madagascar a colony and exiled the queen; no flag described.

loc-tm-f9.title: Turkmenistan: country study (Russian conquest and Soviet period)
loc-tm-f9.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Federal Research Division, via countrystudies.us
loc-tm-f9.note: Says Russia took Gokdepe in 1881 and that the Trans-Caspian District became part of the Turkestan ASSR before the Turkmen SSR (Oct 1924); no flags described.

wikisource-tsfr-1918-f9.title: Regulation on the Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic, 30 April 1918
wikisource-tsfr-1918-f9.note: Founding regulation of the Turkestan republic; searched for flag, banner, arms and seal: none is prescribed.

era-1945.says: A royal decree of 19 February 1937, no. 93, fixed the colours of the flag of the Kingdom as red, white and blue; FOTW and Wikipedia both quote it that way. The Royal House says the colours were bright vermilion and cobalt blue.
era-1945.open: The sources disagree on the shade: FOTW dates 'bright vermilion and cobalt blue' to 1958, while the Royal House page gives that wording as the decree's own. The decree text itself has not been read. The hex swatches on this page are approximations, not a specification.

era-1940.says: FOTW, citing Poels in Vexilla Nostra 198 (1995), says the tricolour stayed the national flag but its use was restricted by the occupiers. NOS reports that from 1940 any demonstrative act for the House of Orange was punishable. Wikipedia (Reichskommissariat Niederlande): 1940-1945, the Reichskommissariat's infobox flag is the German Reich flag. Neerlandia (1957): during the occupation friends of the occupier often used the orange-white-blue as the Dutch flag, devaluing the old Prince's flag.
era-1940.open: The Reich flag as the occupier's flag and the tricolour remaining nominally the national flag under restriction are both stated, but no ordinance was found, so which restrictions fell on the tricolour and when is not established; no source supports a ban in 1943. The page's drawing is the occupier's flag.

era-1830.says: Flags of the World (Netherlands): the Dutch tricolour is the national flag and flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (1813-1940 and from 1945), adopted by Order in Council of 19 February 1937 with no earlier law. Wikipedia's Flag of the Netherlands: in 1813, when the Netherlands regained independence, the red-white-blue flag was flown with orange pennants, and the decree of 19 February 1937 states that the colours of the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands are red, white and blue. Wikipedia's United Kingdom of the Netherlands article dates the Belgian Revolution to 1830 and Dutch recognition of Belgium to 1839 without mentioning the flag.
era-1830.open: Neither source describes the flag at the 1830 secession or any change in it between 1830 and 1937; the card's statement of continuity rests on the kingdom-wide dating (1813-1940) in Flags of the World.

era-1813.says: Wikipedia reports 1813 newspapers describing red-white-blue flags with orange pennants and solid orange flags, and says the question of the national flag was left undecided; its statement that William preferred red-white-blue is marked 'citation needed' there. The Royal House confirms independence returned in 1813 but says nothing about the flag. FOTW: the red-white-blue tricolour was the flag of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (1813-1940 and 1945-now) and the southern Netherlands were united with it 1815-1830. Wikipedia (United Kingdom of the Netherlands): kingdom 1815-1839 with the Flag of the Netherlands as infobox flag. Neerlandia (1957): in 1813 both red-white-blue and orange-white-blue flew from the gables.
era-1813.open: The tricolour's use is attested by several sources, but the formal national status was undecided in 1813 per Wikipedia and no source describes an 1815 decree; FOTW notes there is no law before the 1937 decree. The page's 'treaty-built union of three countries' is not examined.

era-1810.says: The Royal House says the Netherlands was annexed by France in 1810 and the national flag was replaced by the French imperial standard. Wikipedia says the national flag was replaced by imperial emblems in 1810, without a citation there.
era-1810.open: Which French flag flew on Dutch buildings is not established; 'imperial standard' may not be the plain tricolour drawn here. Wikipedia's own Kingdom of Holland page gives the annexation date inconsistently.

era-1806.says: The tricolour continued under Louis Bonaparte. Wikipedia dates the flag without the Maiden to 5 June 1806 (no citation there), records naval crews rioting over the flag in August 1806 and a royal decree of 1 December 1807 affirming the Statenvlag for the navy (both citing de Jonge, 1831). FOTW says Louis proposed adding quartered arms to the navy's flag and withdrew the proposal when the navy would not accept it.
era-1806.open: The 5 June 1806 date has no primary source behind it in either reference. The motive this page used to state ('a deliberate choice to present continuity') had no source and was removed.

era-1795.says: Dirk Langendijk's design in the Rijksmuseum shows the Dutch Maiden and the Lion holding a spear topped with a liberty cap, in the upper-left corner of the existing flag, for the Batavian navy, effective 1 March 1796. FOTW, citing Wilson (1986, p. 60), puts the decree altering the navy's flags (not the merchant flags) on 14 February 1796; the States General publication Wikipedia cites carries the same date.
era-1795.open: The emblem was on the navy's flag only. Its removal in 1806 is Wikipedia's, without a citation. FOTW also describes a tricolour 'with a small white canton' (credited to Roy Stilling, 1996), which we have not reconciled with the Maiden emblem. This page used to describe a 'canton with a liberty cap used briefly 1795-96'; that is not what the sources show.

era-1650.says: Red replaced orange gradually. Wikipedia places the transition between about 1630 and 1660, with red appearing as early as 1596-97 (its infobox and text differ), the name Statenvlag in 1664 (de Jonge, 1833, p. 75) and the navy always flying it after 1663 (de Waard, 1900). The Royal House says red gradually replaced orange during the 17th century because orange is less visible at sea. Wikipedia gives the Republic's distance from the House of Orange as the reason.
era-1650.open: No decree for the change was found, so 'c. 1650' is the midpoint of a transition, not an event. This page used to say the flag flew over the VOC and WIC fleets, New Amsterdam and Batavia; no source for that was found and it was removed.

era-1581.says: Orange-white-blue is attested from the 1570s. Wikipedia cites Rey (1837) for use by the Prince of Orange then, Jacob Duym for officers' brassards at the siege of Leiden in 1574, an order of the Admiralty of Zeeland of 1587 for naval flags in these colours, and de Waard (1900) for the navy flying it from 1588 to 1630. The Royal House dates the first reference to 1572; FOTW says it was used from the second half of the 16th century and named for William of Orange.
era-1581.open: Wikipedia calls it uncertain whether the Sea Beggars carried the colours at Den Briel in 1572, so this page no longer says it flew from the Sea Beggars onward. The era starts at the Act of Abjuration (1581), not at the flag's first appearance. The earliest colour image, of 1575 in Jan van Hout's album, is on Wikipedia without a reference we could read.

era-1433.says: The Cross of Burgundy was the emblem of the Burgundian dukes (Hutchinson, 2007, as cited on Wikipedia). It is drawn here as the emblem, not as a flag of the northern provinces.
era-1433.open: Its use as a flag across the Habsburg Netherlands after 1477 is stated on Wikipedia without a citation and has not been confirmed.

era-1000.says: No single polity existed, so there is no flag to attest; the maroon field is a placeholder.

era-50bce.says: Tacitus (Histories 4.22) describes the force under Civilis following images of wild beasts brought out of woods and sacred groves, and names the Batavian elite and 'German allies'. He describes no flag.
era-50bce.open: This page used to say Tacitus records Batavian and Frisian war-standards; the passage names the Batavians and unnamed German allies, not the Frisii.

era-15.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Afghanistan): the Islamic Emirate flag, a white field with the black shahada, was reinstated on 15 August 2021 after the Taliban victory; a variant carries 'Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan' in Pashto beneath. FOTW: the Taliban flag flew at the Kunduz border crossing on 8 August 2021 with the shahada much larger than the 1996-2001 flag and an extra inscription below; its historical index lists 'Since August 2021' as a separate period.
era-15.open: Neither source says the 2021 flag is identical to the 1997-2001 one: FOTW notes a larger shahada and added inscription, so 'readopted unchanged' is not supported. Wikipedia's adoption dates are 27 October 1997 and 15 August 2021; FOTW's own date for the current flag (4 January 2004) is the tricolour's. The 15 August 2021 date is Wikipedia's; FOTW shows the flag in use from 8 August.
