era-1819.says: Wikipedia: Miranda's flag first raised 12 March 1806; Gran Colombia's Congress adopted the colours on 17 December 1819. FOTW: Angostura Congress of 15 February 1819 adopted Venezuela's flag; Cúcuta constitution promulgated 3 October 1821 ratified the symbols.
era-1819.open: Neither source says whether the flag had a star.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Colombia): the Gran Colombian colours were adopted by the Republic of New Granada on 9 May 1834, and it lists flags for New Granada in 1831-1834 and 1834-1858 (the Granadine Confederation to 1861); Wikipedia (Republic of New Granada) says the 1834 flag, the Gran Colombian colours in a different arrangement, was used until 26 November 1861. Flags of the World (citing a 1986 atlas): until 1834 the flag stayed horizontal yellow-blue-red, 3:2:1, and from 1834 had equal vertical stripes red-blue-yellow until 26 November 1861.
era-1830.open: The card's caption (equal horizontal yellow-blue-red bands) does not match either flag: the 1831-1834 flag had unequal horizontal bands and the 1834-1861 flag vertical stripes. Wikipedia gives the 1834 arrangement only as an image, and the vertical order rests on one FOTW contributor's citation.

era-1550.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy Flag): during the Spanish colonisation of the Americas the Cross of Burgundy served as the flag of the Viceroyalties of the New World (Bandera de Ultramar), and was used by Spain from 1506. Flags of the World (Colombia, historical flags): only Spanish flags were used in New Granada, with a contributor's note that the Cross of Burgundy was the official flag from 1506 until 1785 (other sources say later). Wikipedia (Viceroyalty of New Granada) shows a flag in its infobox.
era-1550.open: The Viceroyalty itself existed only in 1717-1723, 1739-1810 and 1816-1822 (Wikipedia, FOTW). Both sources say the Burgundian flag gave way to Charles III's red-yellow ensigns in the late 18th century, so the saltire fits the whole span only loosely. The viceregal seal's gold sun on the card is not described by any source read.

era-1450.says: Wikipedia (Muisca Confederation), a long article on their goldworking, the zipa's inauguration at Lake Guatavita and the 1537 Spanish conquest, describes no flag or banner. Neither Wikipedia's Flag of Colombia nor Flags of the World's Colombia pages mention the Muisca; FOTW's historical page says Spanish flags were used in New Granada.
era-1450.open: The card says openly that no flag is documented and shows a gold disc for Muisca goldwork. The sources read are silent on a Muisca banner, which does not show that none existed; an ethnohistorical source would be needed.

era-2001.says: Flags of the World: 'On 23 December 2001, a new Constitution was adopted, which prescribed a new flag, which was hoisted on 31 December 2001'; four horizontal stripes for the four islands (Ngazidja blue, Mwali yellow, Nzwani red, Maore white), a green triangle, and a crescent with four stars. Wikipedia: officially adopted on 23 December 2001, replacing the 1996 flag; stripes yellow, white, red, blue for Moheli, Mayotte, Anjouan and Grande Comore, crescent and four stars for the same islands, green for Islam.
era-2001.open: The sources differ slightly on the adoption route (FOTW: constitution of 23 December 2001, hoisted 31 December; Wikipedia: a referendum) and on the meaning of the green triangle (federation and possibly Islam in FOTW, Islam in Wikipedia); the caption's '2001-02' is not needed.

era-1975.says: Three publishers give the same sequence of flags. Flags of the World: Soilih's flag 12 November 1975 - 13 May 1978 (red over green); after the 1978 coup the flag was officially changed on 23 May 1978 to a green field with a crescent and four stars; the 7 June 1992 constitution had the crescent point upward. Wikipedia: Soilih's flag from 12 November 1975, all green from 1 October 1978, 1992 rotated crescent, 1996 Arabic inscription, a new flag in 2001. WorldStatesmen lists five dated Comorian flags: 1975-1978 (to 23 May 1978), 1978-1992 (24 May 1978 - 7 June 1992), 1992-1996, 1996-2002.
era-1975.open: The card's caption names the 1978-92 flag, which all three describe; the other flags in the 1975-2001 span (1975-78 red over green, 1992 and 1996 versions) are different designs. The 1978 date differs (FOTW 23 May, WorldStatesmen 24 May, Wikipedia 1 October); the 2001 end differs from WorldStatesmen's 2002.

era-1841.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Comoros) lists the flag of France as a former flag of the Comoros for 1887-1963 and the local flag of the State of the Comoros, designed by Suzanne Gauthier, for 1963-1975. Flags of the World (Comoros history) says Ngazidja became a French protectorate on 24 June 1886 and was annexed in 1911, and shows an 1889 coin with a French tricolour and 'R.F' beside the sultan's white flag; the Comoros were incorporated into Madagascar in 1896 and became a Territory on 1 January 1947.
era-1841.open: The French tricolour is attested as the flag of the Comoros only from about 1887 to 1963 (and beside the sultan's flag in 1889), not for 1841 (the Mayotte cession is not covered by any page read); the card's end date of 1975 ignores the 1963 local flag that both publishers record.

era-1970.says: Three publishers agree. Wikipedia: the People's Republic's flag (2 January 1970 to 9 June 1991) was a red field with the new arms in the top-left canton, a gold star with an overlapping hammer and hoe within a wreath of two palm branches, inspired by the Soviet flag. Flags of the World (People's Republic of Congo 1969-1991) agrees that a Soviet-based flag was adopted in December 1969 and that the original flag came back in 1991. WorldStatesmen lists the flag for 31 December 1969 - 10 June 1991, and its image shows a red field with a gold star over crossed hammer and hoe in a green palm wreath in the upper hoist.
era-1970.open: Adoption date differs by days (30 December 1969 FOTW, 31 December 1969 WorldStatesmen, 2 January 1970 Wikipedia). The card's drawing is a simplification of the canton emblem.

era-1959.says: Wikipedia: adopted 15 September 1959, a yellow diagonal band with a green upper and red lower triangle, unchanged at independence on 15 August 1960, the only Pan-Africanist flag with a diagonal. FOTW: adopted 18 August 1959 (Loi constitutionnelle no. 8), green, yellow and red diagonal, kept at independence 15 August 1960 and the fifth national flag to use those colours.
era-1959.open: Adoption day differs (15 September vs 18 August); the page's attribution of the colours to Ethiopia and Ghana is not in either source.

era-1880.says: WorldStatesmen lists the French flag for Congo (Brazzaville) from 1 October 1880 to 18 August 1959. FOTW (fr-colon): 'the common and specific flag for all of these possessions [French West and Equatorial Africa] was of course the French Tricolore'; a green-over-yellow Middle Congo flag with the tricolour in the canton was proposed but rejected. Wikipedia (French Equatorial Africa) runs the federation 1910-1958 with the French flag in its infobox, and Wikipedia (French Congo) dates the protectorate at Brazzaville to 10 September 1880; Wikipedia (Flag of the Republic of the Congo) says the French reportedly forbade the colony its own flag.
era-1880.open: The 1959 end is the card's and WorldStatesmen's; FOTW says only 'the 1880s' for the start. The rejected Middle Congo flag proposal is undated, and no source describes a flag flown over Brazzaville in the 1880-1910 years other than the general statements above.

era-1848.says: Wikipedia: current design 29 September 1848 at Pacífica Fernández's suggestion; 27 November 1906 state flag with arms; 21 October 1964 arms altered; colours linked to the ideals of 1848. FOTW: current design 1848; 27 November 1906; 21 October 1964 law.
era-1848.open: FOTW does not give the day or credit in 1848 beyond naming two candidates.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Central America» gives adoption in 1823, 2000 and relinquishment in 1839, within a year of this era's 1823 and 1838. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1838, and has 1823 next to a word about adopting.
era-1823.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1838.says: Costa Rica's Ministry of Culture (Pacheco Ureña, 2010): the federal flag (blue top and bottom, white centre, with the arms on the middle band; decreed with the state arms on 2 Nov 1824) stayed in use until 15 Nov 1838 while Costa Rica belonged to the federation; the 'Free State' flag of Braulio Carrillo, 21 April 1840 to 20 April 1842, was three horizontal bands, blue above and below and white in the middle bearing the Free State arms; Morazán's decree of 20 April 1842 restored the federal flag and arms, 'in use until 28 September 1848'. Wikipedia's list and Flags of the World show several variants for 1838-1848, including a white-blue-white version for 1840-42, a state flag with the shield and a civil flag without it (FOTW).
era-1838.open: The blue-white-blue stripe order for 1842-1848 is attested by an official publication, and that book also gives blue-white-blue for 1840-42 and the federal flag up to November 1838; Wikipedia and FOTW instead show white-blue-white for 1840-42, so the stripe order in those two years is contested. The state flags carried arms on the white band; the plain version drawn here matches only FOTW's civil form. The flag of 1838-1840 is not described by the Ministry book.

era-1821.says: Costa Rica's Ministry of Culture (Pacheco Ureña, 2010) says that after independence the provincial assembly, meeting on 10 May 1823, provisionally adopted the first flag, the 'Bandera Provincial Independiente', white with a six-pointed red star in the centre, sworn on 8 June 1823 and in force until 4 March 1824; it mentions annexation to Mexico only as one of the situations on which the provinces could not agree and describes no Mexican flag. Flags of the World describes a blue-yellow-blue flag of the independence fighters who opposed union with Mexico (September 1821 to May 1822 and again 10 May to 6 June 1823); Wikipedia's list shows flags for 1821-1823 without describing them.
era-1821.open: No source read shows the green-white-red Mexican Empire tricolour flown over Costa Rica. The two sources that describe a Costa Rican flag for these years disagree: the Ministry of Culture names a white flag with a red six-pointed star from May 1823 and nothing earlier, while FOTW gives a blue-yellow-blue flag from 1821. The first Costa Rican flag of 1821-22 is therefore not established by an official source.

era-1564.says: Wikipedia (list of historical flags of Costa Rica): the Cross of Burgundy for 1541-1821 and the 1785 Spanish flag for 1785-1821. FOTW (Burgundy Cross Flag): the red saltire on white was the Spanish ensign from 1506 and the Spanish military flag from the 16th century to 1843. U.S. National Park Service: carried by ships and flown over the fortresses of Spain's New World possessions until the red-and-gold ensign of 1785. The Spanish Army's Institute of History and Military Culture (guide to 'Historical flags of Spain') dates the Cross of Burgundy to 1506, the first Spanish flag in America to 1519, the white flag with the red cross to 1530, the red-and-gold navy flag to 1785 (coastal places 1793) and removal of the cross from regimental colours to 1802.
era-1564.open: Only Wikipedia's list ties the cross to Costa Rica, and it gives 1541 rather than 1564; FOTW, the Park Service and the Spanish Army guide describe Spanish use generally, so Costa Rica is covered by inference from the colonial flag, not by a local source (the Costa Rican Ministry of Culture's book on national symbols, read in full for this task, says nothing of colonial flags). From 1785 the red-and-gold flag replaced the cross at sea and in coastal places, but the Spanish Army guide has the cross on regimental colours until 1802, so the card's end date of 1821 is only loosely supported.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: tricolour adopted 3 December 1959 (law no. 59-240); kept in the constitution of 3 November 1960; Loubao's proposal to replace orange with red not adopted. FOTW: Law No. 240 of 3 December 1959; independence 7 August 1960; Constitution of 2000 Article 29 restates the design.
era-1960.open: Meanings differ: official (Delafosse) vs savanna/forest readings, which Wikipedia calls unofficial.

era-1958.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Cote d'Ivoire says Ivory Coast became an autonomous state in the French Community on 4 December 1958, which allowed a distinct flag in place of the French flag, and that the orange, white and green tricolour was adopted by law no. 59-240 on 3 December 1959. FOTW says the flag was initially prescribed by Law No. 240 of 3 December 1959 and that independence was proclaimed on 7 August 1960.
era-1958.open: The tricolour is documented from 3 December 1959; for December 1958 to December 1959 Wikipedia implies the French flag was still used, and neither source says what flew then, so the era's start does not match the flag's adoption.

era-1848.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) says the red-white-blue tricolour was first used as a flag in 1848, a drawing of a Slavic barricade in Vienna being the first documented use, and that a tricolour in the Varaždin Town Museum dates from 1848 or a few years later. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has the tricolour in use in 1848, without a citation.
era-1848.open: The pan-Slavic colours «formally adopted that same year at the Prague Slavic Congress», stated on this page, were not checked. FOTW says the tricolour was banned from 1852 (imperial decree of 10 September 1852) and reintroduced about 1860; the page's single year does not show that.

era-1868.says: FOTW says the state flag with the arms was in use from 1867 and adopted in 1868 under the Nagodba, with the Crown of St Stephen; an edict of 16 September 1876 specified the crown; a viceroy's decree of 21 November 1914 (no. 8378) named the red-white-blue tricolour the civil flag of Croatia and Slavonia; and the official arms stayed in use until 29 October 1918. Wikipedia says the civil flag was in use, citing Boršak-Marijanović (1996) for the arms variant.
era-1868.open: FOTW notes that Dalmatia was in the Austrian half and that unofficial variants existed (other crowns, none, other shields). The page's remark that the flag asserted «a unity the empire never actually granted» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia (Illyrian Provinces) dates the provinces to 1809-1814/1815 as a province of the First French Empire (Treaty of Schonbrunn, 14 October 1809), and shows a flag and a seal in its infobox without a description in the text. Flags of the World's Croatia and Slovenia pages and its Habsburg-era Croatia page (starting in 1848) do not mention the Illyrian Provinces or any flag for them. Second look: Hrvatska enciklopedija (Leksikografski zavod Miroslav Krleža) describes the Illyrian Provinces as Croatian and Slovene territory under French administration under Napoleon I, 1809-13, with a governor-general at Ljubljana and then Trieste; Britannica has them as part of Napoleon's French Empire from 1809 to 1814. Neither says anything about a flag.
era-1809.open: Two reference works confirm French rule of the provinces but neither describes a flag; that the French tricolour flew over them still rests on Wikipedia's infobox image alone. Hrvatska enciklopedija ends the French period in 1813 (as the page does) and Britannica in 1814.

era-1527.says: Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Croatia) says the checkerboard is first attested as a decorative symbol of the Kingdom of Croatia in 1495 and appears officially on the seal of the Cetingrad Charter of 1527, that historically the first field was mostly white, and that there was no official standard until the 19th century. Flags of the World (Croatia: coat of arms) dates the oldest preserved red-and-white arms to the Cetina seal of 1 January 1527, when the Croatian Parliament accepted the Habsburgs as kings, and says the order of squares did not matter in historical arms.
era-1527.open: Both sources show the checkerboard as arms or a seal device, not as a flag, and neither says it was flown on a red field; the card's flag (checkerboard on red, first square red, 13 red and 12 white) is a stand-in drawn to today's pattern. FOTW does not mention 1495.

era-1918.says: FOTW (credited to Željko Heimer) describes the flag as blue-white-red, used before the law and formally introduced with the 1921 constitution, and prescribed as the civil and state ensign by Article 2 of the 1922 law. Second look at the law itself (FOTW's English translation of Službene novine no. 89/22, 28 February 1922, passed by the Lawmaking Council on 28 December 1921): Article 1 gives the naval ensign as three equal horizontal fields blue-white-red with the crowned state arms; Article 2 gives the merchant ensign as three equal horizontal fields blue-white-red, ratio 1:1.5; later articles build the other ensigns on it. Wikipedia gives 1922 as the first official adoption and says the national flag and civil and state ensign of 1918-1943 was the blue-white-red tricolour, a variation of the Pan-Slavic flag of the 1848 Prague congress; it also says the Corfu Declaration let the Serbian, Croatian and Slovenian flags be displayed freely.
era-1918.open: The law read is a law on ensigns of vessels, so its text fixes the blue-white-red merchant and naval ensigns from 1922, not the flag on land or any flag before 1922; those points, and the 1918 start in Wikipedia's infobox against its text's 1922, rest on FOTW's and Wikipedia's statements. The page's earlier statement that the regional tricolours kept their own orderings is not in either source, and neither says the 1929 dictatorship's ban on them was enforced. Neither source says the ordering was chosen to follow Serbia's flag.

era-1929.says: FOTW says there was apparently no change in the flag law when the kingdom was proclaimed in 1929, and that the 1937 law did not change it. Wikipedia dates the renaming to 3 October 1929 and shows the same blue-white-red flag.
era-1929.open: FOTW adds that the 1929 dictatorship reportedly banned national tricolours such as the Croatian one in favour of the Yugoslav one, and that it is unclear whether this was enforced (Heimer, 2009). This page used to say Croatian politicians resisted through the 1930s; no source for that was found.

era-1939.says: FOTW says all sources seem to agree that the Croatian tricolour was used after 1939, that its use was governed by natural law and not by any written regulation, that a version with the coat of arms in the centre was reportedly for state use, and that the crownless arms seem not to have been official though crownless versions were used on flags. Wikipedia's «Flag of Croatia» has a similar flag without the crown above the checkerboard, uncited.
era-1939.open: No decree for the flag was found, which agrees with the page's «by custom». Wikipedia's Banovina article describes no flag and dates the Cvetković–Maček Agreement to 24 August 1939 and the Banovina's de jure existence to 1945.

era-1941.says: FOTW quotes the law-decree signed by Ante Pavelić on 28 April 1941 and published in Narodne novine no. 15 on 30 April: three horizontal fields red, white, blue, with the state arms (25 fields, the first white) in the middle of the white field and, on the red field near the hoist, a curl enclosing a white field with a dark blue letter U. Wikipedia describes the crown removed, a U added at the top left and the first field white, without a citation.
era-1941.open: The older red-white-blue civil flag stayed in use everywhere except on state or local administration buildings until further regulation (FOTW). The decree text was read only as quoted by FOTW.

era-1943.says: FOTW says the state was Democratic Federal Yugoslavia from 29 November 1943, that before 1946 the red star usually sat in the white field without a yellow edge, and dates the red-star flag to 1941 (July, Heimer; September, Smith 1975). Wikipedia describes the red star added to the white band and the ratio changed from 2:3 to 1:2, with a citation-needed tag.
era-1943.open: Wikipedia's account of this period has no citation. The page's phrase that communism was «laid directly over the old kingdom's flag» is interpretation and was not sourced.

era-1946.says: Second look at the primary text: Article 4 of the Constitution of the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia (31 January 1946) says the state flag consists of three colours, blue, white and red, laid horizontally in that order from the top, each a third of the width, ratio 1:2, with a red five-pointed star in the middle with a golden (yellow) edge, the star's centre at the intersection of the flag's diagonals and its upper point reaching halfway into the blue band. FOTW and Wikipedia both give 31 January 1946 for the yellow-edged red-star flag; FOTW credits Đorđe Andrejević-Kun with the design (Wikipedia has a citation-needed tag on this) and says the state was renamed the Socialist Federal Republic on 7 April 1963 with the flag unchanged.
era-1946.open: The 1946 start and the drawn layout are now fixed by the constitution's own text. Not established by anything read: the designer, the 1963 renaming leaving the flag unchanged (the 1963 text was not read), a Croatian republic-level variant, and the end date, which FOTW puts in spring 1991 (federation's name ending 15 January 1992) and Wikipedia's infobox at 27 April 1992 with a citation-needed tag.

era-1947.says: FOTW says the red-white-blue flag with a yellow-bordered red star was officially adopted on 18 January 1947 and officially abandoned on 25 June 1990, and quotes Article 7 of the 1974 constitution for a red five-pointed star in the centre. Wikipedia has the star with a yellow border replacing the arms in 1947, and the arms returning in May 1990.
era-1947.open: The end is June 1990 in FOTW and May 1990 in Wikipedia; this page says 1990. Wikipedia names no adopter for the 1947 flag.

era-1991.says: Flags of the World (Heimer, 2013) quotes Article 6 of the Republic's constitution, published in the Sluzbeni glasnik on 2 January 1992, prescribing the Serb tricolour, red, blue, white from top to bottom, and says the flag was never formally changed. Serbian Wikipedia (Zastava Republike Srpske Krajine) states the flag was the Serb tricolour in the order red, blue, white from top to bottom, used 1991-1995 under the constitution adopted on 19 December 1991. English Wikipedia lists the Republic's flag for 1991-1995 among the historical flags of the Serbs of Croatia and describes the Serb ethnic flag as a red, blue and white horizontal tricolour.
era-1991.open: The sources agree on the design but give different dates for the constitution (published 2 January 1992 on FOTW, adopted 19 December 1991 on Serbian Wikipedia). FOTW also reports a state version with the coat of arms on the blue band and war flags with swords, which the plain tricolour drawn here omits.

era-1420.says: Wikipedia (Venetian Dalmatia) says Venetian rule over the eastern Adriatic was consolidated in 1420, when Dalmatia was incorporated in the Stato da Mar, and lasted until 1797. Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Croatia) says that in Venetian Dalmatia the older leopard-heads arms attributed to Dalmatia were replaced by the Lion of Saint Mark. Wikipedia (Flag of Venice) gives the Lion of St Mark with an open book in peacetime and an upright sword in war, relinquished in 1797; Flags of the World (Serenissima) has the lion holding a book, the sword variant as the war flag, used until May 1797.
era-1420.open: The sources show the winged lion as the emblem that replaced Dalmatia's arms under Venice and as the Republic's own flag, but none says the lion banner was flown in Dalmatia or by its administration from 1420: Wikipedia's Venetian Dalmatia article does not mention the lion or a flag, and FOTW's Venice page does not mention Dalmatia. The page's carved lions on fortress walls are not covered.

era-1358.says: FOTW, quoting Josip Luetić (1967), says the 1272 Statutes made the flag official as «VIXILLUM S. BLASIJ» and that it flew on Dubrovnik ships until 27 December 1807, when General Lauriston ordered it replaced; a white flag inscribed Libertas is described as a secondary ensign. Wikipedia describes St Blaise's flag as white with gold edging, the patron saint of the Republic, and a surviving flag over 200 years old, citing Britannica.
era-1358.open: The end differs by a year: FOTW gives 27 December 1807 for the flag, this page and the era's title say 1808. FOTW says a Libertas flag on a Croatian stamp was never used in Dubrovnik. The page's statement that Libertas was among the earliest civic mottoes flown as a flag in Europe was not sourced.

era-925.says: Wikipedia's Coat of arms of Croatia describes the central Croatian shield as a golden six-pointed star (the morning star) over a silver crescent on blue, finds its oldest example on frizatik coins of Andrew II as Duke of Croatia, says it 'did not have any Croatian CoA state relevancy and significance in the medieval period' and calls it a common misconception that it is the first and oldest known Croatian arms, naming the three leopard heads instead.
era-925.open: An emblem, not a flag: the drawing shows the later star-and-crescent shield for reference only. Neither flag source describes any flag or banner for 925–1102, and the page does not date the Andrew II coins.

era-1902.says: Wikipedia: designed 1849 by López and Teurbe Tolón; first raised 19 May 1850; adopted 20 May 1902; decree 21 April 1906; meaning of the stripes. FOTW: López credited 1849; adopted 20 May 1902; official explanation of the stripes and triangle.
era-1902.open: Wikipedia's own references differ on the 1906 date.

era-1492.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-4000bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1868.says: Wikipedia: Guáimaro chose López's flag over Céspedes's Demajagua; April 1869 Congress designated it national. FOTW: Céspedes's flag is the official flag of Bayamo.
era-1868.open: FOTW gives no date for the Céspedes flag.

era-1898.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Cuba): the United States flag flew over Cuba from 1 January 1899 until independence on 20 May 1902. Wikipedia (Military Government of Cuba, 1898-1902): the infobox flag is the US flag. The Daily Concord Standard of 10 January 1899 prints a soldier's letter from Camp Columbia near Havana: American flags were raised over Morro Castle and Fort Cabanas and the flags of the two nations were exchanged at the salute.
era-1898.open: The 20 May 1902 end rests on Wikipedia alone; the newspaper is a soldier's letter in OCR text, not an official record. The card's 1898 start is the war, not the first raising of the flag on 1 January 1899.

era-1515.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Cuba) captions the Cross of Burgundy as a flag of Cuba for 1521-1843 and the Spanish red-yellow flag for 1843-1898; Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy) says the flag served in Spain's overseas empire after its 1506 introduction. The US National Park Service page calls it the Spanish Colonial Flag, carried by ships and flown over the fortresses guarding Spain's New World possessions, and says the red-and-gold striped flag replaced it as the naval ensign under Charles III in 1785. Second look: a UCM scholarly survey of Spanish military flags (Manzano Lahoz, Militaria 9, 1997) says the red aspa (Burgundy saltire) was carried on Spanish flags from the early 16th century, and that the red-yellow-red colours came from the 1785 warship flag, were extended to coastal fortifications in 1793 and replaced the army flags in 1843; World Statesmen lists the Spanish war ensign (1785-1931) for Cuba and OzOutback says the Cross of Burgundy was the land flag to 1843 and the 1785 ensign also flew in Cuba.
era-1515.open: The cross is shown as a Spanish flag in the colonial period by the NPS page, the UCM survey and Wikipedia's Cuba caption (1521-1843); no source describes how it was used in Cuba itself, and the survey does not mention colonies. The sources date it in Cuba 1521-1843 at most (ships and forts changed in 1785-1793) rather than 1515-1868, and the Spanish red-yellow flag runs from 1843.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: flag in use from 16 August 1960, designed by Ismet Guney (Turkish Cypriot), neutral design excluding blue, red, crosses and crescents (Article 4); copper map, two olive branches for peace; slight alteration 24 April 2006. FOTW: Constitution 6 April 1960 Article 4 'neutral design and colour'; adopted 16 August 1960; Guney designer; white = peace, copper map, green olive branches; 20 April 2006 ratio 3:5 to 2:3.
era-1960.open: Wikipedia and FOTW differ on the 2006 date (24 vs 20 April) and the colour specifications.

era-330.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1200bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1925.says: Flags of the World (British rule) says a Blue Ensign with a two-lion badge was used from 1922 (the CHC badge of 1881 having been kept on the Blue Ensign until then), a Cyprus Red Ensign was authorised in 1922, and Cyprus became a Crown Colony in 1925; a 1937 traveller describes the Cyprus Blue Ensign with two lions. Wikipedia (Flag of Cyprus) lists the last British-period flag as 1922-1960, and Wikipedia (British Cyprus) shows a flag of British Cyprus in its infobox with the Crown Colony proclaimed 1 May 1925.
era-1925.open: The flag dates from 1922, not 1925, which is only the Crown Colony date. The two-lion badge, not an island-arms disc, is the badge in the sources.

era-1878.says: Wikipedia (British Cyprus) pictures priests blessing the Union Jack raised at Nicosia in 1878; Cyprus was a British protectorate from 1878, annexed in 1914, nominally Ottoman until then. Flags of the World (British rule) records a Union Jack with the 'CHC' (Cyprus High Commissioner) badge for the High Commissioner from 1881, and a 1937 traveller's account of the Union Jack over police stations. Wikipedia (Flag of Cyprus) lists a first British-period flag for 1881-1922.
era-1878.open: The caption's 'before a colonial badge existed' is contradicted: a CHC badge on the Blue Ensign and High Commissioner's Union Jack was approved in 1881 and a two-lion badge in 1905. The Union Jack was not the only flag of the period, and the nominal Ottoman flag's use to 1914 is not described.

era-1571.says: Wikipedia (Ottoman Cyprus) shows the Ottoman crescent-and-star flag in its infobox, labelled 'after 1844'. Wikipedia (Flags of the Ottoman Empire) says a 1793 decree required Ottoman navy ships to fly a red flag with a white star and crescent, officially adopted as the national flag in 1844, and that the crescent and star came into use in the later 18th century. Flags of the World (Ottoman Empire) also gives 1793 for the red flag with white crescent and star and 1844 for the change to a five-pointed star, noting that its source offers no evidence for the dates. Second look: World Statesmen lists an Ottoman flag for Cyprus from 1571 to 1914 without describing it; OzOutback's popular history says the Ottoman flag was initially green and became red in 1793 with a white crescent and eight-pointed star.
era-1571.open: The red crescent-and-star flag is shown for roughly 1793/1844 to 1878 only. For 1571 to the 1790s the sources describe earlier and varying Ottoman flags (OzOutback says green; the card draws a red flag with one dark crescent, which none of the later sources confirm), and none describes a flag flown on Cyprus itself.

era-1489.says: Wikipedia (Venetian Cyprus) calls it a colony of the Republic of Venice, 1489-1571, with a coat of arms but no flag. Wikipedia (Flag of Venice) describes the Republic's flag as a gold Lion of St Mark on dark red, with the book in peacetime and a sword in war, and Flags of the World (Veneto) describes the winged lion flag of the old Republic, noting blue-field variants. Flags of the World's Kingdom of Cyprus page ends in 1489 without a Venetian-period flag. Second look: World Statesmen lists Kingdom of Cyprus flags to 1474/1489 and the Ottoman flag from 1571, with no flag for 1489-1571. OzOutback's popular history says Venice formally annexed Cyprus in 1489 and shows the Republic of Venice's winged-lion flag in the island's flag sequence.
era-1489.open: Only a popular history (OzOutback) presents the Lion of St Mark flag as the flag of Cyprus under Venice; World Statesmen lists none for the Venetian period and the academic and reference sources read describe it as the flag of Venice itself. No source read says the flag was flown on Cyprus.

era-1192.says: Flags of the World (Kingdom of Cyprus, 1192-1489) describes the first flag (1192-1268) as the banner of arms of Guy and Aimery of Lusignan: barry of eight argent and azure with a red lion rampant, armed, langued and crowned gold, the lion being an augmentation granted by Richard I. It says no contemporary depictions of this flag are known and that it is presented as a reconstruction from the arms' eventual standardised blazon, and it describes later flags (quartered Jerusalem and Lusignan from 1268, seen on a c.1385 portolan chart; a new fourth quarter from 1393). Wikipedia (House of Lusignan) agrees the lion was an augmentation granted by Richard I and shows a royal banner of Janus of Cyprus; Wikipedia (Flag of Cyprus) pictures a 15th-century Kingdom of Cyprus flag.
era-1192.open: No contemporary image of the 1192 banner is known, so the card's barry-and-lion flag is a reconstruction, as its caption says. The era runs to 1489 and the flags changed in 1268 and 1393; the card shows only the earliest.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia says the Czech Republic kept the flag in 1992–1993 and that Act No. 3/1993 defined it (the cited version dated 17 December 1992); FOTW (Heimer) says the blue-triangle flag was adopted on 17 December 1992. FOTW also quotes Joe McMillan that neither successor state was to use federal symbols, and Hugh Agnew that the Czech National Council ignored a federal resolution to that effect.
era-1993.open: FOTW's own sources disagree on whether the adoption was 1992 or 1993. This page used to say Slovakia's negotiators objected and that the asset-division law left the flag unsettled; neither source says that.

era-895.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-400bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1989.says: Wikipedia says the Czech part of the federation reverted to the red-and-white flag under Law 67/1990 of 13 March 1990; FOTW (Heimer) gives 13 March 1990 to 17 December 1992 for the official white-over-red flag and Jan Kravcík that it was never actually used, the Czechoslovak flag remaining the familiar one. FOTW gives 1 March 1990 as the approval date in another note.
era-1989.open: This page used to say the flag never changed through these years; the Czech lands had their own white-over-red flag in law.

era-1939.says: FOTW (Blanc, 1996) says the Protectorate flag had three horizontal stripes: white, red, blue. Wikipedia says Nazi authorities banned the wedge flag and that a horizontal white-red-blue tricolour replaced it during the war (citation needed).
era-1939.open: This page used to show a plain white-over-red bicolour; neither source supports it, and the drawing and swatches were corrected. Neither source says who ordered the change or on what date.

era-1918.says: FOTW (Sache) says the white-red flag was first officially hoisted in Washington on 18 October 1918, at Masaryk's residence, and was identical to Poland's. Wikipedia says the National Assembly approved the flag with a blue hoist triangle on 30 March 1920 to distinguish it from Poland's, after Jaroslav Kursa's 1919 proposal.
era-1918.open: Explanations of the blue differ (the third Slavic colour in use since 1848; a nod to Slovaks; Slovak mountains called «late mythology»). Wikipedia marks the rationale citation-needed. This page used to say the blue represented Slovakia and Ruthenia.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: the 1920-1939 flag (white over red with a blue wedge) was restored in 1945 (citation needed) and used until 1992; the Nazis banned it in 1939 and a white-red-blue horizontal tricolour was used in the war. Czech Television (CT24): the state flag lasted, apart from the war years, until the dissolution of the common state. FOTW: the Protectorate's flag was a white-red-blue triband, and the Czechoslovak coat of arms of 1920 stayed unchanged 1945-1960.
era-1945.open: No page read states in so many words the date or act of restoration in 1945; 'legal continuity' reasoning on the page is not covered.

era-1198.says: Wikipedia: Bohemia became a kingdom formally in 1198 under Premysl Ottokar I; from 1253 a two-tailed silver lion on red was the arms of the Kingdom of Bohemia, the oldest surviving full-colour depiction being in the 1310s Passional of Abbess Kunigunde; its Flag of Bohemia article says white-red banners were carried into battle by the Bohemian kings' armies, with a 13th-century description in Ottokar of Styria's rhymed chronicle. FOTW (Bohemia) gives the arms as a white double-tailed lion on red, the basis of the Bohemian white-over-red colours.
era-1198.open: Wikipedia dates the two-tailed lion as the kingdom's arms only from 1253 and says the kings used a black eagle on silver in the first half of the 13th century, so the lion cannot be carried back to 1198; FOTW names the arms without dates and says Bohemia had no flag of its own in the Habsburg period, only arms-derived colours. The legend of the second tail (Dalimil) is not evidence.

era-1158.says: Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Bohemia): a silver lion on red granted to Vladislaus II in the 12th century, at first with one tail, a second added later; the kings used a black eagle on silver in the first half of the 13th century. Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic): the traditional colours originated from an 1192 coat of arms showing a double-tailed lion. Vexilolog.net, a Czech vexillology site (archived 2005): the silver double-tailed lion appears as a symbol of the Czech kingdom at the latest at the start of the 13th century, probably from the mid-12th; its oldest depiction is an equestrian seal of 1213 on which the tails are not visible, and the double tail is reliably documented only by a seal of 1247.
era-1158.open: Wikipedia's accounts disagree with each other (one tail, two tails, an eagle) and the Czech site puts the oldest known depiction at 1213, so no dated banner or depiction of a lion for 1158-1198 was found, and the Wikipedia claim of an 1192 double-tailed lion is not supported by the Czech source. The page's 'first attested on a duke's own seal' is unsupported.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: the 1920 flag (approved 30 March 1920) was restored in 1945 and, as listed for 1945-1992, was one of only three socialist-country flags in Europe without the coat of arms at the centre; captions give separate naval ensigns and a war flag (1960-1990). FOTW records no emblem or flag change in the communist period and says the Czechoslovak flag remained in use; a 1968 idea of separate Czech symbols was dropped after the Warsaw Pact invasion.
era-1948.open: Neither source mentions a 1948 event, the comparison with Hungary or Poland, or a presidential flag in the communist period; Wikipedia gives no dates for this period.

era-1938.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic): the flag approved on 30 March 1920 has been in continuous use except during the German occupation (1939-45), and the 1920-1939 flag is labelled as the state flag of the republic. CT24: the flag lasted, apart from the war years, until the dissolution of the state. FOTW (Bohemia and Moravia 1939-1945): the Second Republic's loss of Sudetenland on 1 October 1938, Slovak and Subcarpathian autonomy on 6 and 8 October 1938 and the annexations of March 1939; the former Czechoslovak state flag was used in the first months of the Protectorate (FOTW, cz_bh).
era-1938.open: No source states the flag specifically for the Second Republic; the sources imply it by saying the 1920 flag was in use until 1939 and the war years were the exception (read as 1939-45). The page's wording about lost population and fortifications is not covered.

era-1526.says: FOTW (Bohemia): the Austrian crown lands had no flags in their own right but Landesfarben derived from their arms; Bohemia's were white over red from the silver double-tailed lion on red, and a white-over-red flag was used in Bohemia from the 19th century to 1918 and became the first flag of Czechoslovakia. Wikipedia (Flag of Bohemia): white-red banners derived from the royal arms were carried into battle by the Bohemian kings' armies; the heraldic flag is described and drawn in Koebel's 1545 work; the Czech national movement adopted the colours in the 19th century. Wikipedia (Flag of the Czech Republic): the traditional colours derive from an 1192 coat of arms.
era-1526.open: A two-tailed lion banner as a distinct flag of the crown land is not documented for the Habsburg centuries beyond Koebel's 1545 description; the sources describe Landesfarben and, in the 19th century, a white-red bicolour rather than the lion banner drawn on the page.

era-1814.says: Wikipedia says a regulation of 1748 (11 June in its infobox, 11 July in the Danish title it cites) set the merchant-ship flag and its proportions, that private use was outlawed by a circular of 7 January 1834 and the ban repealed by a regulation of 7 July 1854 (the swallow-tailed Splitflag excluded), and that the Guinness record for the oldest continuously used national flag dates from 1625. FOTW says regulations of 11 July 1748 set the proportions (28:34 per Southworth) and that regulations of 1 May 1893 allowed up to 28:37.
era-1814.open: The 1748 date differs by a month between Wikipedia's own sources. The German occupation of 1940–45 is not covered by either source.

era-965.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1219.says: Wikipedia says the legend ties the flag to the Battle of Lyndanisse on 15 June 1219 (earliest source: Christiern Pedersen's Danske Krønike of the 1520s) and that the Gelre Armorial of about 1340–1370 is the earliest known undisputed colour rendering. FOTW (Andersen) dates the Gelre Armorial's red banner with a white cross to about 1370–1386, and says a Danish text of 1478 is the first to use the name Dannebrog, a Dutch text having used it about 100 years earlier.
era-1219.open: Neither source supports a flag of 1219 itself. This page used to say the design was unchanged for eight centuries.

era-1397.says: Flags of the World (Kalmar Union Flag): the only evidence is two letters of 1430 in which Erik of Pomerania orders the priests of Vadstena and Kalmar to wear the 'banner of the realms', described as a red cross on top of a yellow field; there is no pictorial evidence and no surviving flag, a museum flag with a red Scandinavian cross on yellow is a recreation, and contributors dispute whether some references mean the union banner or the Dannebrog. Wikipedia (Kalmar Union) pictures the 'unofficial flag of the Kalmar Union as described by Erik of Pomerania' and a 1427 captured ship flag showing the arms of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Pomerania; Wikipedia (Dannebrog) shows a small Dannebrog on Eric's 1398 seal.
era-1397.open: The design rests on one disputed 1430 description (FOTW); Wikipedia's text gives no design. Neither source describes three crowns, and the union's end date varies between sources (1521 FOTW, 1523 here).

era-1523.says: Wikipedia (Denmark-Norway): the infobox flag is the Dannebrog, 'official flag since 1625', for the union of 1537-1814, and Norway had its own royal standard until 1748, after which the Dannebrog became the only official merchant flag. Wikipedia (Dannebrog): the flag of the Kingdom of Denmark, with a regulation of 11 June 1748 defining its proportions. Wikipedia (Flag of Norway): from 1537 to 1814 Norway used the same flag as Denmark, though a red banner with the golden lion and silver halberd was shown as Norway's flag in 1669-70 and flew over Akershus until at least 1698. Flags of the World (Denmark) cites the 1748 decree on the flags of trade ships, with the Dannebrog's proportions of 28:34 from 1748.
era-1523.open: The two Wikipedia articles are not fully aligned (a shared Dannebrog against a separate Norwegian lion banner), and Flags of the World's Denmark page covers only the 1748 decree for this period. The card's 'Norway had no flag of its own' is contradicted by the lion banner.

era-1977.says: Both sources give 1977, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 27 June 1977; Flags of the World dates it 27 June 1977.
era-1977.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1896-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1896.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Djibouti): the flag of France was used between 1896 and 1977 and the only ensign used was the tricolour. Wikipedia (French Somaliland, 1884-1967 in the infobox and formally established 1896 in the text) and (French Territory of the Afars and the Issas, 5 July 1967 to 27 June 1977): both infobox flags are the French tricolour, with a governor's flag also shown and no local flag. FOTW (dj-fs): the colony was formed in 1896; prior to independence the French tricolore 'would have been used' as the national flag; the colonial governor's flag was a blue square with the tricolour in the canton and a swallow tail; independence flag adopted 27 June 1977 (dj.html).
era-1896.open: FOTW's statement is hedged ('would have been used') and gives no dates; the start varies between 1884, 1894 (FOTW dj.html) and 1896. The 'T.F.A.I.' marking is not supported by any source.

era-1978.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives adoption on 3 November 1978. FOTW gives 'Flag adopted: 3 November 1978 (modified 1988)' and the coat of arms 21 July 1961 (the 1961 date belongs to the arms, not the flag), and quotes the description in Act No. 18 of 1978, the National Emblems of Dominica Act, gazetted 1 November 1978 and effective 3 November 1978; a Flag Bulletin report says a revised form was introduced on 3 November 1981. The Office of the President describes the flag as a red roundel with a Sisserou parrot on a twig within ten lime-green stars for the ten parishes, on a triple cross of yellow, black and white over forest green.
era-1978.open: The parrot and stars were modified in 1981, 1988 and 1990 per Wikipedia and FOTW, so the drawing is simplified; the government page does not give the Kalinago/soil/water meanings of the three bands stated on the page (it reads the cross as the Trinity).

era-1493.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-3100bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1783.says: Wikipedia's table: Union Jack 1763-78 and 1784-1801; UK flag 1801-75; Leeward Islands flags 1875-1940; Windward Islands flags 1940-58; a Dominica flag 1955-65 and another 1965-78. FOTW (Colonial Badges and Flags): Blue Ensign with the Leeward Islands' badge 1875-1940, none recorded 1940-55, the Dominica badge (a ship at the Cabrits on a shield) 1955-65, and the full 1961 arms 1965-78, all without a white disc; defaced Union Jacks for governors (full 1961 arms from 1967).
era-1783.open: A Dominica-badge Blue Ensign is documented only from 1955; before 1875 the sources show the Union Jack, and the page's 1783/1805 start dates are not supported. The 1961 arms are described but whether the badge on the page is the parrot is not stated.

era-1763.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Dominica) lists the French royal standard for 1715-1763 and 1778-1784 and the Union Jack for 1763-1778 and 1784-1801. Wikipedia (History of Dominica) says Dominica was ceded to Britain in 1763, recaptured by the French in 1778 and burned at Roseau in 1805; Wikipedia (Union Flag) dates the flag of Great Britain to 1707 and the current design to 1801. Flags of the World's Dominica pages begin in 1875. Second look: Article IX of the Treaty of Paris of 1763 (Avalon Project text) leaves Dominica, with St Vincent and Tobago, in full right to Great Britain.
era-1763.open: The Union Jack for 1763-1778 rests on Wikipedia alone. The French flag flew during 1778-1784, and the end dates of 1783 and 1805 on the card are not in the sources; nothing says which flag flew in 1805. The treaty confirms British possession from 1763 but says nothing of a flag; the Union Jack over Dominica rests on Wikipedia alone.

era-1865.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Dominican Republic): the flag was reintroduced with changes at the 1865 restoration, the coat of arms placed at the centre of the white cross and the fly-side blue and red quarters flipped. FOTW (Dominican Republic): quartered blue and red with a white cross, first and fourth fields blue, second and third red, with the national arms; origin from the Haitian flag, accepted on 6 November 1844. FOTW (history): the 1844 constitution describes a merchant flag of blue and 'rosados' quarters divided by a white cross.
era-1865.open: The two publishers date the present design differently (Wikipedia: changed in 1865; FOTW: 1844), and neither describes later refinements of the arms or proportions, so 'unchanged in core design since 1844' is not established. A 1913 decree mentioned by FOTW is not described.

era-600.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no woven banners; caciques used carved wooden/stone duhos, ceremonial regalia, and body paint as marks of authority».
era-600.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Dominican Republic): after Santana asked Isabella II to regain control, Spain annexed the territory in 1861 and the Dominican flag was replaced by the Spanish flag until 1865. FOTW: second Spanish rule 18 March 1861 to 11 July 1865, a contributor infers the Spanish flag was re-hoisted; it also shows a red-white-yellow flag and a swallow-tailed provincial flag of 1863. The Library of Congress study dates the annexation to 17 March 1861 and Spanish rule to 1865. The Spanish Army's Institute of History and Military Culture dates the red-and-gold flag to the navy from 1785 (coastal places from 1793) and to the army from 1843, so red-and-gold was Spain's flag in 1861.
era-1861.open: No page read describes the flag actually raised over Santo Domingo in 1861-1865; the red-yellow-red design is inferred from Wikipedia's 'the Spanish flag' together with the Spanish Army's dating of the red-and-gold flag to 1785/1843. FOTW lists other candidates (a red-white-yellow flag and a 1863 provincial flag), and the full Spanish flag carried the arms in the yellow band, omitted on the card.

era-1844.says: Wikipedia: Duarte's flag first hoisted 28 February 1844; colours blue, red, white with meanings; arms added in 1865. Flags of the World: colours derive from Haiti's flag; national flag adopted 6 November 1844.
era-1844.open: Dates differ (28 February vs 6 November 1844: hoisting versus adoption); Wikipedia's 1838 Trinitaria flag date conflicts with its own table; arms-at-crossing in 1844 not confirmed.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Dominican Republic): Haiti ruled the eastern part from 1822 to 1844 using the Haitian flag. Wikipedia (Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo): after Boyer's entry on 9 February 1822 the island was unified under the Haitian flag. FOTW (Haiti history): Petion made the blue-red flag horizontal in 1807, Boyer (from 8 October 1820) kept it, and the 1843 constitution confirmed the horizontal blue and red flag.
era-1822.open: No page gives a specific flag-raising in the eastern part; it follows from the unification and the Haitian flag being horizontal blue and red throughout. The short-lived Republic of Spanish Haiti (30 November 1821 to February 1822) had its own flag and is not covered by this card. The panel's arms are described only on Commons, not in the pages read.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo): the Peace of Basel (22 July 1795) ceded Spain's part of the island to France, but the occupation was delayed until January 1801 when Toussaint Louverture took possession for the French Republic; Spanish rule was restored in 1809. FOTW (Haiti history): Toussaint adopted the French tricolour in 1798 and occupied the Spanish part in January 1801. The Library of Congress country study says France nominally held the whole island after 1796-97 without an effective presence in the east, that the remaining French representatives fled in July 1809, and that Spanish rule was restored in 1809 and lasted until the colony declared itself 'Spanish Haiti' on 30 November 1821. Wikipedia (Flag of the Dominican Republic) gives a Spanish flag for 1809-1821.
era-1795.open: The sources tie a French tricolour to the Spanish part only for about 1801-1809, not to 1795-1801 (ceded on paper, Spanish in practice; the Library of Congress says France had no effective presence in the east) or to 1809-1821 (Spanish again). No page read states which flag flew over Santo Domingo in 1795-1801, and none describes the flag of the short-lived 'Spanish Haiti' of 1821. The card presents the French tricolour for the whole span.

era-1492.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Dominican Republic): lists the Cross of Burgundy as the flag of the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo for 1492-1795 and says Spanish military units used it in the 15th to 18th centuries. FOTW (Spain, 1506): the Burgundy cross was a Spanish ensign from 1506 to the 1670s and a jack until 1785, was carried 'if any was' by the conquistadors, and was never the official flag of the Spanish Empire but a military banner.
era-1492.open: FOTW does not mention Santo Domingo, dates its use from 1506 rather than 1492, and calls the cross a military banner, not a standard colonial and maritime flag; the tie to the colony itself rests on Wikipedia's table. The cross stands for the Spanish crown's colony, which had no flag of its own.

era-1997.says: Britannica (Whitney Smith) says Laurent Kabila ordered Lumumba's flag restored from 17 May 1997 (six stars, although the country then had eight provinces) and that the 1963-1966 flag again became official, in a lighter blue, when Joseph Kabila proclaimed the Third Republic on 18 February 2006. Article 1 of the constitution (a primary text) describes the present flag as sky-blue with a yellow star in the upper-left corner and a red band outlined in yellow on the bias. Wikipedia and FOTW give the same dates, and WorldStatesmen lists the 1997 flag for 17 May 1997-18 Feb 2006.
era-1997.open: The era title '1997-present' covers two flags: the blue flag with a large star and six small stars at the hoist (1997-2006), which the card draws, and the sky-blue flag with a red diagonal band (since 2006), which it does not. Both are attested. Wikipedia's explanations of the colours are its own reading and undated.

era-1971.says: Wikipedia: light green field with a yellow circle holding an arm with a red torch, the Popular Movement of the Revolution (MPR) emblem, part of Mobutu's re-Africanisation; in use until Mobutu's overthrow in the First Congo War. FOTW: adopted 19 November 1971 (Loi 71-007), light green field, yellow disc, right arm holding a torch with red flame; green for hope, the disc for natural resources, flames for martyrs.
era-1971.open: Neither source states the colour of the arm; the page's 'black arm' is unsupported.

era-1960.says: Both: the 1960-63 flag was the Free State design with six smaller stars added for the six provinces (Wikipedia; FOTW: six yellow stars in a vertical line on the hoist, a larger star at the centre, used until 1963). FOTW: the 1963 flag was adopted 30 June 1963, light blue with a red diagonal stripe edged yellow and a large yellow star in the canton; Wikipedia: 1963 flag with a smaller star in the top hoist corner and a red yellow-lined diagonal band, slightly modified in 1966 and changed in 1971.
era-1960.open: The red stripe's meaning as blood shed in the Congo Crisis is not stated: Wikipedia gives 'blood of the country's martyrs' for the current flag, and FOTW quotes a contributor's symbolism for the 1966-71 flag. FOTW's start date for the 1963 flag is inconsistent (1963 vs 1964).

era-1908.says: Britannica (Whitney Smith) says the flag of the Congo Free State, dating from 1877, was blue with a gold star, and that at independence on 30 June 1960 six yellow stars were added along the hoist. FOTW's pre-independence page says no change was made to the flag when the state became Belgian in 1908, and Wikipedia (Flag of the DR Congo) dates the single-star flag 1908-1960 with the six small stars added in 1960. WorldStatesmen lists one flag for the Free State and Belgian Congo, 21 Jun 1877-30 Jun 1960.
era-1908.open: Four publishers agree on the single-star flag and the 1960 date for the six stars, so the card's drawing (one large gold star) is supported. Britannica does not state in so many words that the flag was unchanged in 1908; FOTW does. Whether a separate Belgian colonial or governor's flag existed was not read.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia: the 1877 flag of Leopold II's International African Association, a yellow star on blue, continued as the Congo Free State flag. Flags of the World: the Association hoisted the flag since 1877 (per a 1914 booklet by Roland and Duchesne); the Free State 'adopted a blue flag with a golden star in its center', reputedly designed by H. M. Stanley (a claim Bakker says the sources do not confirm), and one commenter cites Pakenham that the design was borrowed from the old kingdom of Congo.
era-1885.open: Neither source calls it Leopold's personal flag; its design origin (Stanley, Kongo) is unverified.

era-1390.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Kongo) says the kingdom was founded around 1390, that Afonso I designed a coat of arms used by later kings until 1860, and shows a flag 'according to Cavazzi, 1650s' and a banner of Afonso I. The Villa Medici book (Sammy Baloji, introducing Afonso's 1514 letter held at the Torre do Tombo) says Manuel I of Portugal proposed that Afonso put the memory of his 1506 victory in his coat of arms, and that the design was brought to Kongo in 1512 by Simao da Silva and Alvaro Lopes, after which Afonso adopted it and distributed arms to his dignitaries. FOTW's Congo pages do not cover the kingdom. The Met Museum record of the arms returned HTTP 429 and was not read.
era-1390.open: The coat of arms is now documented by two publishers, but neither describes a flag: the Cavazzi flag and the banner of Afonso rest on Wikipedia alone, and no source read says what they looked like. The red field with a blue square drawn on the card matches none of them, and the two accounts disagree on who designed the arms (Afonso, or Portugal in 1512). Thornton's articles cited by Wikipedia and Cavazzi (1687) were not read.

era-1830.says: Wikipedia: 19 November 1830 provisional flag; 1835 yellow-blue-red first adopted by law; 1845 Marcista flag; 26 September 1860 restoration; 5 December 1900 arms decree. FOTW: 26 September 1860 decree; 5 December 1900 arms; yellow stripe double width.
era-1830.open: The sources differ on whether the Gran Colombia flag lasted until 1845 or 1830.

era-500.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Gran Colombia» gives adoption in 1821 and relinquishment in 1830, within a year of this era's 1822 and 1830. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1830, and has 1822 next to a word about adopting.
era-1822.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1809.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Quito: the 'Patriots of 10 de Agosto' (1809) adopted a red banner with the white diagonal cross of Saint Andrew (the Burgundy cross), the inverse of the Spanish military flag, which the Quito patriots used when they resisted the Spanish counterattack in 1812 and were captured at the Battle of Ibarra in December 1812; an old transcription error made it seem plain red. Wikipedia's Flag of Ecuador says the Quito rebels raised a reversed Cross of Burgundy on 10 August 1809 (elsewhere it says plain red). The Quito outlet Primicias likewise describes a red flag with a white saltire, used 1809-1812 and captured and destroyed after Ibarra. Wikipedia's Flag of Ecuador adds the Guayaquil flag of 9 October 1820 and the decree of 2 June 1822.
era-1809.open: The attestation covers the Quito junta's flag of 1809-1812; the later flags of 1820 and 1822 belong to Guayaquil, and the card's caption ('reconstructed device, no single fixed design') does not match the sources. Wikipedia's Ecuador article is inconsistent (plain red against reversed Cross of Burgundy), and Primicias is a newspaper, not a scholarly source; Flags of the World's Ecuador page does not cover 1809.

era-1563.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Ecuador: the emblems of the Spanish Empire flew over Quito after its founding, and the Cross of Burgundy flag of the Spanish colonial empire flew over Ecuador for many years (1534-1820). Flags of the World's Spain history pages: the Cross of Burgundy was used by Spain as a naval ensign between 1506 and 1701 and as a war flag on land up to 1843, 'if any was' carried by the conquistadors but never the official flag of the empire; Philip V (1701-46) dropped it from his arms. Wikipedia's Real Audiencia of Quito article dates the Audiencia from the royal decree of 1563 to 1822 and describes no flag of its own.
era-1563.open: None of the sources shows a flag of the Real Audiencia of Quito itself; the Cross of Burgundy is a Spanish crown military banner, which Flags of the World says was never the empire's official flag, and Spanish naval and royal flags changed in 1701 and 1785. The 1563-1809 span is not documented for Quito beyond Wikipedia's general statement.

era-1984.says: Wikipedia: Free Officers introduced the red-white-black flag with the Eagle of Saladin in 1952; current flag since 4 October 1984. FOTW: flag and coat of arms dated 4 October 1984; 1985 laws cited by a comment.
era-1984.open: The sources differ by a year on the laws (1984 vs 1985).

era-642.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: UAR 1958–71 with two green stars; Federation of Arab Republics 1972–84 with a golden Hawk of Quraish, kept until 1984. FOTW: 1958 Presidential Decree, flag red, white with two green stars, black; 1972 law amended, stars replaced with a golden hawk.
era-1953.open: FOTW notes its source list omits the 1952–58 flag.

era-1922.says: Wikipedia: after 1922 recognition King Fuad I adopted a green flag with a white crescent and three stars. FOTW: Royal Decree of 1923 set the first national flag of modern Egypt, green with a white crescent and three stars.
era-1922.open: The year differs (1922 vs 1923); star meanings are not covered.

era-1805.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Egypt says the Muhammad Ali dynasty used a red flag with three stars and crescents, deliberately similar to the Ottoman flag, which Egypt kept after Ottoman sovereignty ended in 1914, and shows variants for 1867-1881 and later. FOTW's Egypt-in-the-Ottoman-Empire page quotes Whitney Smith that Muhammad Ali set three white crescents and three stars on a red field, which became the first real Egyptian national flag, and says it was the khedive's personal standard; a photograph of a flag in the Cairo Military Museum is posted for the 1867-1881 type.
era-1805.open: Both texts describe three crescents with three stars; the card draws one large crescent holding three stars, as on the Commons file, so the details of the design differ from the texts. FOTW and others disagree on how widely the flag was used beyond the khedive's own standard, and the dates of formal adoption are not given in either.

era-1517.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Egypt captions a red flag with white crescent and star as the Egyptian Eyalet's flag in 1793-1844; Wikipedia's Ottoman flag article and FOTW's Ottoman page date that red flag to 1793 (navy decree) and 1844. FOTW's Egypt-in-the-Ottoman-Empire page shows a green-yellow-green 'Mamelik' flag in a 1711 Dutch chart. A peer-reviewed article on Ottoman flags (Cetin 2021) says the sultan's banners (saltanat sancaklari) came in several colours (the chronicler Selaniki lists white, red, green, green-and-red and mixed yellow-and-red ones), describes Selim I's banner (TSM 824) as indigo silk with three gold crescents, and says official crescent-and-star use is generally dated after Selim III; it says nothing specific about Egypt.
era-1517.open: A red flag with crescent and star is documented for Egypt only from 1793, the last twelve years of a 1517-1805 era; for 1517-1793 the sources show other Ottoman banners and the 1711 chart's green-yellow-green flag, none of which is the card's flag.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: 17 May 1912 adopted; hoisted 15 September 1912; replaced the 1865 flag because it resembled the US flag; 14 September 1972 Law of National Symbols. FOTW: 17 May 1912; Decree 115 of 14 September 1972, flag confirmed 27 September; arms adopted 27 December 1972.

era-1200.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1841.says: Wikipedia: 20 February 1822 Arce's blue-white-blue used until 1865; 1865 flag of nine stripes and nine stars, approved 28 April 1865; fourteen stars from 1875 to 1912. FOTW: 28 April 1865 decree replaced the federation-style flag with a nine-star red canton version; stars grew to 14 by 1912.
era-1841.open: The page's 1841–1912 plain flag claim is contradicted.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia: 20 February 1822 blue-white-blue by Arce. FOTW: 21 August 1823 decree of the same flag by the federation; 1822 militia chose the colours.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mexico) and Flags of the World describe the empire's flag as a green, white and red tricolour with a crowned eagle. Wikipedia (First Mexican Empire) says the Central American lands were annexed soon after the empire's establishment, and Wikipedia (History of El Salvador) lists Mexican rule 1822-1823. Britannica says Central America's independence of 15 September 1821 was reasserted in 1823 after two years of Mexican rule, and that Arce's blue-white-blue flag was blessed in San Salvador on 20 February 1822. WorldStatesmen says the province of San Salvador repudiated incorporation into Mexico on 11 January 1822, dates its incorporation into Mexico to 10 February 1823 and Central American independence to 1 July 1823, and lists a provincial flag for 1821-22 and a Salvador civil flag for 1823, with no Mexican flag.
era-1821.open: No source read says the imperial tricolour was flown in El Salvador; the sources show the province resisting under its own flag in 1822, and WorldStatesmen puts actual incorporation at only 10 February-1 July 1823. The Mexican flag for the whole of 1821-1823 is therefore a stand-in.

era-1525.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy) says that during the Spanish colonisation of the Americas the Cross of Burgundy, a red saltire raguly on white, served as the flag of the Viceroyalties of the New World and as a recurrent symbol of the Spanish armed forces. Flags of the World (Spain, historical flags 1506-1700) calls it the Spanish naval ensign from 1506 to 1701 and a war flag on land to 1843, and lists an ensign for Spanish galleons in American waters; Flags of the World (Spain) also says it is the flag, if any, carried by the conquistadors. Wikipedia (History of El Salvador) dates Spanish colonial rule 1525-1821 and places the territory in the Viceroyalty of New Spain.
era-1525.open: The cross is documented as a Spanish military and naval banner used across the Americas, not as a flag of El Salvador or the Captaincy General of Guatemala by name, and neither El Salvador flag page describes a flag before 1822. The card's start year of 1525 is the date of the conquest, not of a flag.

era-1968.says: Wikipedia and Flags of the World both say the flag was raised at independence from Spain on 12 October 1968: a green-white-red tricolour with a blue triangle at the hoist and the coat of arms (a silk-cotton tree under six stars) on the white band. Both say the arms on the flag were changed under Francisco Macias Nguema (Wikipedia: 1978 to 21 August 1979; FOTW: 1972-79) and the 1968 arms restored in August 1979.
era-1968.open: Wikipedia says the coat of arms was added to the flag sometime after independence, while FOTW says the flag with arms was adopted at independence; the dates of the Nguema-era change differ (1978 vs 1972). The 1979 date in both sources is the restoration, not the adoption; the colour symbolism on this page was not compared.

era-1471-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1778.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Equatorial Guinea): the red-yellow-red Spanish flag is captioned 'flag used in Equatorial Guinea during Spanish colonisation (1785-1931)'. Wikipedia (Spanish Guinea): Spanish control from the Treaty of El Pardo (1778) to independence on 12 October 1968. FOTW (Spanish colonies in the Gulf of Guinea): no flag existed for any Spanish colony in the area, only maritime registration flags and a standard for the Governor General (1945-1968).
era-1778.open: The colony had no flag of its own (FOTW), and the Spanish flag is dated by Wikipedia's caption only for 1785-1931; Spain's pre-1785 ensign, the Second Republic tricolour and the Franco-era arms of 1938-1968 are not described in the pages read.

era-1471.says: FOTW (Spanish colonies in the Gulf of Guinea): Fernando Po and Annobón colonised by Portugal in 1474, kept until 1778 and ceded to Spain at El Pardo. Wikipedia (Spanish Guinea) places the Treaty of El Pardo (1778). A heraldry-history page (Hubert Herald) also gives Portuguese colonisation in 1474 and the 1778 cession (and a Dutch West India Company attempt on Bioko in 1641, expelled in 1648). Wikipedia (Flag of Portugal): the royal banner of arms served as the national flag until the 19th century.
era-1471.open: Three publishers support Portuguese control of the islands to 1778 (from 1474, not 1471), but no page read describes a flag flown over Bioko or Annobón; the royal banner of arms is Wikipedia's account of the Portuguese national flag, not a flag shown on the islands.

era-1993.says: Wikipedia: after independence the flag was modified and first hoisted officially on 24 May 1993, the gold olive wreath (14 leaves each side, from the 1952 flag) replacing the gold star of the EPLF flag in the red triangle; the wreath was standardised at 30 leaves and the ratio changed from 2:3 to 1:2 on 5 December 1995. FOTW: the flag has a red triangle at the hoist with a yellow wreath, green over blue in the fly; flag adopted 5 December 1995, coat of arms adopted 24 May 1993; the EPLF flag it derives from had a red triangle and a yellow star.
era-1993.open: The page's date of 'adopted in 1995' is for the standard version; the 1993 version (2:3, 14 leaves) is documented by Wikipedia only. The UN-emblem reading of the wreath is a hearsay remark on FOTW, which says no official meaning is recorded; FOTW and Wikipedia agree green is agriculture, red the independence struggle, blue the sea.

era-1890-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1952.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Eritrea): Eritreans settled on a blue flag with olive branches in 1952 (federation, 15 September 1952); Haile Selassie banned it before annexing Eritrea in 1962, and it continued as the 'flag of liberation' of the ELF; Wikipedia's historical flags show it for 1952-1962. Flags of the World (Eritrea 1952): a light blue flag with a green wreath, adopted 1952, used until absorbed into Ethiopia (1959 per The Flag Bulletin) and continuing as a flag of liberation to 1993. World Statesmen dates the Eritrean flag 15 Sep 1952 - 23 Dec 1958 and Ethiopia's flag from 15 Sep 1952 to 24 May 1993. Flags of the World (Imperial Ethiopia; 1987-91): the Lion of Judah version was the state flag and the plain green-yellow-red tricolour the national flag; the Derg continued with the plain tricolour.
era-1952.open: The end date of the blue flag differs (1958/59 in World Statesmen and FOTW, 1962 in Wikipedia). The card shows the Eritrean blue flag; the Ethiopian tricolour (with or without the lion) is the other flag in force in 1952-1993, and the EPLF flag of 1991-93 is not shown.

era-1941.says: World Statesmen dates the flag of the United Kingdom in Eritrea from 5 May 1941 to 15 Sep 1952, and lists British administration from 19 May 1941 to 15 Sep 1952. Wikipedia (List of Eritrean flags) lists the Union Flag for 1941-1952, and Wikipedia (British Military Administration (Eritrea)) dates the administration 25 February 1941 to 15 September 1952 with a flag in its infobox. Flags of the World (Eritrea) says the British took over after the Battle of Keren in 1941 and administered the territory under a UN mandate until 1951.
era-1941.open: No source read mentions 'B.M.A.' lettering on the flag, and neither publisher describes a distinct Eritrean flag for the period; the end date varies between 1951 (FOTW) and 1952 (Wikipedia, World Statesmen).

era-1890.says: Wikipedia (Italian Eritrea) shows the Italian crowned tricolour as the colony's flag, 1882-1936; Wikipedia (List of Eritrean flags) lists the Flag of the Kingdom of Italy for 1882-1941 as a vertical green-white-red tricolour with the Savoy shield and royal crown. World Statesmen dates the Kingdom of Italy flag in Eritrea from 5 Jul 1882 to 5 May 1941. Flags of the World (Eritrea) says Eritrea became an Italian colony on 1 January 1890 and a province of Italian East Africa in 1936.
era-1890.open: No source read describes a gold colonial badge on the white field; the card's disc is an invention, and the flag in the sources carries the crowned Savoy shield. The sources date the Italian flag from 1882, earlier than the card's 1890 start.

era-1991.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1918, before this era begins in 1991, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 21 November 1918; Flags of the World dates it 21 November 1918.
era-1991.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.
