era-1561-1.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Courland): the state flag of the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia (1561-1795) was a 1:2 flag divided red over white, with a civil ensign carrying a red-and-white chequered hoist square; under Duke Jacob (1642-82) the colonial naval ensign was raspberry red with a crab (a black-eagle variant also existed). FOTW (Courland): Norie & Hobbs (1848) list 'Courland: Red over White', Bellin's 1756 chart shows 'Pavil. de Curlande' as a red and white flag of two equal stripes, and Dzirkalis (1936) is cited for state, merchant and naval flags.
era-1561-1.open: Neither source mentions a stag or a dark red field; the caption's 'dark red field with the duchy's stag emblem' is not supported, and the drawing now follows the red-over-white state flag. FOTW and Wikipedia differ on which red-over-white flag was 'state' and which 'merchant' (FOTW's Steenbergen note calls it merchant). The 1561 and 1795 dates are Wikipedia's.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: the final Soviet Latvian flag was adopted in 1953 and includes blue wavy bands at the bottom; during Soviet rule the national flag was unusable and its display treated as a crime.
era-1953.open: Neither source mentions a star or white in the bands.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: the first Soviet Latvian flag was red with a gold hammer and sickle and 'LPSR' above them.
era-1944.open: The page's claim of a star is not in the source; the dates of use are not given.

era-1941.says: Wikipedia (Generalbezirk Lettland) and Wikipedia (Reichskommissariat Ostland) show the flag of Nazi Germany in their infoboxes; Wikipedia (Flag of Latvia) says the red-white-red flag was unusable 1940-41 and 1944-91 'and briefly during occupation by Nazi Germany'. Wikipedia (German occupation of Latvia during World War II) was also read for any flag provision and gives none in its text. FOTW's Latvia pages are silent on 1941-44.
era-1941.open: The German flag as the occupation authority's flag rests on Wikipedia infoboxes alone (one publisher). The sources do not say what the occupation administration permitted for Latvian use; 'briefly' is undated. Latvian-language articles (lvportals.lv, visc.gov.lv, vestnesis.lv) timed out and were not read, so no archive or Latvian reference could be checked.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia: the first Soviet Latvian flag was red with a gold hammer and sickle and 'LPSR' above them; Soviet rule 1940–41 made the national flag unusable.
era-1940.open: The sources read give no date of adoption in 1940.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: c. 1279 the Rhymed Chronicle of Livonia has Latgalian tribes from Cēsis under a 'red flag with a white stripe'; a design by Ansis Cīrulis was accepted in May 1917; the Constitutional Assembly affirmed the red-white-red flag on 15 June 1921. FOTW: Republic proclaimed 18 November 1918; the flag was used 1921–39.
era-1918.open: FOTW does not cover the chronicle or 1921 law; 'oldest flag in the world' was dropped as unsourced.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Russia): the white-blue-red tricolour was the civil ensign from 1705 and continued as such under the Empire; the black-yellow-white tricolour was declared the national flag in 1858 and the white-blue-red replaced it as the sole national flag in 1896. FOTW (Imperial Russia: Civil Flags 1721-1917): lists the white-blue-red as the Russian civil/merchant flag (1696-1917), with the black-orange-white flag of 1858 and the tricolour as an alternate civil flag, and FOTW's Russia page notes land recognition on 7 May 1883. Wikipedia (Flag of Courland): the Courland Governorate (1795-1918) had its own green-blue-white flag.
era-1795.open: The tricolour is the Russian Empire's civil ensign throughout and its sole national flag only from 1896 (the national flag 1858-1896 was black-yellow-white). The sources give the Courland Governorate its own flag and none for the Livland Governorate, so this is the empire's flag over the provinces, not a provincial flag.

era-1721.says: Wikipedia (Swedish Livonia) and Wikipedia (Riga Governorate): ceded at Nystad in 1721; the Riga Governorate infobox (1713-1783) shows the Flag of Riga. Wikipedia (Flag of Riga) says the Swedish-granted Riga flag was used until 1860, so the city kept its own flag through the Russian period. Wikipedia (Flag of Russia) and FOTW: the white-blue-red tricolour was a civil ensign from 1705 and was recognised for land use only later (FOTW: 1883).
era-1721.open: No page read gives a flag for Livonia as a Russian province in 1721-1795. The tricolour is attested as a Russian merchant/civil ensign, not as a flag flown over the province, and the only flag recorded in Livonia in this period is Riga's city flag. The card's tricolour is not confirmed.

era-1621.says: Wikipedia (Swedish Livonia) shows a provincial Livonia flag and an 18th-century coat of arms in its infobox and no flag text. Wikipedia (Flag of Riga) says the Swedish king gave Riga his royal colours in the mid-17th century, a blue flag with a yellow cross bearing the crossed keys on a red shield, used until 1860; FOTW (Riga) says Riga then had a Swedish merchant flag with its arms on a red field (the two differ on the colour). Neither describes the plain Swedish national flag over Riga or Livonia.
era-1621.open: No source read says the Swedish national flag flew over Livonia; the Riga flags recorded (Wikipedia and FOTW, both compiled and disagreeing on the field colour) are city or merchant flags. The plain Swedish flag drawn is a stand-in. Latvian-language pages tried timed out and were not read.

era-1561.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Livonia): vassal duchy of Lithuania and from 1569 of the Commonwealth, infobox coat of arms and no flag; Wikipedia (Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth): royal banner in the infobox, nothing about Livonia. FOTW (Riga historical flags) and Wikipedia (Flag of Riga) record a Riga merchant flag, white with the city's red arms, after 1582 - a city flag under Polish-Lithuanian rule. No second-publisher or reference source (encyclopedia, archive, museum) naming a flag over Livonia was found.
era-1561.open: No page read gives a joint Polish-Lithuanian banner over Livonia or over Riga; the only flag recorded for the period is Riga's own merchant flag (FOTW and Wikipedia agree on white with red arms), which is a city flag. The Commonwealth flag drawn is a stand-in. Latvian-language pages tried (lvportals.lv, visc.gov.lv, vestnesis.lv) timed out and were not read.

era-1201.says: Re-read for a second look: Wikipedia (Livonian Order) calls it an autonomous branch of the Teutonic Order formed in 1237 and shows no flag text; Wikipedia (Livonian Brothers of the Sword, 1202-1236) describes no banner; Wikipedia (Livonian Confederation) has no flag text; FOTW (Teutonic Order) gives the Order's flag as a black Scandinavian cross on white (Smith 1975; Banderia Prutenorum). A Warsaw-held 1566 Königsberg chronicle print is catalogued (URUS database) as showing a 'coat of arms of Livonian Order', with no description of the design.
era-1201.open: Still no source describes a banner for the Livonian Order, Terra Mariana or the Brothers of the Sword (the 1201-1237 start predates the branch); the black cross on white is the parent Order's flag carried over by inference. The cross-on-white drawing remains an assumption.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: the flag was introduced into the Constitution on 7 December 1943 (first raised 21 November 1943 at Bechamoun), three horizontal stripes with a double-width white stripe and a cedar occupying one third of it. Flags of the World: adopted 07 Dec 1943; the 1926 constitution's blue-white-red with cedar article was changed on 7 December 1943 to red, white and red horizontal stripes with a green cedar.
era-1943.open: 'Unchanged since 1943' is not exact: Wikipedia says the cedar was usually drawn with a brown trunk until a 21 September 1990 amendment made the whole tree green. FOTW says the cedar was officially green from the start; the two differ on that.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia: demonstrators raised a cedar-bearing tricolour at Baabda on 22 March 1920; it captions the State of Greater Lebanon flag as used 1920-1943 and quotes the constitution of 23 May 1926 (blue, white, red vertical bands, cedar on the white). FOTW (citing Heimer): the French tricolour with a cedar in the middle was used under the French mandate; it quotes the same 23 May 1926 article.
era-1920.open: Neither page describes the plain French tricolour as the mandatory power's own flag in Lebanon, or the two flying side by side.

era-1861.says: Flags of the World (Olle, 2003, citing Flaggenmitteilung 84) says the flag of the Mutaserif (governor) and of the Mutasarrifate was the Ottoman state flag, a red cloth with a white crescent and star (Nehme 1995). Wikipedia's Flags of the Ottoman Empire gives the red flag with a white crescent and star as the official national flag from 1844, and its Flag of Lebanon records a 1907 proposal to add a cedar branch to the Ottoman flag for Mount Lebanon and a white cedar flag in 1918-1919.
era-1861.open: The mutasarrifate's flag is stated outright only by Flags of the World; Wikipedia's Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate article has no flag text and its Lebanon article implies the Ottoman flag only through the 1907 proposal. No decree tying the design to 1861-1918 was read.

era-1517.says: Flags of the World lists the Ottoman flag for 1516-1918 as a red cloth with a white crescent and star (Nehme 1995) and, on its Lebanon history page, separate local flags (Maanid emirate c.1119-c.1697, Chehab emirate c.1697-1842 blue with a white crescent, and others). Wikipedia's Flags of the Ottoman Empire shows a simple red-field crescent flag in use c.1480-1780, war flags with the Zulfiqar sword in the 16th-17th centuries, and the star and crescent from the second half of the 18th century, officially adopted in 1844. Wikipedia and FOTW date the Maronite white cedar flag's first attested use to October 1848.
era-1517.open: The two publishers differ on the design: FOTW gives a crescent and star for all of 1516-1918, while Wikipedia has the plain crescent to c.1780 and the star only later, so the card's single crescent fits only part of the span. Neither says the flag flown in Ottoman Syria itself in 1517-1861 was this one; the local emirs' flags rest on FOTW alone.

era-1289.says: Flags of the World (Nehmé 1995): the Mamluk flag in Lebanon was 'a cloth embroidered with golden threads' (tagged plain yellow), listed 1282-1516. Wikipedia (Mamluk Sultanate): the sultans followed the Ayyubids in using yellow as the colour associated with the sultan, on sultanic banners; sultans and emirs also had personal blazons (about forty-five symbols such as a cup, sword or animal) that stayed on their banners; Tripoli fell to the Mamluks in 1289 and Ottoman conquest followed in 1517.
era-1289.open: A gold field is stated by both publishers; the simplified eagle blazon on the card is not, since blazons were personal and the sources name no eagle. The card is a reconstruction, not a surviving banner.

era-1109.says: Wikipedia's County of Tripoli article shows a banner of arms of the House of Toulouse-Tripoli as its infobox flag, derived from the arms, with no description in the text. Wikipedia's Occitan cross article says the Toulouse cross (gold cross on red) appears on 12th-13th-century seals and coins of the counts of Toulouse, with a 1165 seal of Raymond V, and does not mention Tripoli. Flags of the World's Lebanon history lists only the Kingdom of Jerusalem among the crusader entries.
era-1109.open: No source read shows a banner actually used in the County of Tripoli, or the Jerusalem cross the card once drew; the red field with a gold cross is the counts of Toulouse's arms, whose use as the Tripoli branch's banner is only implied by Wikipedia's infobox. All of this rests on Wikipedia, with no independent or primary source found.

era-1109-1.says: Flags of the World's Lebanon history page lists a 'Phoenician (?)' flag, blue for the sea with red added later (Nehme 1995), a 'Tanukh (?)' flag supposed to date from the 4th century, and the Umayyad (660-750) and Abbasid (750-1258) caliphates; contributors on its Phoenician page doubt how old the Phoenician and Tanukh flags are and how reliable their existence is. Wikipedia's Flag of Lebanon describes no flag for antiquity and speaks of the cedar as a tree and Maronite emblem, not an ancient banner.
era-1109-1.open: The card openly shows no flag, which fits FOTW's own doubts, but FOTW does list questioned Phoenician and Tanukh flags and caliphal entries that the card does not draw. No source read says the cedar was a defining symbol in antiquity (FOTW's Phoenician page does not mention cedars); Wikipedia traces the cedar flag to the Maronites from the 18th century, first recorded in 1848.

era-1966.says: Wikipedia: the flag adopted on 4 October 2006, the 40th anniversary of independence, is a horizontal blue, white and green tricolour with a black mokorotlo (Basotho hat) in the centre; blue is the sky or rain, white peace, green prosperity; it replaced the military-emblem flag. FOTW (Lesotho): parliament voted 84 to 18 in September 2006 for the new flag, with the hat and the colours of peace, rain and prosperity; the black symbolises Africa; the flag was introduced at midnight on 3 October 2006. FOTW (previous flags): the 1966 independence flag was replaced on 17 or 20 January 1987 by a flag with a shield and spears, which lasted until 2006.
era-1966.open: The black hat flag dates from 2006, not 1966: Lesotho had a different flag from 1966 to 1987 and from 1987 to 2006, so the era title 1966-present covers three flags. Wikipedia and FOTW give the meaning of blue as the sky or rain and the black as Africa (FOTW).

era-1824.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1868.says: FOTW's Basutoland page says Basutoland 'did not have a distinctive colonial flag of its own and flew only the Union Jack as a national flag' until independence in 1966; Moshoeshoe obtained British protection on 12 March 1868, the territory was annexed to the Cape in 1871 and returned to the Crown in 1884; its Resident Commissioner had a personal flag. Wikipedia's flag article shows the Union Jack as the flag of Basutoland for 1884-1966 and lists an unofficial flag of Basutoland, a Resident Commissioner's flag and arms for 1951-1966. Second look: World Statesmen lists the Flag of the United Kingdom for Basutoland from 12 Mar 1868 to 4 Oct 1966, a Resident Commissioner flag 1951-65 and an unofficial Basutoland flag 1951-66; OzOutback says the Basotho flew the Union Jack for lack of a flag of their own after the 1868 protectorate.
era-1868.open: Four compiled publishers (FOTW, Wikipedia, World Statesmen, OzOutback) agree that the Union Jack was the territory's flag; none documents a Blue Ensign with a Basutoland badge as the colony's flag, and at most an unofficial ensign appears after 1951. Nothing read gives a flag for the territory before 1868/1884 beyond the Cape's; the start date differs (1868 in FOTW and World Statesmen, 1884 in Wikipedia).

era-2003.says: Wikipedia: the April 1961 law specifies eleven alternating red and white stripes and a blue canton with a white star; the Deshield Commission (1974-1978) recommended no changes. Flags of the World (last modified 2026) describes the current flag as eleven red and white stripes with a blue canton bearing a white five-pointed star under the Flag Law of 11 April 1961, introduced on 26 July 1847.
era-2003.open: Neither source discusses the postwar years; that the flag was unchanged since 2003 rests on both describing the same design as the present flag. The meaning of the stripes as eleven signatories is a FOTW contributor's.

era-1000.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — fragmented pre-colonial era, no unifying flag».
era-1000.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1980.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Liberia): the current flag, eleven stripes and one white star on a blue canton, was adopted on 24 August 1847, and the Deshield Commission reported on 24 January 1978 that no flag changes were recommended. Flags of the World (Liberia): the flag was legally established by the Constitution annex of 16 June 1847 and its governmental-flags page carries a contributor note that German television in 2003 showed Charles Taylor with the presidential flag and the national flag.
era-1980.open: No source states what the national flag was throughout 1980-2003 or that no faction replaced it; the evidence is the 1847 design, the 1978 commission and one 2003 report. The silence of the sources on the civil-war years is not evidence of no change.

era-1847.says: Wikipedia: 26 July 1847 independence declared; flag adopted and unfurled in Monrovia 24 August 1847; seven US-born women stitched it; eleven stripes for the signers of the Declaration of Independence; star for the first independent African republic. FOTW: 16 June 1847 Annex established six red and five white stripes, blue canton and white star; Susanna Waring-Lewis chaired the committee; eleven stripes for signers (or convention delegates).
era-1847.open: Adoption date differs (16 June vs 24 August 1847); 'modelled deliberately on the US flag' is not stated by either source.

era-1839.says: Flags of the World (Liberia 1827-1847, after Smith 1980): quotes the Resolution of the American Colonization Society of 9 April 1827 adopting the US flag with a white cross in place of the stars, and says Liberia had had that flag since 1827, a Liberian ship flying it being seized by the British in 1845, until it was altered to eleven stripes and one star on 26 July 1847. Wikipedia (Flag of Liberia): the 9 April 1827 resolution set a US-pattern flag with a white cross for the stars, and its list of historical flags gives 1827-1847 for the Colony of Liberia (citation needed).
era-1839.open: The two sources differ on the Commonwealth's own flag: Wikipedia has the Commonwealth's first government using the US flag until 26 April 1845, FOTW has the cross flag through 1847. Neither describes a Commonwealth flag as such for 1839-1847; the cross banner is the Society's colonial flag.

era-1822.says: Wikipedia: the 9 April 1827 resolution created the first colonial flag (US pattern, white cross in the canton); African Americans began arriving in 1822. Flags of the World (page on the 1827-1847 flag) quotes the resolution of the American Colonization Society board of 9 April 1827: a flag was requested for the colony at Liberia, to be as like the US flag as possible yet distinct, 'omitting the stars and substituting therefore a white cross in the center of the azure field'; its main page says the colony's flag had a cross in the upper-left corner.
era-1822.open: That the US flag itself flew at Cape Mesurado from 1822 until 1827 is not stated by either source. The FOTW quote is a contributor's transcription of part of the resolution, with no addressee.

era-2011.says: Wikipedia: the 1951 red-black-green flag with a white crescent and star was readopted by the National Transitional Council (infobox 23 August 2011, text 3 August 2011) after the fall of Gaddafi. FOTW (Libya): the 1951-1969 flag was used by most flag-bearing protesters as an opposition symbol from the uprising of February 2011, and the NTC's Constitutional Declaration of August 2011 defines the flag.
era-2011.open: Wikipedia's two dates for the readoption conflict (23 August and 3 August 2011); FOTW calls the introduction date uncertain and says no earlier decree regulated its use. The page's claim that it was used from 'the earliest days' is supported by FOTW's reports from 21 February 2011.

era-630bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no flag in the modern sense existed in the ancient Mediterranean».
era-630bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1977.says: Wikipedia: plain green flag adopted 19 November 1977, used until 2011, described as Gaddafi's symbol for his political philosophy. FOTW 'Libya, 1977-2011': the flag was adopted in 1977 after Libya left the Federation of Arab Republics; green is the national colour and a symbol of devotion to Islam; the page also reports unconfirmed variants (a naval ensign with crossed anchors, a late takbir version).
era-1977.open: Neither source mentions the Green Book for the flag, and neither says it was the only national flag without a design. FOTW gives only the year 1977, and the end in 2011 is shown by its 1977-2011 heading.

era-1969.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Libya): after the 1969 coup the Libyan Arab Republic flew the Pan-Arab red-white-black tricolour (Arab Liberation Flag) until 1972; in 1972 Libya joined the Federation of Arab Republics and took its flag with the golden Hawk of Quraish holding a scroll, in use to 1977. Flags of the World (ly_1969): the red-white-black horizontal tricolour (1:2) was adopted on 7 November 1969; (xo-far): from 1972 Egypt, Libya and Syria used the red-white-black tribar with the gold hawk, which Libya gave up in 1977.
era-1969.open: Wikipedia also mentions a flag planned for a 1974 merger with Tunisia that FOTW does not cover, and gives a 3:2 ratio for the Federation flag that FOTW does not state. The drawing shows the 1972-1977 hawk flag, not the plain 1969-1972 tricolour.

era-1951.says: Wikipedia: flag officially adopted 24 Dec 1951 at independence, constitution Article 7 of 7 Oct 1951; attributed to Shennib; star and crescent linked to the Senussi flag. FOTW: Kingdom flag 1951-1969 from independence, and the NTC used it as its symbol from 27 Feb 2011.
era-1951.open: Only the adoption date and 2011 revival are shared by both; the designer attribution is flagged by Wikipedia as needing a citation; first UN-created state claim not covered.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Libya): 1947-1951 the British-administered Cyrenaica and Tripolitania had no flag of their own and used the Union Flag, Fezzan-Ghadames under French administration used the flag of France, and the Emirate of Cyrenaica (1949-1951) kept a black flag with white crescent and star. Flags of the World (Cyrenaica): the black Sanussi flag with crescent and star was recognised for Cyrenaica under British administration after 1945. FOTW (Fezzan): the red crescent flag sometimes given for French-run Fezzan was a phantom image, and 'French Fezzan never had a flag' according to a correspondent. Second look: World Statesmen lists the Union Flag over Tripolitania from 23 Oct 1942 to 8 Mar 1951 and over Cyrenaica from Feb 1941 to 1947 (then a Cyrenaican flag 1947-1950), and the French flag over Fezzan from 12 Jan 1943 to 1951.
era-1943.open: Two publishers (Wikipedia, World Statesmen) now name the Union Flag for the British zones and the French flag for Fezzan; FOTW says French Fezzan never had its own flag and the red crescent flag was a phantom. The card still shows a four-quarter panel that matches none of these flags. The French flag over Fezzan rests on Wikipedia and World Statesmen only.

era-1911.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Libya): after the Italo-Turkish War the colonies of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, merged as Italian Libya in 1934, all used the flag of Italy (listed 1911-1947). Wikipedia (Italian Libya): the infobox for 1934-1943 shows the crowned Italian tricolour with the arms of Savoy. Flags of the World (Cyrenaica): under the Italian treaty with Idris el Senussi (1919) the emir was allowed to hoist his own flag along with the Italian one, which implies the Italian flag was flown there. Second look: World Statesmen lists the Italian flag over Tripolitania from 3 Oct 1911, Cyrenaica from 15 Oct 1912 and Fezzan from 15 Oct 1912, each until the British or French takeover (Tripolitania Oct 1942, Cyrenaica Feb 1941, Fezzan 12 Jan 1943). The Australian War Memorial holds an Italian naval ensign (green-white-red with the arms of Savoy in the white stripe) taken from the mast at Navy House, Tobruk, on 22 January 1941.
era-1911.open: The Italian flag is positively shown from three publishers and a museum object (1941), but the end of the span differs by region: Italian rule ended in Cyrenaica in 1941, Tripolitania in 1942 and Fezzan in January 1943, not 1943 everywhere. The AWM object is a naval ensign; the sources do not say the Italian flag was the sole flag, and the Savoy arms in the white band are omitted from the card's drawing.

era-900.says: Wikipedia (Ottoman Tripolitania): Ottoman rule lasted 1551-1912 (eyalet to 1864, vilayet 1864-1912) and the infobox shows a flag for it. Flags of the World (Tripoli): the only official flag in the Ottoman possessions was the Turkish red flag with crescent and star, while private ships flew many red and red-green variants (a contributor's statement). Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire): the red star-and-crescent flag was the state flag from 1793 and its five-pointed-star form was adopted in 1844. Second look: World Statesmen lists the Ottoman flag over Tripolitania until 1911, Cyrenaica until 15 Oct 1912 and Fezzan until 1912, and a separate local Karamanli flag for Tripolitania c.1727-1835, without describing either in text.
era-900.open: Holds only for the late Ottoman period (mainly after 1793/1844): the Ottoman flag over the three regions to 1911/12 is listed by Wikipedia, FOTW and World Statesmen. Nothing read gives a flag for c. 900 to 1551, and the Karamanli years (1711-1835) are covered by a local flag World Statesmen lists but does not describe, so the card's plain Ottoman flag is not shown for them. The FOTW statement about the only official flag is one contributor's.

era-1937.says: Wikipedia's text says the crown was added on 24 June 1937; its infobox gives 30 June 1982 for the current version. FOTW's history page (after Baert) says a yellow prince's bonnet was added in the blue stripe near the hoist on 24 June 1937 after the confusion with the Haitian flag at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, with the crown modified in 1957 and again in 1982, and its law page quotes Joseph Hoop's 1937 presentation of the flag.
era-1937.open: The crown's shape changed in 1957 and 1982, so 'unchanged since 1937' holds for the blue-over-red bicolour with a crown, not the crown itself. Design and swatch colours not checked against a specification.

era-1719.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1866.says: Wikipedia: blue and red livery colours date from Prince Joseph Wenzel I in 1764, blue and red replaced gold and red on the national flag in 1852, and the October 1921 constitution gave the blue-red banner official status before the crown was added in 1937. FOTW's history page agrees: blue and red have been national colours since 1852, in vertical or horizontal stripes, and the fundamental law of 5 October 1921 prescribed blue over red horizontally; it also says yellow over red is said to have been used until 1921.
era-1866.open: Both sources leave the orientation (vertical or horizontal) before 1921 unsettled, and FOTW's 'yellow over red until 1921' sits awkwardly with blue-red since 1852. The drawn horizontal blue-over-red is firm only for 1921-37.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Liechtenstein) says the gold and red horizontal bands of the coat of arms served as the national flag from 1719 until 1852, when blue and red, the livery colours first used by Prince Joseph Wenzel I in 1764, were chosen for the flag instead, and that the principality was in the German Confederation until 1866. Flags of the World (History of the national flag) says the flag was horizontally yellow over red until 1921 and is still used locally at festivities, and that blue and red have been national colours since 1852, in vertical or horizontal stripes.
era-1815.open: The sources differ on when the yellow-red flag ended (1852 or 1921), and blue and red replaced it as the national colours in 1852, so the drawing fits 1815-1852 rather than the whole span to 1866.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia says the Supreme Soviet readopted the tricolour on 18 November 1988, the Provisional Constitution of 11 March 1990 confirmed it, the 1992 constitution wrote it in without an aspect ratio, and Law IX-2331 of 8 July 2004 changed the ratio from 1:2 to 3:5 and adopted the historical state flag. FOTW adds 7 October 1988 on Gediminas Tower, 25 January 1989 standard and proportions, and the state flag law of 26 June 1991.
era-1990.open: FOTW's header gives 20 March 1989 as an adoption date; the two sources differ on the 1989 act.

era-1150.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-100.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: 1945 SSR flag red with hammer and sickle and 'LIETUVOS TSR'; in 1953 changed to red with a white and green bar at the bottom. FOTW: 15 July 1953 red-white-green flag confirmed, used until 1988.
era-1944.open: Neither source mentions a star on the flag.

era-1941.says: WorldStatesmen lists the interwar Lithuanian flag as 'semi-official' for 18 November 1941 - 1 August 1944, which agrees with Flags of the World (the Germans 'had no major objections') and disagrees with Wikipedia (Flag of Lithuania), which says the flag was prohibited and prosecuted. The Visuotine lietuviu enciklopedija confirms the Lithuanian General District within the Reichskommissariat Ostland under Generalkommissar von Renteln, with no word on flags. Wikipedia's Reichskommissariat Ostland shows a flag in its infobox without a description.
era-1941.open: Two compiled sources call the Lithuanian flag tolerated and one says it was banned, and none describes a flag specific to the Lithuanian General District; that the Reich flag was flown there rests only on the Ostland infobox image. A Lithuanian archive or museum source on flag orders in 1941-44 was not found.

era-1940.says: FOTW: Soviet occupation banned national symbols in June 1940; on 27 September 1940 the Presidium of the Lithuanian SSR replaced the tricolour with a red flag with a golden hammer and sickle. Wikipedia: Soviet occupation began in 1940 and a push by Smetona to change the flag was halted.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia: a commission submitted a protocol for the yellow-green-red tricolour on 19 April 1918 and the Council accepted it; the 1922 constitution adopted the tricolour. FOTW: 19 April 1918 approval by the commission; December 1905 the red flag with a white knight was proposed by Basanavičius and rejected because red suggested revolution.
era-1918.open: Neither source says the tricolour was chosen because it lacked a heraldic precedent; that motive was dropped.

era-1569.says: Wikipedia: the Vytis red banner with a mounted knight was used at the 1410 Battle of Grunwald and was the Grand Duchy's flag until the late 18th century. FOTW: Guagnini in 1578 describes a red silk flag with a white mounted knight under the ducal crown.
era-1569.open: Wikipedia does not say the rider was white; the Polish Eagle contrast is not in either source.

era-1253.says: FOTW: a 1337 chronicle mentions a Lithuanian flag burned at Bajerburg without describing it; Długosz has Vytautas bring 40 regiments with red banners, 30 bearing a mounted knight, to Tannenberg; Guagnini (1578) gives a white knight on red. Wikipedia: Vytis used at Grunwald in 1410.
era-1253.open: The page's earlier claim of attestation from the 14th century is not in the sources; the first description of the knight is 1410.

era-1795.says: WorldStatesmen lists the Russian flag, shown as the white-blue-red tricolour, for Lithuania from 7 January 1795 to 18 September 1915, with no basis given. The LRT history of Lithuanian state symbols says the Grand Duchy's flags and arms vanished with the 1795 partition, that imperial Russia destroyed the former state's heritage, that 19th-century risings used various colour combinations (blue-white-red among 1830-31 insurgents) and that Lithuanian-American groups used several tricolours; it names no flag flown by the Russian administration. Wikipedia and Flags of the World add nothing on 1795-1904 beyond the points already noted by the first reader (Lithuania Minor flag, regimental flags, 1905 proposals).
era-1795.open: Only one compiled list assigns the Russian tricolour to Lithuania, without a basis, and no source read describes a flag raised by the Russian administration over the governorates or a ban. The claim that no Lithuanian flag of any kind existed for 123 years is not supported.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): the horizontal red-white-light-blue tricolour was fixed on 12 June 1845, defined in 1848, and regulated by the law of 27 July 1993 (a 1972 emblems law was amended). Flags of the World (Luxembourg): flag law of 23 June 1972 and a 1993 regulation fixing the shades and proportions. Wikipedia (German occupation of Luxembourg): a photo caption shows civilians in Wiltz 'flying the flag of Luxembourg' at the liberation by US forces (liberation of the capital 10 September 1944).
era-1944.open: No source describes a formal 'restoration' in 1944/45; the 1944 start rests on the liberation dates and the photo caption. The sources differ on the de jure date (1993) and the 1972 law, and proportions were not checked.

era-963.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-53bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia (Gau Moselland) says that after the 1940 conquest Luxembourg was made a part of Gau Moselland, and Wikipedia (German occupation of Luxembourg) describes civil administration under Gauleiter Gustav Simon. Wikipedia (Flag of Germany) and Flags of the World (Third Reich) give the swastika flag as the national flag of Germany from 15 September 1935 to 1945. Flags of the World (German-occupied territories) lists Luxemburg among territories annexed into the Reich that had no flags of their own. Second look: the Deutsches Historisches Museum timeline says Gauleiter Simon took over the civil administration in July 1940 and the country was de facto annexed though not incorporated into the Reich in constitutional law; World Statesmen calls it attached/integrated but not formally annexed; Dostert's article describes Germanisation, party bans and the 15 August 1940 protest of red-lion badges. None mentions a flag.
era-1940.open: No source read says the Reich flag was flown over Luxembourg; the card rests on inference from incorporation into the Reich, and the sources say the annexation was de facto but not formal. The earlier label rested on FOTW's list of annexed territories without flags of their own; the museum and historian pages read here do not support or deny a flag.

era-1890.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg): the grand duchy passed to the House of Nassau-Weilburg in 1890, and its timeline marks 'Full independence' at 1890. Flags of the World: full independence in 1890 under Nassau-Weilburg after William III left no male heir. Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): the tricolour was fixed on 12 June 1845 and defined in 1848, so it was already the flag in 1890; Flags of the World also dates the tricolour to 1845.
era-1890.open: The page's 'first full independence since 1443' and '450 years' are in no source read; no source describes the flag specifically in use 1890-1940.

era-1839.says: FOTW: 1839 agreement made the western part of Luxembourg Belgian, the eastern part stayed under the Dutch crown. WP and FOTW both give 12 June 1845 for fixing the horizontal red-white-blue tricolor, derived from the arms.
era-1839.open: Purpose of distinguishing from Belgian/Dutch flags is not stated; WP calls its origin claims uncited.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg): the 1815 Congress of Vienna made Luxembourg a Grand Duchy in personal union with the Netherlands. Wikipedia (Flag of Luxembourg): 'Luxembourg had no flag until 1830' (uncited), when patriots were urged to display the national colours during the Belgian Revolution. Flags of the World: flags in the arms colours first used around the 1830 revolt.
era-1815.open: The Wikipedia statement is uncited and the drawing on the page shows the later design; no source describes how the Grand Duchy was marked 1815-1830. The 1839 end of the era (partition) was not checked.

era-1795.says: Wikipedia (History of Luxembourg) labels 1795-1815 as French rule, with the country part of the departement of the Forets. Wikipedia (Flag of France) says the blue-white-red tricolour was fixed by a resolution of 15 February 1794 and was France's flag until 1815; Flags of the World (France: First Empire) describes the Tricolore as the Empire's flag from 1804. Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) says Luxembourg was conquered and annexed by Revolutionary France, becoming part of the departement of the Forets in 1795.
era-1795.open: No source read states that the tricolour was flown in Luxembourg itself; it is the flag of the state that annexed the territory.

era-1714.says: Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) places Luxembourg in the Austrian Netherlands 1714-1795. Wikipedia (Austrian Netherlands) shows a 'civil ensign' as the infobox flag. Flags of the World (Austrian Netherlands) describes that flag as the civil ensign used from 24 September 1781 to 31 December 1786: red, white and yellow horizontal, with the Imperial Austrian eagle in front of the Cross of Burgundy. Second look: World Statesmen lists an "Austrian flag" for Luxembourg from 8 May 1713 to 15 Dec 1792 and 28 Apr 1793 to 1 Oct 1795 (French flag in between), without describing it.
era-1714.open: Only the 1781-1786 civil ensign is documented by description; World Statesmen supports an Austrian flag over Luxembourg through most of 1713-1795 but does not say which design, and nothing read shows what flew in the landlocked duchy in 1714-1781 or 1786-1795. The caption's yellow-and-black double eagle is not what the sources describe.

era-1581.says: Wikipedia (Spanish Netherlands) shows the Cross of Burgundy as the top flag in its infobox (with a civil ensign below), and Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) places Luxembourg in the Spanish Netherlands 1581-1714. Flags of the World (Spain, historical flags 1506-1700) lists an 'Ensign for the Spanish Netherlands c.1520-c.1701' and cites a Spanish flag book giving the cross as the flag of the Flemish provinces, probably including Luxembourg, 1520-1648. Flags of the World (Belgium plate) quotes the claim that the cross stayed in use under Spanish rule, mostly at sea. Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy) says the Spanish Habsburgs kept using it.
era-1581.open: The sources tie the cross to the Spanish Netherlands as a whole and mostly to ensigns and military flags, not to the Duchy of Luxembourg by name in text; Flags of the World gives 1648 and c.1701 as end dates for the cited uses. The 'Spanish Habsburg crown' in the caption is not described, and Wikipedia dates Spanish rule from 1556, not 1581.

era-1443.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy) calls the white banner with a red saltire raguly a historical banner and battle flag used by the Dukes of Burgundy and their subjects from the 15th century, ruling much of the Low Countries, and says the Habsburgs took it over after 1477. Wikipedia (Duchy of Luxembourg) lists the duchy as part of the Burgundian Netherlands (1443-1482) and the Habsburg Netherlands (1482-1581). Flags of the World (Spain, historical flags 1506-1700) cites a Spanish flag book that gives the cross as the flag of the Flemish provinces, probably including Luxembourg, from 1520; Flags of the World (Belgium plate) quotes a claim that most Low Countries provinces adopted it in the 15th century and notes first confirmed use in 1411 as a party livery.
era-1443.open: No source says in so many words that the Cross of Burgundy flew over the Duchy of Luxembourg before 1520. The 'whole bloc' wording rests on the plate author's claim, which Flags of the World treats cautiously. Wikipedia's Burgundian period ends 1482, not 1581.

era-1995.says: Both sources give 1995, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 5 October 1995; Flags of the World dates it 5 October 1995.
era-1995.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia: Kutlesh flag with the Vergina Sun adopted 11 August 1992; Greece objected, imposed a blockade from February 1994 and sought trademark protection in 1995; current flag adopted 5 October 1995. FOTW: August 1992 flag of 16 rays, a 1992 competition of over 100 designs, current flag adopted 5 October 1995.
era-1992.open: Neither source gives the 30% GDP figure.

era-1944.says: Wikipedia: ASNOM proclaimed the state on 2 August 1944; the first flag was a gold-edged red star on red, December 1944; an amended version adopted 31 December 1946 stayed in use until 1992. FOTW (Flag of Socialist Macedonia): red flag with a yellow-outlined star in the canton, adopted 31 December 1946 and superseded by the Vergina sun flag in 1992; the 1963 constitution text describes a red star with a gold edge, the star's centre at the intersection of the diagonals of the top hoist quarter; earlier variants were used from 1944 (photos of ASNOM); FOTW's contributors add that the red field was chosen in memory of the Ilinden uprising and Kruševo Republic.
era-1944.open: The Ilinden link is a statement by one FOTW contributor (Todorović), not a document; the page's 'only republic flag that skipped the pan-Slavic tricolor' is in neither source and is not true of the other republics' red flags with stars.

era-13.says: FOTW (mk_1903): in August 1903 a plain red flag was hoisted in the liberated town at Nikola Karev's initiative, with no source named. Wikipedia (Ilinden Uprising; Kruševo Republic): the insurgents flew Bulgarian flags and IMARO banners with 'Freedom or Death'. Tomalevski (1968): Pitu Guli's flag has 'red folds', the insurgents fight under a crimson banner inscribed 'Freedom or Death', and 'the flag of the republic' flies over the town.
era-13.open: Tomalevski describes a red or crimson banner with lettering, not a plain red flag, and does not say Karev ordered a plain red flag; the flag of the republic itself is not described, and the text is Bulgarian-published. H. Silyanov's 1933 history (promacedonia.org, read over http only because its https certificate failed, so not declared) likewise has Pitu Guli's detachment bringing a flag with a golden cross on one side and 'Freedom or Death' in red letters on the other. The card's plain red flag raised by Karev remains unconfirmed, though red flags with the 'Freedom or Death' lettering are described.

era-1941.says: FOTW (Macedonia in WWII): Macedonia was annexed by Bulgaria in 1941 and the Bulgarian flag was used there. Wikipedia (Kingdom of Bulgaria): after Yugoslavia and Greece were defeated, Bulgaria was allowed to occupy most of Macedonia, and Bulgarian troops entered Vardar Macedonia in April 1941. Wikipedia (Flag of Bulgaria): the white-green-red tricolour was the national flag from 1879 to 1947.
era-1941.open: The Bulgarian tricolour over the region rests on one line of FOTW plus Wikipedia's account of the occupation and the Bulgarian state flag; neither source describes the flag being raised there, and 'no separate regional flag was created' is not covered.

era-1912.says: Wikipedia (Vardar Banovina): the 1929-41 banovina (capital Skopje) has the Kingdom of Yugoslavia state flag as its infobox flag and no flag of its own is described. FOTW (Serbia 1882-1918): the national flag of the Kingdom of Serbia remained the red-blue-white tricolour of the Principality. FOTW's Macedonian pages (mk, mk_hist) start in 1945 and give no flag for Vardar Macedonia.
era-1912.open: The card presents the Yugoslav blue-white-red tricolour as a stand-in; the sources read name no regional flag, and the Serbian tricolour (red-blue-white) is the state flag only for 1912-18. Which flags were flown in the region is inferred from the ruling states, and a Flags of the World page for the Kingdom of Yugoslavia could not be found.

era-1392.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Ottoman Empire): pre-modern Ottoman armies used the horse-tail tugh; a simple crescent flag appears from 1453 and is reported until 1780; the star and crescent comes into use in the second half of the 18th century, with a 1793 naval decree and the 1844 national flag; its gallery shows a flag of Rumelia Eyalet (1365-1867). FOTW: the 1793/1844 dates are given 'without evidence'. Çetin (2021) says the Ottoman state used many banners at once and surveys museum flags of the 16th-19th centuries.
era-1392.open: No page read covers Macedonia or the vilayets of Rumelia, Kosovo and Manastir, and no single flag is shown to cover 1392-1912. The sources describe several concurrent banners, a crescent flag c. 1480-1780 (Wikipedia only), the star-and-crescent later, and the Rumelia Eyalet flag. 'Vilayets had none of their own' is not covered.

era-1346.says: Wikipedia (Serbian Empire, 'State insignia'): the 1339 map by Angelino Dulcert depicts Serbia by a flag above Skopje, a red double-headed eagle that the article says represented the realm of Stefan Dusan; a reconstruction from the map is shown in the article's gallery. The same section adds a red-white-red triband and a red-and-yellow cavalry flag said to be kept at Hilandar and a purple imperial divelion with a gold cross.
era-1346.open: The map is of 1339, seven years before the empire (1346) and while Dusan was king. The article does not state the ground colour (the card's gold) or name the Paris chart-holder, and calls the eagle double-headed whereas the drawing is a simplified single eagle silhouette. No Flags of the World page for the empire was found, so this is a single-publisher description.

era-1958.says: Wikipedia: the design was chosen by a technical commission on 15 October 1958 and officially adopted on 21 October 1958, a week after the Malagasy Republic was proclaimed; it describes a white vertical band at the hoist and red over green horizontal bands. FOTW's colonial page says Madagascar adopted a flag on 16 October 1958 similar to the current one, and FOTW's Madagascar page says the coat of arms was adopted on 24 December 1959 and the flag with the arms came later (possibly 1960).
era-1958.open: The sources give 21 October (Wikipedia) and 16 October (FOTW) for the 1958 adoption and FOTW's own Madagascar page has a 1959-60 flag with the arms; the page's account of the colours is contradicted: Wikipedia says the colours originally had no meaning and were explained in 1958 as white purity, red sovereignty, green hope, and FOTW notes that sources disagree on the green (Hova, not coastal peoples).

era-500.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — early Austronesian-descended settlement and pre-Merina kingdoms, no flag survives».
era-500.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1896.says: FOTW (Madagascar protectorate): the French protectorate ended on 29 September 1896 when General Gallieni had the royal eagle on the Queen's palace taken down and the French national flag hoisted. FOTW (French colonies): the common flag of all French possessions was the French Tricolore, and Madagascar adopted its own flag on 16 October 1958. Wikipedia (French Madagascar, 1897-1960): infobox shows the flag of France and a governor's flag. The Library of Congress study says France declared Madagascar a colony in 1896 and deported the queen.
era-1896.open: Two compiled publishers and the Library of Congress support the French tricolour as the flag over Madagascar from 1896 until 1958. No source read shows a Madagascar-specific colonial badge, so the brown disc in the caption's 'colonial badge' is unsupported; the evidence is for the plain French tricolour (and a governor's flag). Wikipedia dates the colony from 1897 and FOTW the end of the protectorate to 1896, and Wikipedia's infobox date for the own flag is 21 October 1958 against FOTW's 16 October.

era-1810.says: Wikipedia: in 1810 Radama adopted a white-and-red bicolour combining his father's two standards, and rulers put their name in red lettering on a white or white-and-red flag. FOTW (citing DK, 1997): the Merina Kingdom's flags were all red and white, with no dates or designs.
era-1810.open: Neither source describes a red disc with a white star or a red border; that emblem is the page's own reconstruction. FOTW gives no dates.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: adopted 6 July 1964 at independence, a black, red and green triband with a red rising sun of 31 rays on the black band; changed in 2010 (white sun, red-black-green) and restored on 28 May 2012. Flags of the World: the Protected Flag, Emblems and Names Act says the flag was 'adopted at independence on 06 July 1964'; the 2010 change and the re-adoption signed 28 May 2012; black for the people of Africa, rising sun for the dawn of hope and freedom, red for the blood of martyrs, green for the nature of Malawi.
era-1964.open: A 1999 article cited by FOTW dates the colours to July 1961 (the party's colours); the flag was off the national scene 2010-2012, so 'unchanged since 1964' is not exact. The page's phrase about the sun echoing Pan-African suns is not in either source.

era-1953.says: Flags of the World's Nyasaland page says that after Nyasaland joined the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland in 1953 the Federal Blue Ensign was flown in the colony alongside the Union Jack, and dates Nyasaland's own badge ensign to 23 October 1953; its Federation page describes the Federal flag as a Blue Ensign with the Federation shield (arms granted by Royal Warrant on 22 July 1954), the rising sun taken from Nyasaland's arms. Wikipedia's Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland article shows the Federation flag in its infobox, and its Nyasaland article places Nyasaland in the Federation from 1953 to 1963. Second look: OzOutback's 'Flags from Malawi' also says the Federation's flag was again the British Blue Ensign with the Federation's coat of arms on the fly.
era-1953.open: Only Flags of the World states that the Federal ensign was flown in Nyasaland; Wikipedia's Federation flag is an infobox image without text. The Union Flag stayed official beside it, and no separate territorial ensign for 1953-1963 is listed. OzOutback does not say the Federal ensign was flown in Nyasaland, and may rest on the same Flags of the World material.

era-1891.says: Flags of the World describes a Blue Ensign with a badge of a branched tree with red fruits for the British Central Africa Protectorate (renamed from the Nyasaland Districts protectorate declared 15 May 1891, in 1893), and, after the arms granted on 11 May 1914, a Blue Ensign with a badge of a leopard before a rising sun for Nyasaland (renamed 6 July 1907), on a white disc until 1919, used until 23 October 1953. Wikipedia's British Central Africa Protectorate and Nyasaland articles each show a flag of the territory in the infobox (1893-1907; 1925-1964), as images with dates only. Second look: a second compiler, OzOutback's 'Flags from Malawi', agrees that the 1891 protectorate flag was a Blue Ensign with its emblem on the fly and that in 1914 the new arms (leopard and rising sun) were placed on a white disk on the Blue Ensign, with the arms placed directly on the ensign from 1919, a change of colour in the arms in 1925, and that flag lasting until 1953.
era-1891.open: Only Flags of the World describes the badges in words; Wikipedia's flags are infobox images without description. The badge changed (tree before 1907 or 1914, leopard and sun after), so the card's single 'Nyasaland badge' fits 1914-1953 only, and no flag is described for 1891-1893. The badge drawn on the card matches neither. OzOutback is a hobby compilation and may rest on the same Flags of the World material, and it does not describe the 1891 emblem; no government, admiralty or museum record was reached.

era-1963.says: Both sources give 1963, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 26 May 1950; Flags of the World dates it September 1963.
era-1963.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1957.says: Wikipedia: Federation of Malaya flag, 11 red and white stripes with a blue canton, yellow crescent and 11-point star; approved 19 May 1950, first raised 26 May 1950, raised at Merdeka Square on 31 August 1957, 14 stripes and 14 points from 16 September 1963. Flags of the World (Federation of Malaya 1950-1963): eleven stripes and an 11-pointed star on a blue canton, approved by King George VI on 19 May 1950 and first raised on 26 May 1950, increased to 14 in 1963; FOTW's 1949 proposals page quotes Evans (1953) that the eleven stripes and points indicate the eleven states of the Federation.
era-1957.open: The 31 August 1957 raising is stated by Wikipedia and a FOTW reader comment, not by FOTW's Federation page; FOTW dates the Legislative Council approval to 19 April 1950.

era-1946.says: Wikipedia: the Federated Malay States tiger flag (1896-1946) was used by the Malayan Union (1946-1948) and the Federation of Malaya (1948-1950), with the 11-stripe Federation flag from 1950. Flags of the World (Malay Flag of 1905-1950) covers the Federated Malay States, Malay Union and Malay Federation. Britannica gives the Malayan Union founding (1 April 1946), the Federation (1 February 1948), the tiger on a white oval in the Federated Malay States ensign and the 11-stripe flag first hoisted on 26 May 1950.
era-1946.open: This holds for 1946-1950 only, and for the Malayan Union and Federation, not for the Crown Colonies of Singapore, Penang and Malacca (separate badged flags). Britannica does not say which flag the Malayan Union used; that rests on Wikipedia and FOTW (two publishers). The 1950-1957 striped Federation flag is not drawn.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia's Japanese occupation of Malaya article carries the Japanese flag as the flag of Japanese-occupied Malaya in its infobox, and its Flag of Japan article says the flag was a tool of Japanese imperialism in occupied Southeast Asia, where people had to use it (with local flags allowed in some areas such as the Philippines and Indonesia). FOTW's Malaysia history index lists the Japanese occupation (1941-1945) only as a date.
era-1942.open: Both Wikipedia statements are one publisher, and neither names Malaya among the areas where local flags were or were not allowed; FOTW gives no occupation flag. The card's 'Japanese military administration ensign' wording is the page's own.

era-1826.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Malaysia dates Straits Settlements flag versions 1826-1868, 1868-1877, 1874-1904, 1904-1925 and 1925-1946, and the Federated Malay States tiger flag 1896-1946. FOTW's Straits Settlements page says the settlements were administered together after 1826 and became a Crown Colony in 1867, with a Blue Ensign and gold crown from c.1868, then a Blue Ensign with a three-crown badge on a red lozenge (white disc dropped after 1925), plus a Union flag and red ensign variant; its Malaya pages date the Federated Malay States flag from 1905 and list the Straits Settlements as 1826-1946.
era-1826.open: The flags changed several times across 1826-1942 and the drawing shows only the 1868-1877 version; the Malay states' own flags are not covered, and FOTW's tiger-flag date (1905) differs from Wikipedia's (1896). The caption's plain 'British colonial ensign' wording is looser than the sources.

era-1826-1.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Malaysia and Malacca Sultanate articles and FOTW's Malaysia and Malacca pages describe no flag of the Malacca Sultanate or the successor sultanates; they say only that yellow is the Rulers' colour. Britannica's Flag of Malaysia says the flag traditions of the states emphasised white, red, yellow and black and gives the 1896 Federated Malay States ensign, with no mention of Malacca or a pre-1826 banner. The Malaysian government flag page cited by Wikipedia returned HTTP 404.
era-1826-1.open: A plain red field as the sultanate's banner is not found in any source read; nothing read dates a banner before 1826. No Malay chronicle (Sejarah Melayu) text could be searched.

era-1968.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1965.says: Wikipedia: independence from the UK in 1965 removed the black-and-white striped hoist, giving the modern design (green rectangle on red with a white crescent), adopted 25 July 1965; Sultan's Standard 1965-1968, Presidential Standard from 1968. FOTW: current flag adopted 25 July 1965, hoist strip withdrawn in 1965, the Sultanate ended about three years after independence.
era-1965.open: FOTW cites Crampton for the current national and presidential flags being introduced officially on 26 July 1968, which conflicts with 1965; the sources read do not reconcile the dates.

era-1954.says: Wikipedia: the Sultanate was restored in 1954 but the flag was not changed back; a Sultan's Standard with a five-pointed star was used 1954-1965. FOTW's protectorate page (Crampton 1990): the Sultan was reinstated in 1954 'and there were no changes to Maldivian flags', continuing to independence in 1965; the sultanate page (Flaggenbuch) gives the state flag as red with a green panel and crescent plus a striped hoist band. World Statesmen: sultanate from 7 Mar 1954, one flag image for 1953 - 26 Jul 1965.
era-1954.open: The crescent's direction is disputed (Wikipedia: toward the hoist; FOTW and the Maldives Royal Family page: toward the fly). The green-rectangle design is described in words by FOTW's sultanate page (Flaggenbuch) and shown in Wikipedia's gallery, whose text only says the state flag's crescent was reversed.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: on becoming a republic in 1953 the national flag was dropped and the crescent on the state flag was reversed to face the hoist. FOTW (Crampton 1990): a republic 1953-1954; the crescent was turned to face the fly and the service flag became the national flag. World Statesmen: republic from 1 Jan 1953 to 7 Mar 1954, with a flag image captioned 1953 - 26 Jul 1965. A Maldives Royal Family opinion page shows a 1949-1965 flag with the crescent facing the fly. Three independent compiled publishers agree that the state flag (red, striped hoist, green rectangle with white crescent) served as the national flag in 1953.
era-1953.open: The crescent's direction is disputed (Wikipedia: toward the hoist, as drawn; FOTW and the Royal Family page: toward the fly). Neither Wikipedia nor FOTW describes a newly added crescent, and both place the crescent earlier; no Arabic calligraphy is mentioned. Dates on the Royal Family page differ (crescent 1903, reversed by 1949).

era-1887.says: Wikipedia: red with a black-and-white striped hoist (1796/1903-1926), with a white crescent added between 1926 and 1932 and a separate state flag with a green rectangle. FOTW (Flaggenbuch): national flag red with a striped hoist band and a white crescent toward the hoist. Romero-Frias: a rectangular national flag, red with the striped hoist, designed towards 1903; attempts in the 1920s to add a small crescent or a green rectangle were not sanctioned; the official flag later gained a green rectangle with a small white crescent pointing outwards. World Statesmen: British protectorate from 16 Dec 1887, flag images labelled up to c.1933 and c.1933-1953 (captions only).
era-1887.open: The crescent is placed in the late 1920s or 1930s by Wikipedia, Romero-Frias and the World Statesmen caption, so the card's flag with a crescent fits only roughly 1926-33 to 1953; for 1887-1903 the sources describe a striped hoist with no date, and for 1903-1926 a striped red flag with no crescent. The crescent's direction is disputed (Flaggenbuch: toward the hoist; Romero-Frias: outwards). No source mentions a black panel with the Shahada.

era-1573.says: Wikipedia dates a plain red flag 1117-1796 in its gallery (its list of Maldivian flags says double pennants and a red field 1796-1903) and says a black-and-white striped hoist, the Dhandimathi, was added later. FOTW (quoting Crampton 1990) says the flag was originally plain red and later given a striped hoist band, undated. The ethnographer Xavier Romero-Frias (essay on the Maldives Royal Family site) says the royal flags were plain red since very old times, the king's a two-pointed red pennant, that no rectangular national flag existed before about 1903, and that the striped hoist was added at an undated moment perhaps in the early nineteenth century.
era-1573.open: Red as the royal colour is supported by three publishers, but the shape (pennant against rectangular flag) and the date the striped hoist appeared (1796 on Wikipedia, perhaps early nineteenth century on Romero-Frias, undated on FOTW) are not agreed, so a plain red field running to 1887 is contradicted for the later decades. No source describes a restoration after the Portuguese period.

era-1558.says: World Statesmen's Maldives chronology dates the Portuguese occupation of Male under Andreas Andre (Andhiri Andhirin) from 19 May 1558 to 1 Jul 1573, so the occupation itself is dated. Flags of the World's Portugal historical page (a discussion citing Portuguese sources) gives the royal flag of Sebastiao (1557-78) as the arms on white with a closed crown, which matches the crowned-shield drawing as Portugal's royal flag of the time. Wikipedia's Flag of Maldives and both Maldives FOTW pages say nothing of the occupation or of a flag for it.
era-1558.open: No source read says a Portuguese flag was flown over Male in 1558-1573 or what it looked like; the Portuguese royal flag is described for Portugal generally, not for the occupation. The card stays a stand-in.

era-1153.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Maldives) says the earliest flag of the Maldives was a plain red field, and its gallery dates that first flag 1117-1796. Flags of the World's main page and its sultanate page both quote Crampton (1990): 'The flag of the Maldives was originally a plain red flag.' Two publishers therefore describe a plain red banner for the early Sultanate.
era-1153.open: Neither source gives a flag specification or a document for the year 1153 (the conversion date used on this page); Wikipedia's 1117-1796 dating is a gallery caption with no explanation in the text read, and no early banner survives in what was read, so the drawing is a projection back across 1153-1558.

era-1961.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1959.says: Both: Mali Federation flag adopted 4 April 1959, green-gold-red vertical with a black kanaga on the gold band (Wikipedia explicit on layout). Flags of the World: independence 20 June 1960, Senegal's secession 22 August 1960, kanaga abolished and plain tricolor adopted 1 March 1961. Wikipedia: removal after Islamic opposition.
era-1959.open: Wikipedia and Flags of the World disagree about the 1958/1959 labelling of the French Sudan flag; neither explains the kanaga as a Dogon symbol; reasons for 1961 removal rest on Wikipedia's secondary citations.

era-1464.says: Wikipedia (Songhai Empire and Askia Muhammad I), searched for flag, banner, standard, regalia and emblem, describe none. Wikipedia's Flag of Mali only links the Songhai Empire article, and Flags of the World's Mali pages carry nothing on the empires.
era-1464.open: The card presents its sun-and-river motif as a reconstruction with no flag documented, and the sources read describe no Songhai banner. This is silence in the sources read, not evidence that none existed.

era-1235.says: Wikipedia (Mali Empire, 'Imperial regalia'): a red banner struck with a golden disc, the 'Mali djondjon' or 'Sun Banner' of Sundiata, appears in oral histories, and written sources have Mansa Musa using a similar banner, with yellow symbols on a red background, in Cairo; the article shows two possible reconstructions. Wikipedia (Flag of Mali): the royal standard of Musa I was reportedly a yellow rectangle centred on a red field, c. 1324, marked 'possible' and cited to Conrad (2010). Flags of the World's Mali pages carry nothing on the empire. Second look: Wikipedia's notes show the banner passage resting on oral histories and on al-Umari as quoted by al-Qalqashandi (through Levtzion and Hopkins' Corpus of Early Arabic Sources), which are not online in a form that could be read.
era-1235.open: The card shows a gold field with a disc and star as a motif for gold wealth. The sources read describe a red banner with yellow or golden charges, the reverse colour scheme, and rest on oral history and a single 2010 book; they do not describe a fixed flag for the whole empire from c. 1235 to 1464. The written source for Mansa Musa's banner could not be reached; it would describe a red banner with yellow symbols, not a gold field.

era-1964.says: Wikipedia: on 21 September 1964 (independence) the blue canton was replaced by a red fimbriation around the George Cross, which had been added to the flag on 28 December 1943. FOTW: on 21 September 1964 the flag and arms were changed, the blue canton removed and a red fimbriation added; the Republic followed on 13 December 1974.
era-1964.open: Neither source says the George Cross was newly moved to the canton in 1964; it was already on the flag from 1943. Wikipedia and FOTW differ on the Roger I date (1091 vs 1090), not relevant here.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia: the George Cross was officially added to the flag on 28 December 1943 (an unofficial flag listed for 1943-1964); its Crown Colony of Malta infobox shows the 1943-1964 flag and a colonial badge for those years. FOTW: the George Cross first appeared on 28 December 1943 on a small blue canton, the red-and-white flag was approved as official on 9 November 1954, and the badge was a white-and-red shield; its Historical Flags page lists State Ensign and Governor's Flag 1943-1964, quoting Barraclough & Crampton (1981).
era-1943.open: The badge was a white-and-red shield with the George Cross in a blue canton, not a blue shield; the drawing's field is a Union Jack with a small square rather than a Blue Ensign. The drawn details need checking against the badge.

era-1814.says: FOTW (Malta, historical flags) lists the State Ensign for 1875-c.1898, c.1898-1923 and 1923-1943, and cites Barraclough & Crampton (1981) and the Flaggenbuch (1939) for blue and red colonial ensigns with a badge of a white and red shield with a yellow relief border, on a white circle that disappears on the blue ensign. Wikipedia (Flag of Malta) shows the colony's flags for the 19th century, 1875-1898, 1898-1923 and 1923-1943, and its Crown Colony article dates the colony 1813-1964.
era-1814.open: The blue ensign with a white and red shield badge is attested for 1875-1943 only; the 19th-century flag before 1875 is listed by Wikipedia without a description, and the badge changed between 1875, c.1898 and 1923. Wikipedia dates the colony from 1813, not 1814. The drawing now follows the Blue Ensign layout.

era-1800.says: Hardman's 1909 history quotes General Pigot's dispatch from Valletta, September 1800: 'the British colours only are flying in Valetta and its dependencies', against the wish of Captain Ball and the British minister that Sicilian colours also be hoisted; a note by Ball says Sicilian colours had been hoisted everywhere on the island and were still flying in most parts of it. WorldStatesmen lists the flag of the United Kingdom for Malta from 8 Sep 1800 to 1875. Wikipedia (Malta Protectorate) shows the flag of the United Kingdom in its infobox and describes no flag in the text; FOTW and Wikipedia (Flag of Malta) describe Maltese flags from the 19th century and 1875.
era-1800.open: Positive evidence for the Union Flag covers September 1800 (Hardman) and the whole span as a list entry (WorldStatesmen); the later years to 1814 are not described in any text read. Sicilian colours also flew over much of the island in 1800. The card draws the post-1801 Union Flag design, and no text read describes the design hoisted in 1800. The claim that no Maltese colonial symbol existed yet is not covered. Wikipedia dates the protectorate 1800-1813 and the colony from 1813.

era-1798.says: Hardman's 1909 history, built on contemporary dispatches, says the French proclamation obliged all inhabitants to wear the tricolour cockade, that the tricolour floated at Valletta, and that in the revolt of September 1798 the French flag was lowered at Cospicua and the ancient white and red standard of Malta was raised on the ramparts of Notabile. WorldStatesmen lists the French flag for Malta from 12 Jun 1798 to 8 Sep 1800. Wikipedia (Flag of Malta) reports the white and red standard used by insurgents in September 1798; Wikipedia (French occupation of Malta) shows the French flag only in its infobox.
era-1798.open: Three publishers place the French tricolour over Valletta in 1798-1800, but after September 1798 the French held only Valletta and the Three Cities; the countryside flew the Maltese white and red standard and then Sicilian and British colours together (Hardman). None describes the arrangement of the tricolour's bands, so the vertical drawing is not documented by them.

era-1530.says: Wikipedia says the Knights' flag, a white cross on a red field, is a more likely source of Malta's colours than the Roger I legend. FOTW's Order of Malta pages give the Order's flag as red with a white (Maltese) cross, seen at buildings in Valletta tied to the Knights, and list the Order's historical ensigns flown in Grand Master Rohan's time (1775-97), citing Strickland's vexillological paper.
era-1530.open: Neither source gives 1530 or 1798 as dates; FOTW's page notes naval and signal variants (a red flamma, pennants and a naval jack) that this drawing does not show.

era-1986.says: Wikipedia: the flag was adopted at the start of self-government on 1 May 1979 (designer Emlain Kabua): blue field, two diagonal orange and white stripes, a white star in the upper hoist with 24 points for the electoral districts, four long points for Majuro, Jaluit, Wotje and Ebeye; the diagonal represents the equator and the stripes the Ratak (sunrise) and Ralik (sunset) chains. FOTW: adopted 1 May 1979 (DK Pocket Book), Bill 4 of 12 June 1979 approved 22 June 1979 describing blue with two contiguous trapezoidal bars from the lower left, orange above white, and a white 24-point star; the four longer points are Majuro, Ebeye, Jaluit and Wotje; the blue stands for the Pacific.
era-1986.open: The design and its meanings are attested by both. The page begins the flag in 1986, but both sources date it to 1979; 1986 (end of US administration, 21 October 1986 per Wikipedia's Trust Territory article) is the polity's date, not the flag's. Wikipedia reads the 24 points as electoral districts, FOTW as municipal districts; the page's cross-and-Christianity reading of the long rays is FOTW's (star as a cross) but Wikipedia assigns them to four centres.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands): the UN flag was used 1947-1965 and the US flag (50 stars since 1960) throughout; the territory's own flag, light blue with six white stars (one for the Marshalls), was first flown 24 October 1962, approved by the Congress of Micronesia in July 1965 and official 19 August 1965, in use until the 1970s and early 1980s. FOTW (xp-pc): the same six-star flag first hoisted 24 October 1962, official 19 August 1965; before it the US and UN flags were used; it ceased to be used after the trust's dissolution (1980 per FOTW). Wikipedia (Flag of the Marshall Islands) captions: UN flag 1947-1965, TTPI flag 1965-1979. Wikipedia (Trust Territory): 1947-1994; US administration of the Marshalls ended 21 October 1986.
era-1947.open: The sources show the US and UN flags and, from 1965, a territorial flag; the page's single plain US flag drawing is a simplification, and the territorial flag is not drawn. End dates of the TTPI flag differ (1979 caption, 1980, early 1980s); the Marshalls' own flag was adopted 1 May 1979. Wikipedia Trust Territory text read to 100,000 of 160,783 characters.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia's Flag of the Marshall Islands captions a flag used during Japanese colonial rule 1914-1944 and a flag of the Governor of the South Seas Mandate 1920-1944; its South Seas Mandate article shows a Japanese flag in the infobox and a separate Governor's flag, and dates the mandate 1919-1947. FOTW's Marshall Islands and German colonial pages do not cover the Japanese period.
era-1914.open: The Japanese flag's use rests on Wikipedia alone; no source describes the Governor's flag or says a separate territorial flag was issued, and the caption ends in 1944 while the mandate runs to 1947.

era-1885.says: FOTW's Ralik Islands page: the Ralik flag was adopted 20 November 1878 and suppressed in 1885; the Jaluit Company flag (based on the German national flag) was used until the colony was created on 1 April 1906. FOTW's German colonial flags page describes the Jaluit Gesellschaft flag as white with a black-white-red striped disc. Wikipedia captions the Jaluit Company flag 1885-1906 and a German New Guinea flag 1906-1914. A 1982 University of Hawaii thesis (Henning) says Lt Raettger claimed the protectorate in 1885 in the name of the German Empire, that administration was first placed in the Jaluit Gesellschaft's hands, and that the charter ended in 1906 with the islands put under the Island Sphere; it describes no flag.
era-1885.open: The Jaluit flag was a company flag; whether it, the German imperial flag or another flag stood for the protectorate is not stated by any source read, and no source describes a 1906-1914 colonial flag. The publishers disagree on the Ralik flag's end (1885 vs 1894).

era-2017.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.
