era-1959.says: Wikipedia: the first flag was adopted on 1 April 1959, a green field with a golden star and crescent, unchanged at independence on 28 November 1960 and until the 2017 change; green, crescent and star are symbols of Islam. FOTW (Former Flag): adopted 1 April 1959 (decree cited from Carr 1961; Rabbow gives the constitution of 22 March 1959), an emerald-green flag 2:3 with a gold crescent and five-pointed star in the centre; green and gold are Pan-African colours and the crescent and star Islamic symbols; the yellow stands for the Sahara (Znamierowski).
era-1959.open: Neither source gives a 'no French influence' reasoning. Wikipedia puts the 2017 change at a first raising on 28 November 2017; FOTW describes the 2017 flag as the old one with red stripes added.

era-1904.says: Wikipedia: the French flag flew in Mauritania from the early 20th century until 1 April 1959, when the national flag was adopted; the territory had been an autonomous republic since 28 November 1958. FOTW (French Colonial Empire): in French West Africa, which included Mauritania, the common flag of all possessions was the French Tricolore, local flags being adopted only by some territories shortly before independence; Mauritania's own flag was written into the constitution on 22 March 1959 and adopted officially on 1 April 1959.
era-1904.open: The page's 1904 start (the creation of the territory) is not dated by either source, and both sources show the national flag replacing the Tricolore in 1959, before independence on 28 November 1960 rather than at the end of the era.

era-1040.says: Wikipedia (Almoravid dynasty): the Almoravids adopted the Abbasid black standard, an emissary of 1104 announcing the adoption of the official Abbasid black for banners; the Lamtuna and Massufa used black for veils and war banners; the Almohads adopted white against them. Its sources include El-Hibri (The Abbasid Caliphate, CUP 2021) and Ibn Idhari, neither read here. Flags of the World (Morocco, historical): a contributor writes that the Almoravids institutionalised white silk banners, one per unit of 100 soldiers, with the shahada on leaders' banners, citing no source. TDV Islam Ansiklopedisi (BAYRAK), read for this pass, does not treat the Almoravids.
era-1040.open: The two sources contradict each other on the colour (black in Wikipedia, white in an uncited FOTW contributor note); neither shows a plain white field as the dynasty's single flag. No independent reference on Almoravid banners could be reached. The page's start year 1040 is the dynasty's beginning in Wikipedia's tables, 1062 in FOTW.

era-1968.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives adoption on 12 March 1968. Flags of the World (Mauritius): 'adopted upon independence, on 9 January 1968' (registered that day) and 'first officially hoisted on 12 March 1968, the day of independence' (Southworth 2004); designed by the College of Arms before independence (DK Ultimate Pocket Flags of the World, 1997); when Mauritius became a republic on 12 March 1992 the independence flag did not change (Zrzavy 2002).
era-1968.open: The 1968 start and the unchanged flag since are covered by both publishers; the meanings of the four colours on this page were not checked against either source.

era-1810.says: Flags of the World (pre-independence flags, Prothero citing CO 325/54 and ADM 116/1847B): the Blue Ensign badge, a quartered shield with the motto 'stella clavisque maris indici', was approved 14 December 1869; the arms granted in 1906 (25 August) were placed on a white disc, which was agreed unnecessary on 7 July 1921 and officially removed 14 December 1923, though the disc was used until independence in 1968 (Moss 2005); no defaced Red Ensign existed. Wikipedia's flag table lists British colonial flags for 1810-1869, 1869-1906, 1906-1923 and 1923-1968, and a colonial civil ensign for 1906-1968.
era-1810.open: A Blue Ensign with a Mauritius badge is documented from 1869, not 1810: neither source describes the flag of 1810-1869; the page's single drawing does not distinguish the 1869 badge from the 1906 arms.

era-1715.says: Wikipedia (French Mauritius): infobox flag for 1715-1792 whose file is the Royal Standard of the King of France, and no flag in the text; the colony was established in September 1715 and disestablished in December 1810. Wikipedia (Flag of France): before 1790 the royal government used many flags, the best known a blue shield with gold fleurs-de-lis on white. FOTW (Mauritius history): Ile de France from 1711 or 1718 to 1810, owned first by the Compagnie des Indes, with no French-period flag described.
era-1715.open: No source read says a white ensign with a gold fleur-de-lis flew at Isle de France, or describes the colony's flag in text; the infobox file name and the general account of royal flags are single-publisher and do not establish what flew in the colony. The Revolutionary tricolour (from 1790-92) is not covered for the island, and the start date varies (1711, 1715, 1718).

era-1598.says: Wikipedia (Dutch Mauritius): an official VOC settlement from 1638 to 1710, frequented by Dutch ships from 1598 but settled only in 1638 and abandoned in 1710; its infobox flag, dated 1638-1710, is the VOC flag. FOTW (Mauritius history): 1638-1710 Dutch administration; one contributor thinks only the normal Dutch flags and perhaps VOC flags were used. A VOC history site cited by Wikipedia (vocsite.nl) returned HTTP 403 and was not read.
era-1598.open: The VOC flag rests on Wikipedia's infobox alone and FOTW is speculative; no source read documents a Prince's Flag or any flag for the 1598-1637 landfalls, so the caption's Prince's Flag is unsupported.

era-1917.says: Wikipedia says the current flag was adopted on 16 September 1968 and confirmed by law on 24 February 1984, that a presidential decree of 1916 changed the eagle from front-facing to side-facing, and that a rule on the reverse side's eagle was published on 9 May 1995. FOTW says a decree of 17 August 1968 in the Diario Oficial adopted the flag and arms, that a decree of 8 February 1984 confirmed them, and that the law of 24 February 1984 did not change the design.
era-1917.open: The 1968 dates differ between the sources (16 September, 17 August, and this page's earlier 24 September). The era starts in 1917 and the sources date the current design to 1968. The colours' meanings are disputed and the law gives none.

era-1500bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner in any modern sense from any pre-Aztec Mesoamerican civilization».
era-1500bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1864.says: Wikipedia: the Second Empire flag had a 1:2 ratio with four crowned eagles at the corners; the arms were described in a November 1865 decree. Flags of the World (Second Mexican Empire page): flag and arms adopted by decree of 18 June 1864, confirmed on 1 November 1865 (ratio 1:2), abolished 15 July 1867; the republican government under Juarez kept using the 1823 flag throughout.
era-1864.open: The golden colour of the corner eagles is not stated by either text, and the FOTW text read does not mention corner eagles (only its images do). The 1863 start date on FOTW's page title reflects the empire's proclamation; the flag decree is 1864.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia: in April 1823 the first federal republic adopted a flag with the crown removed from the eagle and a serpent added to its talon; the republic's flag was discontinued in 1864. Flags of the World (1823-1880 page): adopted by decree of 14 April 1823, the crown removed from the eagle and a half circle of oak and laurel added; in use 14 April 1823 to 30 December 1880, with the republican government using it again from 20 September 1863 to 14 July 1867.
era-1823.open: The sources agree on the 1823 decree but differ on the end: Wikipedia says the republic's flag was discontinued in 1864, FOTW says the republican government kept using it through the Second Empire. The page's 'turbulent 19th century' narrative is not itself sourced.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia: Army of the Three Guarantees, 24 February 1821, first use of green, white and red; Iturbide's imperial flag with a crowned eagle decreed November 1821 (or 7 January 1822), first officially used July 1822. Flags of the World (Mexican Empire page, quoting the decrees): decree of 2 November 1821 and confirming decree of 7 January 1822 set vertical green, white and red stripes with a crowned eagle on the white stripe; used from Iturbide's coronation on 21 July 1822; abolished by decree of 14 April 1823. FOTW's main page names Iturbide as creator and mentions a Celaya theory of origin.
era-1821.open: What each colour meant in 1821, and the Mexica eagle-on-cactus symbolism drawn on the page, are not stated in the sources read; the FOTW page says its image of the flag is based on written sources only.

era-1867.says: Wikipedia: a 1916 decree by Carranza made the eagle side-facing; current flag adopted 16 September 1968. Flags of the World: the 1823 decree stayed in effect until 1968 with the flag restored officially on 15 July 1867 and revised in 1880, 1899, 1916 and 1934; its Carranza page gives a decree of 20 September 1916 in effect from 1 October 1916, arms approved 22 August 1918.
era-1867.open: The Porfiriato and Revolution as political periods are not described by the flag sources; the revisions of 1880 and 1899 were found on FOTW only, and the details of those arms changes were not read.

era-1521.says: Wikipedia (Cross of Burgundy): the saw-toothed red saltire on white flew in the New World viceroyalties, and a viceregal banner lasted as a symbol of New Spain until 24 August 1821. Flags of the World (Mexico history page): the flag and arms of New Spain were those of Spain; its Spain page says the red Burgundy cross, most often on white, was the main symbol of Spanish ships from Charles I (1518) to 1665 and the naval ensign 1506-1701, and a land war flag to 1843.
era-1521.open: The 1521 start and the cross's use over the whole of New Spain are not stated; after 1701 Spain changed royal banners and, in 1785, the sea ensign to red-yellow-red, so 'for most of the period' is as far as the sources go. Cortes's own 1519-1521 standard (red with the Virgin Mary) is a different flag.

era-1325.says: Wikipedia (Coat of arms of Mexico) says the eagle-on-prickly-pear emblem recalls the founding of Tenochtitlan, that for the people of Tenochtitlan it had strong religious connotations, and that it reads as a pictographic spelling of the capital's name; it adds that the Aztecs used flags (pantli) made of coloured feathers, displaying the officer's personal arms and carried on the back, with Bernal Diaz's account of the battle of Otumba. Wikipedia (Flag of Mexico) covers the eagle legend behind the arms without a date or a banner. Flags of the World (Evolution of the Mexican flag) says banners with the old pre-Hispanic emblem of eagle, snake and prickly pear were widely used on conquest expeditions such as Florida (c. 1550), after the Mexica period.
era-1325.open: The sources show the eagle-and-nopal emblem as a symbol of Tenochtitlan and feather standards as the Aztec form of flag, but none shows a rectangular banner bearing the emblem for the Mexica empire in 1325-1521; the card's green field with an eagle-and-cactus device is an invented reconstruction, not a documented banner.

era-1986.says: Wikipedia: adopted 30 November 1978, a light blue field with four white stars for Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae and Yap, derived from the Trust Territory's six-star flag of 1962 (approved 1965); the blue was changed to the UN-flag shade after the Compact of Free Association took effect on 3 November 1986. Flags of the World: 'adopted on 30 November 1978', stars reduced from six to four when Palau and the Marshall Islands went their own way; law describes a circle of four white stars on blue. Wikipedia (Trust Territory): US administration of the Micronesian districts ended 3 November 1986.
era-1986.open: The flag dates from 1978, so this card's 1986 start is the Compact, not the flag; the earlier note that FOTW dates it to 1962 reflected the Trust Territory flag, not the current one. Wikipedia's wording on the 1986 colour change is ambiguous about which blue replaced which.

era-1885-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact era, four distinct societies, no single flag».
era-1885-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1947.says: Wikipedia (Trust Territory): UN trusteeship began 18 July 1947 and US administration of the Micronesian districts ended 3 November 1986. Flags of the World: 'Before this flag was adopted the flags of the US and UN were used'; the Trust Territory flag (six stars on blue) was first hoisted 24 October 1962 and made official 19 August 1965, and flew beside the US and UN flags on UN Day. Wikipedia's FSM article: the six-star flag was adopted in 1962 and approved in 1965.
era-1947.open: The trust-territory flag (1962/65-1978/86) is a real flag of this era that the card does not draw; FOTW's fm page and its Trust Territory page give different 1962 days (3 October vs 24 October). The US flag is stated as in use but no source describes how it was flown across 1947-1986.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia's South Seas Mandate: Japan held the islands from its occupation in 1914, a League of Nations Class C mandate from 1920 to 18 July 1947; its infobox shows the flag of Japan, and a separate flag of the Governor of the Mandate is pictured without description. World Statesmen's flag captions: Japan flag from 7 Oct 1914 to 1944, then the US flag. Flags of the World (South Pacific Agency): Japan administered the islands from Koror and made no special regional flag apart from a 1930 fishery vessel service flag. OzOutback (unsigned, no sources): the Japanese Navy seized the islands in 1914 flying the naval ensign (red Rising Sun with 16 rays on white), and the 1919 mandate flag showed a stylised emblem in a laurel wreath.
era-1914.open: The end date differs (1944 on World Statesmen, 1947 on Wikipedia); the unsigned OzOutback account of a naval ensign in 1914 and an emblem flag for the mandate is uncorroborated and conflicts with the other three, and the Governor's flag Wikipedia pictures is not described. The drawing shows the plain red disc.

era-1899.says: Wikipedia's German New Guinea: Germany bought the Carolines and Marianas from Spain in 1899 and administered them from German New Guinea until the Japanese occupation of 1914; drafts of colonial flags made in 1914 were never put into use. The Bundesarchiv gallery documents the imperial decree of 18 July 1899 (protectorates) and the handover protocol at Ponape of 12 October 1899, with the district attached to German New Guinea. World Statesmen's flag caption: German Empire flag from 12 Oct 1899 to 7 Oct 1914. OzOutback (unsigned): the flag in the protectorate was the black-white-red flag of the German Empire with the coat of arms on a white disk. Flags of the World's German colonies page: colonial territories showed the national flag, the naval ensign and service flags (one with a white disc in the centre).
era-1899.open: The German imperial flag is supported in general (World Statesmen, FOTW, archive dates), but no source read ties a specific flag design to the Carolines; the eagle on a white disc rests on the unsigned OzOutback page and a service flag with a disc on FOTW without naming the Carolines. The white flag with a black-white-red canton is the 1914 draft, which Wikipedia says was never used.

era-1885.says: Wikipedia (Spanish East Indies): the Carolines ('Nuevas Filipinas') were Spanish from 1686 until sold to Germany, effective 12 February 1899; its infobox shows the Spanish flag of 1785-1873 and 1875-1931. OzOutback: the red-yellow-red war ensign (yellow band double width) was adopted in 1785 and became the national flag in 1843 with the arms of Castile and Leon; Flags of the World's Spain page lists the 1843 decree and the 1785 ensign.
era-1885.open: No source describes a separate colonial flag or says how the flag was flown in the Carolines; the Cross of Burgundy ensign of earlier centuries (OzOutback) is not relevant to 1885-1899 but shows the sources' chronology.

era-1991.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Moldova and of the Moldavian SSR): the blue-yellow-red vertical tricolour with the coat of arms (an eagle bearing a shield with an aurochs head, star, rose and crescent) on the yellow stripe was adopted on 6 November 1990 and retained when Moldova declared independence in 1991; 27 April 1990 is the day the tricolour was first adopted by the Supreme Soviet and is Flag Day. FOTW: the flag was established in 1990 and has the arms on the yellow stripe; a national flag of 27 August 1991 bears the arms on a darker yellow rectangle; flag laws of 1994, 2001 and 17 September 2010 define it.
era-1991.open: Both sources date the flag to 1990, not 1991 (27 April tricolour without arms, 6 November 1990 with arms). The page's claim that the colours are a 'more saturated' palette than Romania's is not covered; Wikipedia says the reverse side used a lighter blue before 2010.

era-1359.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — founding era, no flag survives this early».
era-1359.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-100bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no state banner from Dacian, Roman, or migration-era rule survives».
era-100bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1940.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Moldavian SSR): the SSR's first flag, from 1940, was red with the gold hammer and sickle and the Cyrillic initials РССМ above; on 31 January 1952 a decree approved a red cloth with a green stripe in the middle along the whole length (red-green-red, 3:2:3), with a gold hammer and sickle and a red star in the canton, used until 1990. FOTW: the 1941-1952 flag was red with curved yellow initials RSSM and a hammer and sickle (Constitution of 1941, art. 123); the flag of 31 January 1952 had a green bar in the middle, one quarter of the width, with hammer, sickle and star.
era-1940.open: The page's 'plain red until 1952' and a green stripe 'near the bottom' do not match the sources: the early flag carried the initials, and the green stripe was in the middle. The first flag is dated 1940 by Wikipedia and 1941 (constitution) by FOTW; 1990-91 saw the tricolour as the SSR's flag.

era-1918.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Romania says the vertical blue-yellow-red tricolour was Romania's flag from 1867 to 1948, with the arms placed only on army and princely flags while civilian flags stayed plain. FOTW's Romania page quotes a Romanian source that the national flag was a plain tricolour from 1872 until 1948. FOTW's Moldova page says Bessarabia proclaimed independence in 1917, went back to Romania in 1918 and passed to the USSR in 1940.
era-1918.open: No source read says the tricolour was flown in Bessarabia or that Bessarabia had no flag of its own; its use there is inferred from Bessarabia being part of Romania. FOTW reports an unsourced dark blue over red bicolour for 1917-1918, before the union.

era-1812.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Russia article says the white-blue-red tricolour was adopted as the commercial maritime flag in 1705 and continued as a civil ensign under the Russian Empire, with the black-yellow-white tricolour decreed the official state flag in 1858 and white-blue-red made the sole national flag in 1896; FOTW's Russia page likewise says the tricolour was originally the civil ensign, recognised for land use on 7 May 1883, with a separate black-orange-white state flag. FOTW's Moldova page says Bessarabia became Russian in 1812 (1810 in another line) and joined Romania in 1918.
era-1812.open: No source read describes a flag flown specifically in Bessarabia under Russian rule. The white-blue-red tricolour was the civil ensign, not the state flag, from 1858 to 1896, as the caption says; the sources do not discuss whether Bessarabia had any flag of its own.

era-1600.says: Wikipedia (Flag and coat of arms of Moldavia): the arms are an aurochs head with a star between its horns, a rose and a crescent, in sable or gold; Stephen the Great's princely flag of 1485 was red silk with the arms in gold; flag use declined under Ottoman control and, from the early 19th century, red-and-blue standards replaced the red and gold. FOTW (Principality of Moldavia): a 1533 document describes the great flag as red with the arms of Moldavia in gold; a flag of Ieremia Movila captured in 1601 is red with a gold border and the aurochs head, star and crescents in silver; a 1813 document gives a red, yellow and blue standard under Scarlat Calimachi.
era-1600.open: The colour of the aurochs varies in the sources (gold, silver or black) and the 1601 flag shows two crescents instead of a rose; Wikipedia says flag use declined under the Ottomans, and FOTW's 1813 red-yellow-blue standard shows the design changed at the end of the period. The page's 'at least from the 15th century' is supported by the 1485 and 1533 reports.

era-1861.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption of the present flag as 4 April 1881; FOTW gives 4 April 1881, by decree of Prince Charles III, and quotes the Constitution (Article 7): two equal horizontal stripes, red above white. Wikipedia says the earlier flag was similar but with an older coat of arms and was used until 1881.
era-1861.open: The flag dates from 1881, not 1861 (the 1861 Franco-Monegasque Treaty starts the era); the 1861-1881 flag is described only by Wikipedia (an older arms version). The drawing's colours were not compared against a specification.

era-600bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner from Ligurian, Greek, or Roman-era Monoikos survives».
era-600bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1815.says: Wikipedia (History of Monaco): after French control ended in 1814 the Congress of Vienna made Monaco a Sardinian protectorate in 1815, lasting to 1860. Wikipedia (Flag of Monaco): the original flag, similar to the present one but with an older coat of arms, was in use until 1881 (start marked 'when?'), and the red-lozenge banner was an unofficial flag used at various times. FOTW's historical page covers only the lozengy banner, used mainly in the 17th century. The Monaco government's history page (gouv.mc) was read and only links to a symbols section without text.
era-1815.open: No source states which flag Monaco flew in 1815-1860, or that the lozengy banner was restored in 1815; Wikipedia's earlier flag with an older coat of arms is undescribed. FOTW dates the Sardinian protectorate from 1814, Wikipedia from 1815.

era-1793.says: Wikipedia (History of Monaco): French revolutionary forces seized Monaco in 1793, it was part of the Alpes-Maritimes department, and French control lasted until 17 May 1814. Wikipedia (Flag of Monaco): the original Monaco flag was in use except during the annexation to the French First Republic from 1793 to 1814. Wikipedia (Flag of France) and Flags of the World (France): the blue-white-red tricolour was decreed on 15 February 1794, and the First Empire used it as the national flag; FOTW's Monaco page also dates the annexation to 1793.
era-1793.open: No source says the tricolour was hoisted at Monaco itself, only that Monaco was annexed to France and its own flag unused; the tricolour is inferred from that. A flag between 1793 and the 1794 decree is not covered.

era-1297.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Monaco): red and white have been the Grimaldi heraldic colours since at least 1339, and a banner of red lozenges on white, the banner of the arms, was used at various times, particularly in the 17th century, as an unofficial flag. Flags of the World (Monaco, historical): the lozengy banner appears to have been used mainly in the 17th century, with a variable number of lozenges. Wikipedia (History of Monaco): Francesco Grimaldi seized the Rock in 1297, with Spanish authority from 1524 and French recognition in 1641.
era-1297.open: Both sources call the lozengy banner unofficial and mainly 17th-century; neither names a state flag of the lordship for 1297-1793, so the card's banner for the whole span is an approximation that stands in for it.

era-1992.says: Wikipedia: the current flag was adopted on 12 February 1992, the communist star above the Soyombo removed, colour standards set on 8 July 2011; the blue stripe is the eternal blue sky and the red stripes are thriving for eternity. Flags of the World: adopted by the new constitution of 13 January 1992, the star surmounting the emblem removed in 1992; Article 12 gives blue as the eternal sky in the middle and red as progress and prosperity on either side.
era-1992.open: The adoption day is 12 February on Wikipedia and 13 January (the constitution) on FOTW; the Soyombo's element meanings differ between the sources.

era-1924.says: WP: first constitution (26 Nov 1924) described a red flag with the state emblem in the centre; 1940 flag had no star; 1945 design with star; star above soyombo for the final 47 years. FOTW: 1924 constitution describes a red flag with the soyombo in the centre; soyombo adopted as state symbol 1924; 1949 gold star over soyombo; star removed 1992.
era-1924.open: The star is not in 1924; exact date of the star differs (1945 per WP, 1949 confirmation per FOTW). Page drawing shows the later layout.

era-1911.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mongolia) says that after the 1911 declaration of independence the Bogd Khanate adopted a national flag as a symbol of independence, listed for 1911-1919, and that the flag remained after 1921 until 1924; Wikipedia (Bogd Khanate of Mongolia) says a state name and a state flag were adopted when the new government was set up after the 1911 declaration, and captions its infobox flag 1911 to 1924. Flags of the World (Mongolia): independence was declared on 29 December 1911; its 1911 and 1912 flags show the soyombo in the older religious colours, a 1911 army flag is shown from museum photos, and a yellow square with orange border and streamers is reported for 1911-1919.
era-1911.open: Both publishers attest a national flag with the soyombo from 1911, but neither describes a red field: FOTW points to the older religious colours and to a yellow flag, so the card's red field is not confirmed. The 1911-1919 versus 1911-1921 span differs between the sources.

era-1691.says: Wikipedia (Flag of the Qing dynasty) says the Yellow Dragon Flag (blue dragon on yellow with a red pearl) was adopted in 1889 as China's first national flag, with a dragon flag for the dynasty from 1862, and replaced in January 1912. Neither Wikipedia's nor Flags of the World's Mongolia flag pages describe flags under Qing rule; FOTW's early Mongol flags page covers the Mongol Empire but no Qing-era banners. World Statesmen's Mongolia flag sequence begins on 29 Dec 1911. Vexilla Mundi (an image-based page) lists pre-1872 sulde banners (white-haired banner, Nine White Banners) and Qing dynasty flags for Mongolia in 1872-1890 and 1890-1911.
era-1691.open: Whether the Qing Yellow Dragon Flag flew over Outer Mongolia is not stated in any text read, and the flags the sources date are from 1862, 1872 or 1889, not 1691. No flag for Outer Mongolia under Qing suzerainty is described in text.

era-1368.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mongolia) and Flags of the World (Mongolia) describe no flags of the post-Yuan khanates. Wikipedia (Northern Yuan) narrates the khanates from 1368 to the Qing conquest without describing a flag. Flags of the World's early Mongol flags page records white and black nine-tailed banners attributed to Chinghiz-khan (Lomantsov, who calls modern reconstructions very doubtful) and Mongol Empire flags, but nothing for the Northern Yuan or later khanates.
era-1368.open: No source read establishes a black Mongol imperial banner, or any flag, for 1368-1691; the nearest evidence concerns the 13th-century empire. The card's drawing is a text placeholder, not a flag, and its caption's 'Mongol imperial black' is not supported.

era-2006.says: Both sources date the current flag to 2004, before this era begins in 2006, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 13 July 2004; Flags of the World dates it 15 September 2004.
era-2006.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1496.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — direct Ottoman provincial rule, no local banner survives».
era-1496.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-168bce.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — no banner survives from Illyrian, Roman, or early Duklja/Zeta rule».
era-168bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1992.says: FOTW (cs.html): the blue-white-red federal flag was adopted 27 April 1992 and stayed official after the 2003 renaming as Serbia and Montenegro until the union ended in 2006. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): the new union removed the red star and kept a plain tricolour. For the republic, Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) says it adopted its own red, light-blue and white tricolour in 1993; FOTW (cs-cg) gives the law published 29 December 1993, three equal horizontal stripes, red, light blue and white, differing from Serbia's flag in ratio and blue shade.
era-1992.open: Wikipedia's Flag of Yugoslavia contradicts itself on whether the red-star version continued after 1992; FOTW (27 April 1992) is followed here. The page's older statement of a tricolour-and-eagle flag flown alongside is not found in any source read.

era-1943.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro): the Yugoslav republic used a red, blue and white tricolour with a red star, 1945-93, adopted late 1946. FOTW (yu_fy-cg): the Montenegrin flag, a red-blue-white tricolour with a star, was officially adopted 31 December 1946 (arms probably the same time); the republic was a People's Republic until 1963 and Socialist from then until 1991. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia) describes the federal red-star flag as having a gold-yellow border to the star.
era-1943.open: The gold border is documented for the federal flag, not stated for the Montenegrin one; FOTW gives no end date for the flag; neither source says the old royal eagle was deliberately dropped.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia: the Kingdom of Montenegro used a tricolour with an eagle bearing the initials NI in 1910-18. FOTW (me_k): the 1905 Constitution (Art. 39) set the national colours red, bluish and white; Montenegro became a kingdom in 1910 and the court flag's crown changed from princely to royal; the civil ensign 1881-1916 was a plain tricolour with a crown and cypher in the centre.
era-1910.open: The two sources differ on the central device: Wikipedia has an eagle with the NI initials, FOTW a crown with the cypher on the civil ensign (and notes McCandless' claim of a war-ensign version as doubtful). The page's 'peak of territory and diplomacy' wording is not in either source.

era-1852.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) lists a red flag with a white two-headed eagle over a lion for Danilo I, 1852-1860, says the cross on the alaj-barjak was replaced under Danilo by the two-headed eagle with his initials and a lion passant beneath, and that the 1905 constitution made the red-blue-white tricolour the national flag. FOTW (Principality / Kingdom of Montenegro) says Danilo first added only his golden cypher to the old cross banner and that the eagle-and-lion alaj-banner, with a double-headed white eagle, was designed in 1858 before the battle of Grahovo; a tricolour was raised in 1860 and the tricolour became the national colours by 1905. FOTW (Montenegro) gives Danilo's arms as a golden double-headed eagle with a lion on the breast shield.
era-1852.open: The sources agree on a red flag with a white double-headed eagle and a lion in Danilo's time but differ on when it began (1852 on Wikipedia's list, c. 1858 on FOTW, which says the 1852 change was a cypher on the cross banner); the golden eagle belongs to FOTW's account of the arms, not the flag. The card's '(1852)' is therefore uncertain, and the Pan-Slavic tricolour is attested by FOTW from 1860 and by Wikipedia from 1905.

era-1516.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) lists a white cross pattee on a red field for the Prince-Bishopric, 1516-1852, and says the principal Montenegrin flag before Njegos was the alaj-barjak with a single symbol, the cross; the first written description dates from Scepan Mali's time (white with a red frame and a golden cross on the spear), then 1838 (pale yellow with a small red cross) and 1876 (red with a white cross). Wikipedia (Principality of Montenegro) calls the historical war flags krstas-barjak, plain flags with crosses in the centre. FOTW (Principality / Kingdom of Montenegro) says Montenegrins in 1814 refused the Slavic tricolour, serving only under the cross banner, and describes the theocratic state's banner as a red flag with a yellow border and the cross inside.
era-1516.open: Both publishers attest a cross banner for the Prince-Bishopric, but the colours vary between descriptions (white cross on red, red cross on pale yellow, yellow-bordered red), and the earliest written description is from the 1760s-70s. No source read dates the flag itself to 1516, the state's date, and the page's 'some variants reverse the colours' is only loosely covered by the differing descriptions.

era-1451.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) lists a red flag with a golden two-headed eagle for medieval Zeta, 1451-1496, and says the double-headed eagle has a long prehistory in the Zeta region under the Nemanjic and Crnojevic states. Wikipedia (House of Crnojevic) pictures Crnojevic arms from the Illyrian Armorials and a flag with captions only. Flags of the World (Montenegro) quotes a Montenegrin parliamentary explanation of 2004 that the state coat of arms began with the Crnojevic dynasty as a golden double-headed eagle, and its editor adds that he is not sure all of these claims would pass a historical analysis.
era-1451.open: No contemporary flag, seal or description of a Crnojevic flag is given by either source; the red field and golden eagle rest on Wikipedia's list entry and on a modern statement about arms. Wikipedia's Zeta (state) article describes no flag.

era-1918-1.says: FOTW (Montenegro): in 1918 Montenegro was incorporated into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and the red flag with gold arms was not raised again until 2004. FOTW (Royal Yugoslavia): a new state formed in late 1918 from the united kingdoms of Serbia and Montenegro and the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; its blue-white-red tricolour was in use even before it became the national flag by the 1921 constitution. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): the tricolour was first used by the Kingdom of Yugoslavia from 1918. Wikipedia (Zeta Banovina) dates the banovina 1929-1941.
era-1918-1.open: Neither publisher says the tricolour was hoisted in Montenegro in 1918 itself; the card draws the new state's tricolour as a ghosted stand-in for a Montenegrin flag that no source shows.

era-1941.says: FOTW (Yugoslavia in WWII): Montenegro was nominally declared an independent kingdom in personal union with Italy and the Montenegrin tricolour was used at least in the first days. FOTW (Principality / Kingdom of Montenegro): the Montenegrin tricolour was banned by the Italian authorities within months, who allowed only Nicholas's military banner, though some collaborators kept using it. Wikipedia (Italian governorate of Montenegro): its infobox pairs the Italian flag with a local Montenegrin flag (the image file is labelled 1905-1918, 1941-1944); the governorate lasted 3 October 1941 to 12 September 1943, and the text describes no flag. Wikipedia (Flag of Montenegro) has nothing on 1941-43. Hrvatska enciklopedija (Crna Gora) says Italy occupied Montenegro and that under Italian protectorate an independent Montenegro was proclaimed by the Montenegrin assembly on 12 July 1941, with an uprising starting the next day; it describes no flag.
era-1941.open: Neither publisher describes a tricolour with a crowned eagle for 1941-43, or a propaganda purpose; FOTW's remarks are the author's own and uncited, and the Wikipedia flag is only an infobox image. Which flag, if any, represented the nominal kingdom is not established. A national encyclopaedia (Hrvatska enciklopedija) confirms the 12 July 1941 proclamation but says nothing of its flag.

era-1918.says: FOTW (me.html): incorporation into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918, Yugoslavia 1929, the traditional red flag with gold arms not raised again until 2004. FOTW (yu_shs): the blue-white-red tricolour was formally introduced as the national flag with the 1921 Vidovdan Constitution and made the civil and state ensign by the 1922 law. Wikipedia (Flag of Yugoslavia): a horizontal blue-white-red tricolour, first officially adopted 1922. Wikipedia (Zeta Banovina): established 3 October 1929; its infobox shows the Yugoslav state flag under the caption Flag of Zetska Banovina. Hrvatska enciklopedija (Crna Gora) says the Zetska banovina was created by the law of 3 October 1929 and under the 1931 constitution took in Montenegro, Herzegovina, the Sandzak and southern Dalmatia; it mentions no flag.
era-1918.open: The Yugoslav tricolour as the state flag in force is supported; that the banovina had no flag of its own rests on the Wikipedia infobox and on silence in Flags of the World and Hrvatska enciklopedija, and the page's wording about deliberate erasure of national symbols is interpretation not found in the sources. The banovina's boundaries are not covered by the flag sources.

era-1956.says: Wikipedia: the flag adopted by dahir on 17 November 1915 stayed in use; after independence in 1956 it was also allowed as the maritime flag. FOTW: the 1915 decree was confirmed in 1956 and not superseded; Constitution of 1974 (revised 1992) Article 7 describes a red flag with a green five-pointed star.
era-1956.open: Star drawing varies between flag books (FOTW); a 2005 decree set the construction (Wikipedia).

era-1912.says: Wikipedia: 17 November 1915 dahir of Sultan Yusef introduced the green pentagram on red; protectorate-era use limited at sea; merchant flags for the French zone 1919-1956 and Spanish zone 1937-1956. FOTW: Decree of 1915 set the star's size, and the flag was limited as the national flag in the French zone until independence.
era-1912.open: The page's stated reason for the star, and the 1912 start of the protectorate, are not covered by either source.

era-1666.says: Flags of the World's historical page says the Alawites have ruled Morocco since 1666, that the flag 'was originally plain red', that the Alawites were the first to introduce the red flag, raised each day on the fortresses at Rabat and Sale, and that the French Protectorate began on 30 March 1912. Wikipedia's Flag of Morocco says the Alawi dynasty used a red field as its flag from the 17th century, 'solid red at first' (citation needed), and dates the Alawi flag 1666-1915 before the current design of 17 November 1915.
era-1666.open: Both publishers agree on a red Alawite flag, plain at first. FOTW also shows later red flags with white zulfiqar scissors, triangle borders or a forked pennant (Bellin 1756, Diderot 1780, Norie and Hobbs 1848, Sinclair 1858), so 'plain red for nearly two and a half centuries' is not supported. The era end of 1912 (card) versus 1915 (Wikipedia) is unresolved.

era-1983.says: Both sources give 1983, the year this page starts the current flag. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 May 1983; Flags of the World dates it 01 May 1983.
era-1983.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1498-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Swahili trading towns and interior chiefdoms, no flag survives».
era-1498-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1975.says: Wikipedia: independence 25 June 1975 with a flag defined by Article 68 of the constitution: four diagonal stripes from the upper hoist in green, red, black and yellow with white fimbriations, and a white cogwheel near the upper hoist bearing a red star and an AK-47 crossed by a hoe over an open book; changed in 1983. FOTW (mz_old): the first official flag was adopted 25 June 1975, four irregular triangles of yellow, black, red and green fimbriated white radiating from the upper hoist, with the arms (a black-lined cogwheel, a rifle and a hoe in saltire over an open book, red star) in the canton; replaced in April 1983 (adopted 1 May 1983 on mz.html).
era-1975.open: The sources agree on date, colours and emblem elements; FOTW says 'a rifle' where Wikipedia says AK-47, and the exact stripe order and the wording 'diagonal bands' differ. Article 68 appears only in Wikipedia.

era-1498.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Mozambique): Mozambique flew the Portuguese flag when it was under Portuguese colonial rule, and during the 1974-75 transition the Portuguese flag flew beside FRELIMO's; FOTW (first Mozambican flag) agrees that FRELIMO's flag flew alongside the Portuguese flag from the truce of 5 September 1974 to independence on 25 June 1975. Wikipedia (Portuguese Mozambique): the colony is dated 1505-1975, an overseas province from 1951, and its infobox shows a flag dated 1911-1975.
era-1498.open: Only the Portuguese flag of 1911-1975 is shown; no source read describes flags from 1498 to 1911 or a distinct colonial ensign. Use over the long span rests on Wikipedia, with FOTW covering only 1974-75.

era-2021.says: Both sources date the current flag to 2010, before this era begins in 2021, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 21 October 2010; Flags of the World dates it 21 October 2010.
era-2021.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-200bce.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-2011.says: Both: the current yellow-green-red flag with a large white star adopted 21 October 2010 (Wikipedia: Union Flag Law, 2008 Constitution, 2:3; FOTW: State Flag Law 8/2010, 2:3, raised 3 p.m.).
era-2011.open: The 2011 civilian-led government is not covered by either flag page.

era-1974.says: Wikipedia: adopted 3 January 1974, designed by Mya Thaung, 5:9, a blue canton on red with 14 stars round a cogwheel and paddy ear, used to 2010. FOTW: flag adopted 27 December 1973 (the constitution is dated 3 January 1974); a red flag with a blue canton and a white emblem of a cog wheel and a paddy ear surrounded by 14 five-pointed stars; ratio usually 5:9.
era-1974.open: The two sources differ by a week on the adoption date (27 December 1973 vs 3 January 1974); neither mentions ruling-party ideology.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia: used 4 January 1948 to 3 January 1974, designed by Maung Win, no stripes, one large star and five small stars in a blue canton on red. FOTW: the 1948 flag is red with a blue canton holding one large white star and five small white stars; adopted with the constitution of 24 September 1947 and hoisted first at 4:25 a.m. on 4 January 1948; a contributor says the big star stood for the Union and the five small ones for five states (another recalls the Anti-Fascist League flag as the source of the large star).
era-1948.open: What the five small stars stand for is a contributor's statement in FOTW, not a document; Wikipedia does not explain them.

era-1942.says: Wikipedia: the peacock flag was the State of Burma's national flag 1943-45 (state flag from 1 August 1943), with a gold peacock for the State of Burma and a red peacock for the Burma Defence Army; a provisional Japanese Military Administration flag 1942-43. FOTW: the Japanese created a puppet state on 1 August 1943 with a flag 'probably' horizontally yellow, green and red with a peacock on a disc (a Japanese newspaper shows yellow-green-red with a peacock on a white disc), abolished 1 August 1945; in 1942 the pro-Japanese provisional government used the Synyethe-Wunthann party flag unofficially.
era-1942.open: The sources disagree on design (Wikipedia: peacock flag; FOTW: yellow-green-red triband with peacock), so the single 'green field' drawn on the page is not confirmed; the 1942 provisional flag is described differently by the two (Japanese Military Administration vs party flag).

era-1886.says: Wikipedia: the UK Union Flag was the colonial flag 1886-1942 and again 1945-48, with a separate British Burma colonial flag 6 February 1939 to 30 March 1941 and 1945-1948 and a provisional one in 1941-42. FOTW: from 1886 to 1939 Burma was part of India and the British (or Indian) flag flew; from 6 (adopted 9) February 1939 the Blue Ensign with a Burmese badge (a golden disc with a peacock) until 1941 and again in 1945-1948.
era-1886.open: The page's 'colony' wording: Burma was part of British India until 1937 (FOTW notes 1886-1939 as part of India); the designs of the 1941-42 provisional flags are not described.

era-1044.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Myanmar has a gallery caption 'Flag used as national flag of Burma under Konbaung Dynasty (c. 1752-1885)', with several footnotes, and ties the peacock to the Konbaung in its account of the 1930s tricolours. FOTW's historical flags page describes the Konbaung Dynasty flag, dated 1700-1885, as white with a peacock, generally on a red disk or inside a red ring. Wikipedia also lists a Hanthawaddy kingdom flag (c. 1287-1552), and FOTW a golden hintha on green for the early Mon and a Thu Ye Gyee military flag c.1300-1885.
era-1044.open: Two publishers support the Konbaung peacock flag only, with start dates of 1752 (Wikipedia) and 1700 (FOTW, from web and private sources); neither gives a flag for Bagan (from c. 1044) or Toungoo, so the card covers only the last part of its stated span, as its caption already says.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia's infobox: adopted 21 March 1990. FOTW (Namibian flag 1990 - ): on 21 March 1990 South West Africa gained independence as the Republic of Namibia and adopted a new flag chosen by a committee; the symbolism given by the chairman of the National Symbols Sub-committee on 2 February 1990 (citing F. G. Brownell, Archives News 1990) is red for the people and their heroism, white for peace and unity, green for vegetation and agriculture, blue for the sky, the Atlantic Ocean and rain, and the gold sun for life and energy; one source says the colours came from the SWAPO flag adopted in 1971.
era-1990.open: Neither source says the design 'deliberately breaks' from the German and South African flags; FOTW's note that the colours came from the SWAPO flag (adopted 1971) is a single attribution to a 1990 flag book.

era-1884-1.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder maroon field — Herero, Nama, and Ovambo societies, no flag survives».
era-1884-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1915.says: Wikipedia's captions: a South West Africa flag for 1915-1919 (identification uncertain), a merchant flag 1915-1928, South African-derived flags for South West Africa 1928-1990, bantustan flags and the SWAPO flag at the UN 1976-1990. FOTW (Flag History of Namibia): South African troops took German South West Africa on 9 July 1915; under the mandate the South African Red Ensign was flown in the territory until 31 May 1928, when the South African national flag (orange, white and blue stripes with flaglets in the centre) was adopted; FOTW also lists the bantustan flags.
era-1915.open: FOTW's account stops at the 1928 adoption; the flag shown on the page is the plain orange-white-blue without the flaglets, a simplification, and the SA Red Ensign (1915-28) is not what the page shows for the whole span.

era-1884.says: Wikipedia: the Reich Colonial Office flag was used in German South-West Africa from 24 April 1884 to 9 July 1915, with an undated proposed colonial flag shown. FOTW (Flag History of Namibia): German colonies had no distinctive flags or arms of their own; the Imperial German arms and flags were used throughout the empire, including German South West Africa; colonial flags designed in 1912-14 (the German tricolour with a blue shield bearing a silver ox's head and a diamond for South West Africa) were never taken into use because of the war; German forces surrendered on 9 July 1915.
era-1884.open: The exact imperial flag flown (the black-white-red civil ensign drawn on the page vs. the Reich Colonial Office flag Wikipedia names) is not described by either source.

era-1968.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1888-1.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1920.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Nauru) says a Blue Ensign with the seven-pointed Commonwealth Star and the five stars of the Southern Cross was used under Australian occupation and the League of Nations mandate (to 1942) and again from 1945 under the UN trust territory to 1968, and that New Zealand and the United Kingdom were co-mandatories whose flags were not used. Flags of the World (Nauru) describes no flag for the administration; its history page records a 1924 Chiefs' proposal for a flag that Melbourne would not recognise, a 1925 suggestion from London of a Nauru badge on British-pattern ensigns and the Union Jack for the Administrator, and a Customs Flag for 1921-1968. World Statesmen lists an Australian flag for 17 December 1920 to 26 August 1942 and 13 September 1945 to 31 January 1968, without saying which Australian flag. A Commonwealth circular printed in The Register (Adelaide, 6 March 1924) says the Commonwealth Flag, the British Blue Ensign with the stars of the Southern Cross and a seven-pointed star, is flown at Commonwealth public buildings and establishments, and the British Blue Ensign with State badge on State buildings and vessels; it does not mention Nauru.
era-1920.open: A second compiled page (World Statesmen) lists an Australian flag but not which one, and the 1924 circular does not name Nauru, so the Blue Ensign with the Commonwealth Star rests on Wikipedia, which relies on a commercial flag-maker's document. Flags of the World's 1925 account points to British-pattern ensigns and the Union Jack for the Administrator, and the card's 'Britain, Australia, New Zealand jointly' wording is contradicted by Wikipedia's note that only Australia's flag was used.

era-1888.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Nauru) lists a white flag with a black-white-red canton and a black lion holding a red fleur-de-lys (the German New Guinea Company) for 1888-1899 and a German tricolour with the arms in a white circle (Imperial Colonial Office) for 1899-1914. Wikipedia (German Marshall Islands) says Nauru was incorporated into the Marshall Islands protectorate on 16 April 1888, administered by the Jaluit Company, with direct German control from 1906; Wikipedia (History of Nauru) says instead that it joined Germany's New Guinea Protectorate. Flags of the World (Colonial flags 1914) says the colonies had no flags of their own and used imperial German flags until Solf's 1914 colonial flag designs, which were never put in use, and lists Nauru among them; Flags of the World (German colonies) lists a Jaluit Company flag (white with a black-white-red disc) and no Nauru flag. Colonel Holmes's telegram of November 1914 (State Library of NSW) says that when his troops took Nauru on 6 November "German Flag lowered, British Flag hoisted", and a Gazette account in his diary says the British flag took the place of the German flag on the Government House flagstaff. World Statesmen lists a German protectorate by proclamation and flag raising on 2 October 1888 and shows the German Empire flag for 1888-1914, the UK flag for 1914-1920.
era-1888.open: A German flag at Nauru is attested for 1914, and a flag raising for 1888, but none of these pages describes its design: the black-white-red tricolour is taken from the German Empire's flag in general and the eagle on the card is not supported. Nothing read describes a flag specific to German Nauru, and for 1914-1920 the primary sources show the British flag under Australian military occupation, not a German one.

era-2008.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1990.says: Wikipedia: the 9 November 1990 constitution (Article 5, Schedule 1) gave a geometric description of the flag; in 2008 a proposal to change the design was rejected. FOTW's page on the flag's legal basis quotes the constitution's Article 5, that the flag 'as handed down by tradition' has two juxtaposed triangular figures with crimson base and deep blue borders, a white moon with eight visible rays and a twelve-rayed sun, with Schedule 1 construction steps; a contributor note dates that constitution 9 November 1991 (a probable slip) and FOTW's main page says the double pennant was adopted officially on 16 December 1962.
era-1990.open: FOTW labels its extract '1999' and gives 1991 for the adoption in a contributor note, so the year of the text it quotes is not firm in FOTW; the 2008 rejected proposal is only in Wikipedia. Neither source says the design changed in 1990.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: flag adopted 16 Dec 1962 with the new constitutional government, standardised by Rimal at King Mahendra's request; human faces removed to modernise. FOTW: adopted 12 Dec 1962, sun and moon stylised 16 Dec 1962; a contributor believes the faces were removed in 1962.
era-1960.open: Adoption date differs (12 vs 16 Dec 1962); FOTW's face-removal statement is a contributor's belief; the 1960 start of the period is not covered.

era-1951.says: Wikipedia: sun and moon carried human faces until 1962. FOTW: flags with faces in 1939 and 1958 reproductions and in a 1928 book.
era-1951.open: Origin of the faces is only in Wikipedia (some historians credit Jung Bahadur); 'older informal proportions' not covered.

era-1846.says: The double pennant with faces is documented in this era's later part by several publishers. Flags of the World (Landon's 1928 book) shows 1928 flags of two red triangles with a green border and white faces on the crescent and sun; Wikipedia and Atlas Obscura both describe a 1928 French book showing a double pennant with a green border and faces on sun and moon; Ratopati says that before 1962 the flag was two triangles with a moon and sun, sometimes with faces, and with the sun placed above or below. For the earlier part, WorldStatesmen shows separate pennants, a Flag of the Kings (a moon with a face) and a Rana prime ministers' flag (a sun with a face), for c.1847-1923, and a combined flag from 1923.
era-1846.open: The sources do not support one unchanged flag through Rana rule: c.1847-1923 WorldStatesmen shows separate single pennants, the combined flag with a green border appears in 1923-c.1930 sources, and Atlas Obscura says the border became blue shortly after 1928. FOTW says the double pennant has been used since the 19th century, and Wikipedia gives no dates for the Rana period. The drawing therefore rests on the 1928 form.

era-1768.says: Atlas Obscura, citing a Nepali vexillology contact, says many accounts date the double-pennant flag to Prithvi Narayan Shah's unification (mid-1700s) or the early 1800s, but that there are no historical reproductions of a flag recognisable as the Nepali flag from that period, and that it was probably standardised sometime in the 1800s. WorldStatesmen's earliest Nepal flags are dated '19th cent.' (c.1847 onward). Wikipedia gives the Gorkha flag as a single red triangular banner, and Flags of the World says the double pennant has been used 'since the 19th century'.
era-1768.open: No source read gives a dated flag for 1768-1846; the double pennant with faces on the card is a reconstruction, and the faces are credited by Wikipedia to Jung Bahadur (after 1846).

era-1902.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 24 March 1902; Flags of the World dates it 12 June 1902. Flags of the World's history pages (David Prothero, from Admiralty and Gazette sources) reconcile the two: the New Zealand Ensign Act 1901 received royal assent on 24 March 1902 and the proclamation was published in the New Zealand Gazette on 12 June 1902, making the Blue Ensign with four red white-bordered stars the national flag.
era-1902.open: The design and colours were not checked against a specification. The page's wording on the Union Jack and the Southern Cross meaning is its own and was not tested.

era-1300.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — pre-contact era, no single flag».
era-1300.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1840.says: FOTW's origins of the New Zealand flag (Prothero) says that after the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840 the Union Jack became the national flag and remained the land flag until 1902; a New Zealand Blue Ensign with red letters NZ was warranted on 10 January 1867 for colonial vessels and the Blue Ensign with four red stars was gazetted on 23 October 1869. Wikipedia's Flag of New Zealand says British ensigns began to be used after the colony was formed in 1840, that the current flag was designed for the colony's ships in 1869, and that it received statutory recognition in 1902.
era-1840.open: The caption's plain Blue Ensign without letters or stars is not described by either source; the colony's flag was the Union Jack, and the 1867 and 1869 ensigns were for government vessels. Wikipedia also notes the United Tribes flag stayed in some use.

era-1834.says: Wikipedia: adopted at Waitangi in March 1834, designed by Henry Williams; an 1835 New South Wales gazette notice describes a red St George's cross on white with a canton of a red cross on blue and four white stars. Flags of the World (historical flags pages): Busby's despatch of 26 March 1834 reports that 25 chiefs chose, on 20 March, among three flags (3, 10 and 12 votes), the one the missionaries had adopted; it was gazetted in 1835, the canton blue with a red St George's cross fimbriated white and four stars, and replaced by the Union Jack on 6 February 1840.
era-1834.open: The star points differ among accounts (eight-pointed in Busby's 1834 drawing, five- or six-pointed in the gazetted version) and the canton cross's fimbriation changed from black to white. FOTW's own caption notes the original had eight-pointed stars, so the page's eight-pointed stars fit the 1834 drawing, not the gazette.

era-1908.says: Wikipedia: September 1908 (11 or 5 September); official 27 August 1971; 30 January 2025 FSLN flag recognised. FOTW: 4 September 1908 decree; 5 September arms; Decree 1,908 of 25 August 1971 published 27 August; 2002 Law 432.

era-1200.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1823.says: Wikipedia's «Flag of Central America» gives adoption in 1823, 2000 and relinquishment in 1839, within a year of this era's 1823 and 1838. The Flags of the World page that article links also carries 1838, and has 1823 next to a word about adopting.
era-1823.open: Only the dates were compared. The Flags of the World page was matched on the two years appearing in its text and on one of them sitting beside the word adopt, introduce, establish or the like; it was not read for what it says about this flag. The design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1838.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Nicaragua says Nicaragua kept using the federation's flag (a blue and white triband with a coat of arms showing a rainbow over mountains and a Phrygian cap) until 1854, then a yellow-white-scarlet tricolour in 1854-1856, lists William Walker's flag of 1855-1857, and gives further flags for 1858-1889, 1889-1893, 1893-1896 and 1896-1908. Flags of the World says a blue-white-blue flag was reportedly first hoisted in 1818, that a national flag adopted on 21 April 1854 ran with interruptions to 1889, that the 1858 constitution under Tomas Martinez readopted blue-white-blue, and that Nicaragua left the Federation in 1838 with state flags based on the federation's blue-white-blue. Second look: the Academia de Geografia e Historia de Nicaragua source says Nicaragua left the federation on 30 April 1838; an 1851 decree made the federation's blue-and-white flag compulsory with arms of three volcanoes, a rainbow and a liberty cap; a yellow-white-pearl flag was decreed on 21 April 1854 and Walker designed a blue-and-white flag with a red star in 1856 (later annulled); in 1858-1893 the blue-and-white flag and federal arms were used again, and the law of 4/5 September 1908 fixed the blue-and-white flag. World Statesmen lists a national flag for 1838 - 21 Apr 1854 and 1858 - 1908 and a different state flag for 1854-1858.
era-1838.open: Blue-and-white flags with the federal arms (volcanoes under a rainbow) are shown for most of 1838-1908; they are not shown for 1854-1858 (yellow-white-pearl flag) or Walker's 1855-57 flag, and the academy text dates the federal arms mainly from 1851 and 1858-1893. The exact proportions, the arms and the three-band layout varied (Wikipedia and FOTW sequences do not match) and the card's small volcano emblem is a simplification.

era-1821.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Central America table gives a flag for the Captaincy General of Guatemala (Mexico) from 5 January 1822 to 1 July 1823 and shows the First Mexican Empire flag file for it, without describing it; its First Mexican Empire article says the Central American provinces were annexed in 1822-1823 and maps Nicaragua inside the empire. Flags of the World (cam-us) gives independence from Spain on 15 September 1821, incorporation into Mexico on 5 January 1822 and independence restored on 1 July 1823, with no flag described. Wikipedia's Flag of Nicaragua has no 1821-1823 entry. Second look: the Academia de Geografia e Historia de Nicaragua (school anthology chapter) says that during the 1822-1823 incorporation into Mexico the Imperial Junta ordered the use of the Mexican arms and national flag, and that Gabino Gainza declared the insignia of Iturbide's empire in force in the annexed territory; World Statesmen lists the Kingdom of Guatemala flag for 15 Sep 1821 - 1 Feb 1822 and calls the 1821 incorporation into Mexico de jure ambiguous.
era-1821.open: The Mexican imperial flag over Nicaragua is shown from January 1822 to 1823 by the Nicaraguan academy source (an order, not a description) and by the image in Wikipedia's Central America table; the academy text does not describe the design, so the green-white-red with a crowned eagle comes from Wikipedia and Commons only. The card's era starts in September 1821, but the order dates from January 1822 and World Statesmen lists a different flag until then; León and Granada were split at first.

era-1524.says: Wikipedia's Flag of Nicaragua lists the Cross of Burgundy flag for New Spain until 1785 and a Spanish flag for the Captaincy General of Guatemala from 1785 to 1821; its Cross of Burgundy article says the cross served as the flag of the viceroyalties of the New World during the Spanish colonisation of the Americas. Flags of the World's Spanish history pages say the Cross of Burgundy flag was the Spanish naval ensign 1506-1701 and a jack until 1785, that it is the flag the conquistadors carried 'if any was', and that the red-gold-red ensign was introduced on 28 May 1785. Wikipedia's Captaincy General of Guatemala article dates colonisation to 1524 and the captaincy general to 1609-1821, including Nicaragua.
era-1524.open: No source read says the Cross of Burgundy flew over Nicaragua itself; it is shown for the Spanish Americas and for New Spain, of which the captaincy general formed part. From 1785 both publishers give the red-yellow-red Spanish flag, so the card's Cross of Burgundy covers only about 1524-1785; FOTW adds that it remained a land war flag to 1843.

era-1960.says: Both sources date the current flag to 1959, before this era begins in 1960, so the flag was already in use at the start. Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 23 November 1959; Flags of the World dates it 1959.
era-1960.open: Only the year the current flag was adopted was compared; the design and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification.

era-1958.says: Both: the orange-white-green flag with orange disc adopted 23 November 1959 (Wikipedia: Territorial Assembly; FOTW: Acte No 59-1, Journal Officiel 1 Jan 1960); Wikipedia: designed 1958, retained at independence 1960.
era-1958.open: Neither describes a distinct flag for 1958-59 or the French Community status in flag terms; ratio and colour meanings unconfirmed officially.

era-1963.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 1 October 1960. Flags of the World (Nigeria): the flag was chosen in 1959 from 2,870 entries in a competition, designed by Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi of Ibadan (Pedersen), and 'first officially hoisted on 01 October 1960' (Smith); it is governed by the Flag and Coat-of-Arms Ordinance of 1960. Neither source reports any later change to the green-white-green design.
era-1963.open: The two sources date the adoption to 1960 (FOTW: chosen 1959), so the 1963 start of this era is the republic, not a new flag; absence of any later change is not a positive finding beyond what the two pages say.

era-1914.says: Wikipedia ('Flag of Nigeria (1914-1960)'): adopted 1952, in use 1914, relinquished 1960; a Blue Ensign with the Union Jack and a badge (red disc with green hexagram, crown, 'Nigeria'). Flags of the World (Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria): the colony 'flew a British Blue Ensign with the Colonial badge in the fly', the badge a red field with two interlocked triangles forming a six-pointed star and a crown, with the Tudor Crown before 1953 and St Edward's Crown from 1953 to 1960; a Red Ensign was used at sea; a governor's flag was the Union Flag with the badge in a laurel wreath.
era-1914.open: The two descriptions of the badge differ in detail (Wikipedia: red disc and green hexagram with 'Nigeria'; FOTW: red field with interlaced triangles and a crown), and the page's drawing is schematic; the Tudor-to-St Edward's Crown change in 1953 is not shown.

era-1960.says: Wikipedia: in 1959 Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi won the flag competition; the green-white-green flag was officially adopted at midnight on 1 October 1960 and hoisted by Lt David Ejoor; green stands for agriculture, white for unity and peace. FOTW: the flag was chosen in 1959 from 2,870 suggestions, first officially hoisted on 1 October 1960; green is agriculture, white is peace and unity.
era-1960.open: Neither source mentions forests or a deliberate absence of regional symbols.

era-1861.says: Flags of the World: Lagos Colony (annexed 6 August 1861) flew a Blue Ensign with the colony's badge from 1886 to 1906 (Prothero 2001); Southern Nigeria (1900) and Northern Nigeria (1900) each 'flew a blue ensign defaced with the badge of the protectorate in the fly', badges added to the 1889 Admiralty Flag Book by amendment in March 1901 (Prothero 2002); Lagos was merged into Southern Nigeria in 1906 and the two protectorates amalgamated in 1914. Wikipedia: infobox ensigns for the Colony of Lagos (file dated 1888-1906) and for the Northern and Southern Nigeria Protectorates (1900-1914).
era-1861.open: Neither publisher describes the badges' designs, and no ensign is documented for Lagos in 1861-1886; the page's unbadged Blue Ensign is a generic stand-in.

era-1948.says: Wikipedia's infobox gives the adoption as 8 September 1948. FOTW quotes Crampton (1985) that the flag was created in 1948 (blue-red-blue stripes) and its 1946-1948 page ends the provisional People's Committee flag on 8 September 1948.
era-1948.open: Only the date was compared; the design symbolism (star, disc, stripe meanings) and the swatch colours were not checked against a specification. FOTW's 'North Korea 1948 (dubious)' page describes a different, probably fictional, flag and gives no adoption date.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia: the taegukgi was widely used in both occupation zones in 1945-1947; the Soviets began proposing a new flag only in 1947; the design was written into the provisional constitution on 20 February 1948. FOTW: a taeguk-type flag with trigram and colour differences from today's South Korean flag was used from February 1946 to 8 September 1948 by the Korean Provisional People's Committee; Wikipedia's Flag of Korea lists a People's Committee flag for 1945-1946.
era-1945.open: The north's 1946-48 flag was a variant of the taegukgi, not identical to the page's drawing; no source read describes a flag of a Soviet administration itself.

era-1910.says: Wikipedia: from 1910 the Japanese flag replaced the taegukgi on the peninsula and the taegukgi became a symbol of resistance. FOTW: under Japanese rule (1910-1945) the Korean taeguk flag was prohibited; the Hinomaru was used in Korea until 15 August 1945; the exile government enacted a law on making the national flag on 29 June 1942.
era-1910.open: Wikipedia's Flag of Korea lists a Provisional Government flag for 1919-1945; the exile government is not otherwise covered here.

era-1897.says: Wikipedia (Flag of North Korea): the taegukgi, adopted in 1883, was used by the Korean Empire until Japan annexed Korea in 1910. Flags of the World (history of the Korean flag): King Gojong formally proclaimed the Taegeukgi as the national flag on 6 March 1883, it was in use as the old flag of Korea before the 1905 Japanese occupation, and Korea was annexed on 22 August 1910; a flag from the 1899 Flags of Maritime Nations 'might be' the national flag of the Korean Empire (1897-1910). Wikipedia (Flag of Korea) also lists taegukgi versions for 1882-1910 and imperial standards for the Korean Empire.
era-1897.open: FOTW is explicitly cautious about which version the Empire used, and the exact trigram arrangement varied between versions; the 1897 founding date is not tied to a flag change by either source.

era-1883.says: Wikipedia: the taegukgi ('Flag of Great Extremes') was adopted in 1883 as Korea's first national flag. FOTW: Bak Yeong-hyo used it from September 1882 and it was formally proclaimed on 6 March 1883 (another contributor gives 27 January 1883).
era-1883.open: FOTW contributors disagree on the exact 1883 date and on the first hoisting in 1882; symbolism of the design is not covered.

era-1392.says: Wikipedia (Flag of North Korea) gives 1883 as the year Korea adopted its first national flag, the taegukgi. Flags of the World (history of the Korean flag) says King Gojong formally proclaimed the Taegeukgi as the national flag on 6 March 1883. Earlier items are only listed: FOTW shows an 1856 Japanese flag chart titling a yellow dragon flag 'Korean National flag' and an 1876 chart titling a blue dragon flag 'Korean King Standard'; Wikipedia (Flag of Korea) lists a personal standard of the King of Joseon (1876) and Joseon military flags.
era-1392.open: The card presents a placeholder panel, and the sources agree that the first national flag dates from 1883. The 'royal blue' dynastic colour is not documented by any source read; the 1856 and 1876 Japanese chart entries are late, single-source and not described as a Joseon state flag, and a second Japanese book shows a yellow king's standard.

era-918.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Korea) lists three Goryeo royal banners, the Bong-gi (phoenix), Haema-gi (seahorse) and Sang-gi (elephant); Wikipedia (Goryeo), in a footnote, cites Xu Jing's Xuanhe Fengshi Gaoli Tujing for the yellow phoenix flag. Reading that work itself (Xu Jing, 1123, juan 14 'Flags'): the Goryeo court used ceremonial flags in five colours, including an elephant flag (black body and streamer), a hawk flag (red), a sea-horse flag (blue), a phoenix flag (yellow, with a flying phoenix) and a white Taibai flag, and plain five-direction flags (black, red, blue, white, yellow) and small flags for the procession.
era-918.open: The primary source confirms the royal procession banners named by Wikipedia, for 1123, but describes no national or state flag, and the card shows neither. Nothing is dated outside 1123 and the Wikipedia list marks the banners 'Extant 1392' without further dating. The card's placeholder claim that no state flag is documented stands; the claim of Goryeo royal banners is now supported by a primary text.

era-676.says: Wikipedia (Flag of North Korea) and Wikipedia (Unified Silla) describe no flag for Silla. Wikipedia (Flag of Korea) has a table entry 'Military flag of Silla', a blue banner with a white crescent moon, with no date or source given in the entry; the article's reference list contains no source for it. The Flags of the World Korea page does not mention Silla.
era-676.open: The card presents a placeholder saying no flag is documented, but Wikipedia does list a Silla military banner. The entry is undated, unsourced and not tied to Unified Silla (676-935) or to a state flag, and rests on one publisher. I found no reference work or primary text for it (the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture and the Samguk sagi were not reached before the web-search budget ran out).

era-1972.says: Wikipedia: the Union Flag is the only official flag for Northern Ireland; the government and parliament were abolished in 1972 (elsewhere attributed to the Constitution Act 1973); a 2021 commission recommended a Civic Flag. FOTW: Flags Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2000 restrict flags on government buildings to the Union Flag; College of Arms advised in November 1973 that use of the arms was improper after the 1973 Act.
era-1972.open: 1972 versus 1973 for the end of the Ulster Banner's official status; the March 1972 prorogation is not in either source.

era-450.says: This page's own caption calls the image a placeholder: «placeholder — Gaelic over-kingdoms, no heraldic banner survives».
era-450.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.

era-1953.says: Wikipedia: Royal Warrant of 1924 for the government's arms; the banner was first flown over Parliament Buildings for the 1953 coronation and officially used with Tudor Crown (1924-1953) and St Edward's Crown (1953-1972). FOTW: 2 August 1924 Royal Warrant, 29 May 1953 Royal Assent for widespread use, arms redrawn with St Edward's crown on 6 January 1971, abolished 1973.
era-1953.open: The crown on the 1950s-60s flag is disputed between the two sources; the design (star and red hand) is not specified in the Wikipedia text read.

era-1921.says: Wikipedia (Flag of Northern Ireland): there is no official flag for Northern Ireland except the Union Flag; on 1 July 1953 the Minister for Home Affairs said the Union Flag was the only officially recognised flag. FOTW: 'The official flag of Northern Ireland is the Union Flag' (Prothero 2002), made official for all purposes after the Stormont government went in 1973.
era-1921.open: Both sources also describe the Ulster Banner, which Wikipedia dates to a 1924 royal warrant for the Government of Northern Ireland (official use 1924-1953 with the Tudor Crown) and FOTW treats as introduced and widely used from 1953; neither describes a flag specific to 1921.

era-1801.says: FOTW (United Kingdom): the Union Flag was adopted 1 January 1801 with St Patrick's saltire added after the Union with Ireland Act 1800. Wikipedia (Union Jack): design in force from 1 January 1801; after the 1921 Treaty, Northern Ireland's Prime Minister Craig welcomed that the flag would not need changing ('mutilating the Union Jack') and in December 1922 the flag was not changed.
era-1801.open: Neither source describes use of the flag in Ulster specifically before 1921 beyond Ireland being part of the United Kingdom; the 1801-1921 span is inferred from the Union Flag's continuous use.

era-1177.says: Wikipedia (Kingdom of Ireland): the arms of the Kingdom are blazoned azure a harp Or stringed argent, and although numerous flags of Ireland existed in the period, the Kingdom 'had no official flag or arms'; its Royal Standard of Ireland is captioned 1542-1801. Wikipedia (Flag of Northern Ireland): the Royal Standard of Ireland is listed for 1541-1800 and the origin of the Red Hand is disputed. FOTW (Lordship of Ireland): the Lordship's banner of arms is a modern construction, not a documented flag, and arms of three crowns on blue are attributed to the 1380s.
era-1177.open: Only Wikipedia gives the harp on blue, as arms and a standard for 1542-1801; the Lordship (1177-1542) is not covered by any harp-on-blue evidence, and FOTW says its banner is non-historical. No source puts a red hand on this flag, so the caption's 'red hand added for Ulster's own device' is unsupported.

era-1945.says: Wikipedia's chronology of the flag marks a break in 1940-45 and the cross flag as the flag again from 1945. Store norske leksikon (L. Roede): the national flag was drawn by Frederik Meltzer, adopted by royal resolution of 13 July 1821 and is Norway's flag today (navy-blue Nordic cross with white borders on red); 8 May is flag day for the liberation of 1945.
era-1945.open: The page's statement that the exiled government and the resistance kept the flag flying throughout is not covered by either source.

era-872.open: Whether a flag, banner or standard existed in this period was not checked. The colour shown is not evidence of one.
